jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Company Overview

TENEX is an AI-native, automation-first, built-for-scale Managed Detection and Response (MDR) provider. We are a force multiplier for defenders, helping organizations enhance their cybersecurity posture through advanced threat detection, rapid response, and continuous protection. Our team is composed of industry experts with deep experience in cybersecurity, automation, and AI-driven solutions. Backed by leading investors, we are rapidly growing and seeking top talent to join our mission of revolutionizing the AI-Native MDR landscape.

We’re a fast-growing startup backed by industry experts and top-tier investors led by Crosspoint Capital Partners and also backed by Shield Capital, DTCP (formerly Deutsche Telekom Capital Partners), Deepwork Capital, and the Florida Opportunity Fund. Seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). As an early employee, you’ll play a meaningful role in defining and building our culture. Get in on the ground floor. We’re a small but well-funded team that just raised a substantial round – joining now comes with limited risk and unlimited upside.

As the Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) at TENEX, you will be a strategic leader responsible for orchestrating the delivery of our most complex AI-native security initiatives. You will drive cross-functional programs that bridge the gap between frontier AI research, infrastructure engineering, and security operations. This high-impact role requires a sophisticated blend of technical program management expertise, a deep understanding of cybersecurity threat landscapes, and the ability to navigate the operational challenges of deploying AI at scale in high-stakes environments.

Location: San Jose, CA or Kansas City, KS. Hybrid work model.

Job Responsibilities

 - Cross-Functional Program Leadership: Lead end-to-end delivery of complex technical programs, ensuring alignment between AI research, engineering, and security detection teams to meet critical product milestones.

 - AI Operationalization: Establish and manage the frameworks for scaling AI-driven security capabilities, from prototype development to production-grade deployment and ongoing lifecycle management.

 - Risk & Dependency Management: Proactively identify and mitigate technical risks, dependencies, and bottlenecks across distributed teams, ensuring seamless integration of AI models within the MDR pipeline.

 - Strategy & Governance: Define program management best practices for AI projects, ensuring that security, compliance, and performance standards are met throughout the development lifecycle.

 - Stakeholder Communication: Bridge the gap between highly technical AI researchers/engineers and executive stakeholders, translating complex technical hurdles into clear business outcomes and actionable roadmaps.

Required Skills & Qualifications

 - Cybersecurity Fluency: Strong understanding of the cybersecurity domain, including threat intelligence, SIEM/SOAR integration, and security operations (SecOps) workflows.

 - AI Program Management: 5+ years of experience in technical program management, with a proven track record of delivering large-scale AI or ML initiatives from concept to production.

 - Technical Depth: Ability to engage deeply with engineering teams on architectural decisions, particularly regarding LLM deployment, model performance, and data infrastructure.

 - Operational Rigor: Experience building scalable processes in high-growth startup environments, balancing the need for speed with the necessity of technical stability and security.

 - Communication & Influence: Exceptional ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority and to clearly communicate technical strategy to non-technical stakeholders.

Education & Certifications

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security, or a related field.

 - CISSP or other cybersecurity certifications are a significant plus.

Why Join Us?

 - Opportunity to work with cutting-edge AI-driven cybersecurity technologies and Google SecOps solutions.

 - Collaborate with a talented and innovative team focused on continuously improving security operations.

 - Competitive salary and benefits package.

 - A culture of growth and development, with opportunities to expand your knowledge in AI, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies.

jobs.title: IT Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role:

We are seeking an IT Security Engineer to own the security standards and controls that protect Alpaca’s workforce identities, endpoints, and critical business systems. The scope includes identity and access management, single sign-on, privileged access, multi-factor authentication, endpoint security, secure network access, and email security.

You will maintain those standards, measure how the controls are working, and partner with IT, who run devices and day-to-day administration.

This role reports to the Enterprise Security Architect and works closely with IT, DevOps, Engineering, GRC, and the wider Security team.

The Security Team is 100% distributed and remote.

Things You Get To Do:

The core responsibilities of the IT Security Engineer are focused on identity security, endpoint security, email and domain protection, and measurable control enforcement.

Identity and Access Security:

• IAM and SSO Standards: Define and maintain security standards for SSO and conditional access across cloud, SaaS, and internal systems.

• Multi-Factor Authentication: Own multi-factor authentication standards, including phishing-resistant methods, and keep them enforced.

• Privileged Access: Maintain privileged-access standards, approval policies, and periodic access reviews with system owners.

• Joiner, Mover, Leaver: Partner with IT and People teams so access changes are timely, complete, and auditable.

Endpoint, Email, and Domain Security:

• EDR Policy: Own endpoint detection and response policy and tuning, with IT handling deployment.

• Device Posture: Maintain device-posture and secure network access requirements for access to business applications.

• Control Measurement: Measure identity and endpoint controls and follow up where they are not met.

• Detection Partnership: Work with Security Operations on identity, endpoint, and email detections and response playbooks.

• Admin Access: Maintain security baselines for administrator access to critical SaaS platforms and vendor accounts.

• Vendor Security Events: Assess the identity and account impact when a SaaS provider or vendor reports a security event.

• Email Security: Own email authentication standards and email security configuration.

• Domain Protection: Maintain security standards for company domains and for monitoring lookalike domains.

• Phishing Response: Triage reported phishing and coordinate takedowns.

Incident Response and Collaboration:

• Incident Support: Lead the identity, endpoint, and email aspects of security incidents, including account containment.

• On-Call: Participate in the Security Operations on-call rotation after onboarding and cross-training.

• Enablement: Give IT and employees clear guidance on security requirements, so controls are adopted without slowing the business.

Who You Are (Must-Haves):

• Excited about Alpaca’s mission and what we’re building

• 3+ years of experience in IT security, identity security, or security engineering roles

• Hands-on experience with an identity provider and SSO, including SAML and OIDC

• Experience enforcing phishing-resistant MFA, such as FIDO2 or hardware security keys

• Hands-on experience with an endpoint detection and response platform

• Scripting or automation experience (Python, Bash, or PowerShell)

• Experience with zero-trust network access or device-posture controls

• Working knowledge of email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and phishing response

• Experience working closely with IT teams and translating security requirements into operational workflows

• Experience investigating identity, endpoint, or email security alerts

• Willing to participate in an on-call rotation

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially during incidents

• Comfortable working cross-functionally and handling escalations calmly and decisively

Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves):

• Experience securing financial, trading, or other highly regulated platforms

• Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001

• Experience with just-in-time privileged access tools

• Experience securing administrator access to SaaS platforms

• Experience with password managers and secrets management at company scale

• Experience with MDM platforms for macOS and Windows

• Experience with cloud IAM in AWS, GCP, or Azure

• Ability to balance security rigor with operational efficiency and business needs

How We Take Care of You:

• Competitive Salary & Stock Options

• Health Benefits

• New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500

• Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

Alpaca is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to pursuing and hiring a diverse workforce.

jobs.title: Batch Record Review Lead
jobs.description:
We're so happy you're here! Thank you for checking our job out and we hope to have the chance to meet you in our interview process!

About the role

Nothing we make ships until the paperwork proves it should. Today our Production Supervisors review every batch record on top of running the floor, which pulls them away from production and slows release. As our Batch Record Review Lead, you’ll own that process end to end at our Roanoke, TX facility. You’ll make sure every executed record is complete, accurate, and GMP-compliant, and that finished product never waits on a review.

This role is fully on-site at our Roanoke, TX facility. We’re hiring across three shifts (Monday–Friday):

• 1st shift: 6:00 am – 2:00 pm | $22/hr

• 2nd shift: 2:00 pm – 10:00 pm | $23/hr

• 3rd shift: 10:00 pm – 6:00 am | $24/hr

In this role, you will:

• Own day-to-day review of every executed batch record, so Production Supervisors can stay on the floor

• Check each record for completeness, accuracy, and GMP compliance before it goes to QA for review and release

• Complete reviews within one day of submission, consistently

• Verify master record version, lot numbers and quantities, equipment and cleaning entries, in-process checks, signatures, and dates

• Reconcile yield, labels, and components with precision

• Catch errors, omissions, and potential deviations early, and escalate to QA when a discrepancy is more than a simple correction

• Run a closed-loop process for returning records, tracking corrections to completion, and escalating deviations

• Track and report error trends, then work with Production and QA on the training and form changes that stop repeat errors

• Work on the production floor in required PPE, building trust with operators and Supervisors

We’re looking for someone who:

• Has 3+ years reviewing batch records or other controlled GMP documents in a regulated manufacturing setting, ideally supplements or food

• Has working knowledge of GMP, data integrity principles, and excellent documentation practices

• Is bilingual in English and Spanish

• Is comfortable in ERP and WMS systems (Fulfil.io is a plus)

• Is accurate with yield, label, and component reconciliation math

• Is comfortable working on the production floor in required PPE

Approach to the role:

• Treats record accuracy as non-negotiable

• Works systematically, in the same rigorous order every time

• Gives clear, respectful feedback to operators and Supervisors, even when it’s not what they want to hear

• Knows the difference between a simple correction and something that needs QA, and acts accordingly

• Looks for patterns and recommends fixes, not just corrections

• Builds enough trust with the production team that issues get raised early

• Moves with urgency and precision, because slow reviews hold product

Compensation & Benefits:

At Grüns, we’re committed to providing a competitive total compensation package — grounded in market data that considers our size, stage, industry, and location. For this role, the hourly rate is $22/hr for 1st shift, $23/hr for 2nd shift, and $24/hr for 3rd shift, paired with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the well-being and growth of our team.

A bit about us...

At Grüns, we believe that foundational nutrition should be simple and convenient for everyone. We're dedicated to bringing comprehensive and real nutrition to you through our gummies, formulated from 60 nutrient-dense and whole-food ingredients. Simply enjoy a grab-and-go snack pack of gummies daily whenever fits best in your schedule and wherever life takes you.

Like you, we were disappointed. There’s an infinite number of “nutrition” companies, all focused on what’s best for them — not what’s best for you. Hundreds of products to sell you on, low-quality ingredients, and small nutrient doses. We’ve seen it all.

So we decided it was time to fix it. No more choking on and popping pills like a pharmacy. No more clean-up and disgust from gross powders. And no more cobbling together handfuls to dozens of supplements. Grüns is comprehensive nutrition, made convenient and delicious.

What we care about...

Be the Best: We hold ourselves, our teams, and our partners to an incredibly high standard - and we raise the bar constantly. "We've never done this before" isn't an excuse here. It's an invitation.

Own It: We act like our name is on the door. That means taking complete ownership of outcomes, collaborating deeply, working through roadblocks - not around them - and never waiting for someone else to solve the problem. Great owners are great partners.

Drive Impact, Urgently: We measure impact, not effort. We work smart and hard, move fast, and use every tool at our disposal - including AI - to focus our energy where it matters most.

Compensation & Perks:

For every role, we aim to have highly competitive compensation and opportunity for impact and career growth.

Everyone at Grüns works hard, but we believe in wellness and balance too. We have super strong benefits coverage -- for you and your family, generous PTO, free Grüns, and a few more perks centered around health and well-being that we can't wait to tell you about!

Lifting

jobs.title: Behavior Clinician II  Adapted Dialectical Behavior Therapy Program
jobs.description:
The Clinician II will serve as a member of the Adapted Dialectical Behavior Therapy (A-DBT) team, dedicated to addressing the unique needs of individuals with developmental disabilities and comorbid mental health conditions. Individuals receiving services, which are provided in the home and community, are adults with multiple diagnoses and typically present with significant challenging behaviors. Using the principles of A-DBT, the Clinician II will provide assessment, clinical support and consultation based on their unique skills and needs of the individual. Supports include running A-DBT groups, leading social events, identifying challenges within the environment, creating support plans to increase positive behaviors and social skills to promote overall independence, and providing training/modeling to direct care staff in the home. Additionally, the Clinician II may provide training and supervision to Clinicians I and relevant operations roles on development of support plans, measurable goals, and data collection. The Clinician II will maintain a caseload under the supervision of the Clinical Services Manager for implementation of treatment as specified by their respective discipline (ABA, CBT, DBT, etc.) and as designated by the funding source

What You Get To Do:

• Manage caseload of individuals for treatment implementation, using DBT therapy.

• Conduct Functional Behavior Assessments and develop Positive Behavior Support Plans (BSPs)

• Provide clinical guidance to Direct Support Professionals and Program Supervisors

• Conduct program visits to interact with staff and support individuals

• Foster positive rapport with individuals, parents, and guardians

• Review data to ensure care meets individual's current needs

• Complete progress reports and update plans as necessary

• Assist in providing on-call support, crisis intervention and outreach as needed and appropriate.

• Consult and assist with assessment and implementation of supports needed such as reinforcement systems, coping skills, adaptive equipment, etc.

• Provide guidance and assistance with admission and discharge decisions on high needs cases.

• Participate in the debriefing of significant incidents of individuals on caseload when requested

• Attend person-centered planning meetings and home staffing meetings

• Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with external service providers including DDA, Consultants, Hospitals, Schools, ABA Providers, etc.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

• Must have a master's degree in psychology, behavior analysis, mental health, special education, social work, or other related discipline; or be graduating with master's degree within the next 6 months.
• 2+ years of professional experience with individuals with intellectual developmental disabilities (IDD) is required
• Relevant experience in designing and implementing support plans for individuals with developmental disabilities, autism, and/or challenging behaviors
• Experience with Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) preferred

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

jobs.description:
Domino’s Pizza Supply Chain Center is hiring for a Production Sanitation Associate.  The Production Sanitation Associate takes part in the complete processing and manufacturing of pizza dough in their distribution center.  Production Associates will rotate to various positions (dough maker, dough placer, tray washer, and cross/down stacker) throughout their shift.

The Production Sanitation Associate also cleans and sanitizes production equipment and areas and may be cross-trained to work in the warehouse or sanitation areas.

Schedule: 11 AM Start. 10 hour shift/4 days. OT mandatory as needed (Sunday-Friday)

Compensation: $22.00/hour; bi-weekly

Production Room and Dough Processing

• Determine correct batch recipe to gather, measure and mix ingredients Ensure dough is delivered into rounder
• Record batch data and maintain proofing library
• Achieve and maintain dough certification
• Metal detector checkups, and dough temperature, monitoring document accordingly

Dough Cooler and Staging Product for Shipment

• Troubleshoot automated equipment, when needed, such as stacker, dolly loader, and/or tray buffer

• Monitor gauges and setting to ensure water pressure, water temperature, and detergent levels consistently meet company standards determined to thoroughly clean and sanitize trays, record findings

• Be able to perform interventions as needed utilizing an HMI

• High school diploma or GED
• Ability to work with yeast and flour products
• Must successfully pass a pre-employment background check

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

• Ability to stand and/or walk for long periods of time, climb stairs, and lift up to 30 lbs. frequently and 50 lbs. on occasion, perform heavy pushing/pulling of product, work in refrigerated conditions [33-38 degrees], and work in environment with exposure to loud machinery, when necessary

Job duties include, but are not limited to:

Each pet has their own room or suite for down-time, but will participate in a Group-Play environment during the day as well, as long as they have passed our temperament test for Group-Play. For our Hotel pets who do not enjoy group play, they get one-on-one time with a kennel assistant dependent on their needs and/or requirements. The cleaning will entail keeping the individual pet's rooms/suites clean, but also the yards and wards clean/sterile in general. Duties include but are not limited to vacuuming, moping, doing laundry, feeding and medicating pets that are boarding. Our Group-Play environment is based off of the Dog-Gurus series called "Knowing Dogs 101 & 201." Knowing Dogs 101 is about Dog Language and Knowing Dogs 201 is about Group Play. We do require all of our staff to watch this series of 16 videos (that are about 20-25 minutes each) and pass the quizzes that go along with each lesson, this way our entire staff are all on the same page concerning dog behavior (from the doctors and receptionists to the kennel staff). We also have individual cat suites and a separate cat Play-Room, however cats will be rotated through their Play-Room individually, since cats are not so fond of a Group-Play environment (except for those that are boarding with a sibling), therefore we need our kennel assistants to also be comfortable handling kitties. Most importantly, we are looking for passionate individuals who enjoy not only the time with the pets, but interacting with the pet owners as well.

**Bathe and groom dogs according to hospital and client standards, ensuring pets are clean, comfortable, and well cared for.

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.
Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.
Prepare product.
Receive and process telephone orders.
Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.
Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.
Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).
Must be able to make correct monetary change.
Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.
Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.
Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.
In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.
Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.
Fumes from food odors.
Exposure to cornmeal dust.
Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.
Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
Depth perception.
Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.
Surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.
Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.
Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72 high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.
Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.
Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24- 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.
Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

At Domino's, we are a brand of honesty, transparency and accountability and we want exceptional people like you to join our team! We have continued to prove we “Put our People First” by making sure our work environment is safe and provides stability for you as a team member. The brand continues to deliver the “Power of Possible” to local Domino’s store owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores!

Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge.

For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles.

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more.

We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet.

Apex believes in creating a work environment that you look forward to embracing every day. Our employees love working at Apex, and we want you to love it too. We're a fast-growing startup that has raised more than $500M in funding, and we invest heavily in our people from day one.

jobs.title: Mission Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge.

For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles.

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more.

We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet. 




ABOUT THE ROLE

In this position, you will own or contribute to the authorization posture of two systems: a space vehicle and a classified cloud mission operations environment. You will contribute to cyber engineering and produce RMF authorization documentation, build and sustain authorization packages, own the plan of action and milestones day to day, and run continuous monitoring. This is mission systems work throughout, not traditional enterprise IT security.

We are open to candidates from ISSE, SSE, ISSM, or ISSO backgrounds, and are hiring across levels: from new and recent graduates through senior engineering, officer, and manager experience.

Responsibilities:
May include any or all of the following:

Authorization Ownership

 - Build and sustain authorization packages for both boundaries: system description, boundary definition, categorization, control selection and tailoring rationale, implementation statements, assessment coordination, and the residual risk picture carried to the AO.

 - Get assessors engaged early on our evidence-generation approach so generated artifacts are trusted before a package depends on them.

 - Own the POA&M.

 - Maintain the authorization system of record (eMASS or equivalent).

Space Vehicle Segment

 - Own the authorization boundary determination for the flight segment and the rationale that survives assessor scrutiny.

 - Categorize under CNSSI 1253 and defend overlay selection, treating the Space Platform Overlay as the starting place it is rather than a finished answer — pushing back where our onboard security capability exceeds what the published tailoring assumes.

 - Tailor the control baseline with per-control rationale, using Aerospace's Space Segment Cybersecurity Profile (TOR-2023-02161 Rev A) and SPARTA-linked tailoring, including arguing controls back in where our onboard capability exceeds what those baselines assumed.

 - Define the type-authorization for the bus and design how each vehicle off the line generates its own conformance evidence so fleet growth does not mean linear growth in assessment labor.

 - Derive verifiable security requirements from threat using SPARTA TTPs as the traceability key, owned by the software and mission integration engineers who will build and test against them.

 - Translate verification and production artifacts into assessment evidence and tell engineering early when what they produce will not satisfy an assessor.

 - Own the continuous monitoring story for a fielded fleet: security audit downlinked across contact windows, configuration drift across vehicles, and on-orbit software update as a recurring authorization event.

Classified Cloud Mission Operations Environment

 - Define and document the authorization boundary for mission systems in classified cloud (AWS, Azure classified regions, or equivalent), including impact-level scoping and the seam with ground stations and the RF edge.

 - Own the control and evidence story for operator command authority: identity, role separation, least privilege, two-person integrity, non-repudiation, and complete audit of every command that reaches the vehicle.

 - Build and defend the control inheritance model and prove the customer-responsible set with live evidence rather than assertion, validating what the cloud service provider and the platform satisfy versus what remains customer responsibility for the mission-unique applications.

 - Implement controls as code, so infrastructure-as-code, policy-as-code, and pipeline configuration serve as the implementation and the evidence at once.

 - Make change control and continuous monitoring work at operations tempo, never putting a contact window at risk, positioned for the DoD transition toward the Cybersecurity Risk Management Construct (CSRMC) and continuous authorization.

 - Manage security incident reporting and coordination for the boundary.

Automation and Generation

 - Define what evidence you need and in what form.

 - Design the OSCAL-based evidence data model and the mapping layer that resolves a property assertion to control identifiers across 800-53, CNSSI 1253 baselines, overlays, and program-unique control sets.

 - Build the pipeline that renders SSP sections, assessment evidence, POA&M items, and continuous monitoring reports deterministically from pinned evidence snapshots.

 - Integrate with the authorization system of record (eMASS or equivalent) programmatically, so generated artifacts land where assessors actually look.

 - Use AI-assisted drafting and crosswalk tooling for control narratives, framework mappings, and monitoring summaries, with human review on anything an AO reads and full traceability from every statement to a source record.

 - Push toward controls whose satisfaction is demonstrated by system state rather than by narrative.

Required Qualifications

At Every Level

 - U.S. Citizenship (must possess the ability to access export-controlled data)

 - Active Top Secret clearance with SCI access and SAP eligibility strongly preferred

 - Experience with technical tooling: reading pipeline output, querying an API, interpreting scanner and configuration state

Entry Level (1–3+ Years)

 - Bachelor's, master's, or PhD in systems engineering, computer science, cybersecurity, aerospace, or a related field

 - Clear experience with hands-on building via coursework, internships, research code, personal projects, CTFs, a co-op, or an early role and/or some exposure to RMF, security compliance, cloud, or software engineering

 - Willingness to learn RMF from the ground up, with a demonstrated ability to pick up a complicated technical domain quickly and hold a lot of detail without losing the thread

Senior Level (5–10+ Years)

 - Strong experience in embedded/space systems or cloud infrastructure

 - Multiple systems taken to authorization in national security or DoD environments, with fluency in RMF as practiced: categorization under CNSSI 1253, overlay selection, tailoring rationale, assessment coordination, POA&M management, continuous monitoring, and reauthorization triggers

 - Ability to speak concretely about categorization, tailoring, assessment, and authorization, and to design, document, or test a report and determine whether it constitutes evidence that a control is satisfied

 - Direct experience with at least one accredited cloud environment and one non-traditional system such as embedded, weapons, platform IT, industrial, or space

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with OSCAL, eMASS APIs, Xacta, controls-as-code, or continuous-controls-monitoring implementation 

 - Skilled in Python, Go, or equivalent, in CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, and Git-based workflows

 - Experience with continuous authorization, ongoing authorization, or cATO

 - Experience building with AI-assisted development

 - Understanding of Mission Operations including satellite command and control, mission planning, flight dynamics, telemetry processing, or multi-mission ground segments

 - Embedded or safety-critical background in space, automotive, or industrial control

 - Experience with SPARTA, NIST IR 8270 or IR 8401, CCSDS security standards, Space Platform Overlay, NASA/Space Force system protection standards, or space-system threat modeling

 - Experience with classified cloud accreditation at IL5/IL6 or IC equivalents, or accreditation under JSIG or ICD 703

 - Qualified, or able to qualify, under DoDM 8140.03 for a systems security engineering, security architecture, or Information Systems Security Manager work role. CISSP, CISSP-ISSEP, CISM, and SecurityX map well.

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role:

We are seeking a Security Operations Engineer to own the daily operation and continuous improvement of Alpaca’s SIEM and SOAR capabilities. You will onboard security logs, develop and tune detections, keep alerts actionable, maintain operational dashboards, and automate repeatable response actions.

You will be hands-on and operationally minded. You will keep log onboarding, detection quality, and alert handling consistent, and you will turn security signals into action as the business grows.

This role reports to the Enterprise Security Architect and works closely with Security, IT, DevOps, and Engineering.

The Security Team is 100% distributed and remote.

Things You Get To Do:

The core responsibilities of the Security Operations Engineer are focused on detection, response automation, operational excellence, and cross-functional coordination.

SIEM Operations and Detection Engineering:

• Log Onboarding: Onboard new security log sources across cloud, identity, endpoint, SaaS, and application systems, including parsing, normalization, and data quality checks.

• Detection Development: Build, test, and tune detection rules based on threat intelligence, incident learnings, and emerging attack techniques, mapped to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.

• Alert Quality: Tune, enrich, and manage the lifecycle of detections so alerts stay actionable.

• Detection Coverage: Maintain detections for critical systems and priority attack techniques.

• Operational Dashboards: Build and maintain dashboards for alert volume, ingest health, and response status.

Incident Response & Metrics:

• Incident Support: Support security incidents with evidence collection, detection queries, and containment actions, working with IT, Engineering, and external partners.

• Runbooks: Develop and improve alert-handling and incident response runbooks and escalation paths.

• Operational Metrics: Track and report security operations metrics, including mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to respond (MTTR).

• On-Call: Participate in the Security Operations on-call rotation after onboarding and cross-training.

SOAR and Response Automation:

• Playbooks: Design, build, and maintain SOAR playbooks that automate repeatable response actions, including enrichment, containment, ticketing, and notification.

• Triage and Investigation: Triage, investigate, and respond to security alerts across endpoints, identity, cloud, network, and application logs.

• Threat Hunting: Run hypothesis-driven hunts based on threat intelligence and incident learnings, and turn findings into new detections.

Who You Are (Must-Haves):

• Excited about Alpaca’s mission and what we’re building

• 3+ years of experience in Security Operations or detection engineering roles

• Hands-on experience operating and tuning a SIEM

• Experience building SOAR playbooks or equivalent response automation

• Working with Linux

• Scripting or automation experience (Python, Bash) for security operations tasks

• Experience onboarding and parsing log sources from cloud, identity, and SaaS platforms

• Strong alert investigation skills across identity, endpoint, network, and cloud environments

• Understanding of common attacker techniques and detection methodologies

• Experience supporting security incidents, including evidence collection, detection queries, and containment

• Willing to participate in an on-call rotation

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially during incidents

• Comfortable working cross-functionally and handling escalations calmly and decisively

Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves):

• Experience securing financial, trading, or other highly regulated platforms

• Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001

• Experience with detection-as-code, GitOps, and CI/CD pipelines

• Knowledge of cloud security logging (AWS/GCP/Azure) and SaaS security telemetry

• Familiarity with Kubernetes-hosted security tooling

• Experience working with a managed SOC or MSSP

• Security certifications (GCIA, GCIH, GCED, or similar)

• Ability to balance security rigor with operational efficiency and business needs

How We Take Care of You:

jobs.title: Scientist I, High-Throughput Biology
jobs.description:
Eikon Therapeutics is a new biopharmaceutical company employing revolutionary technology at the intersection of chemistry, engineering, computation, and biology to discover novel treatments for life-threatening diseases. Eikon’s discovery platform is built on groundbreaking innovations from its founders (Nobel Prize, 2014), culminating in the creation of microscopes which enable real time, molecular-resolution measurements of protein movement in living cells, thereby unlocking otherwise intractable classes of proteins as drug targets.

Position

As a member of the High-Throughput Biology Team, you will play a key role in pioneering drug discovery screening assays using Eikon’s proprietary live-cell, single-molecule high-throughput super-resolution microscopy platform. You will work at the intersection of biology, automation engineering, and computational science to design, execute and deliver scalable, reproducible, decision-enabling biological data that drives progress across drug discovery portfolios.

About You

You are a highly motivated, rigorous, and interdisciplinary scientist who enjoys developing, optimizing, and validating live-cell imaging-based assays at scale to push the frontier of drug discovery. You are creative, data-driven, and skilled at problem solving in a fast-paced, dynamic, and matrixed environment. You are conscientious, detail-oriented, and organized, and are committed to delivering high-quality and actionable data in a timely manner. You are an effective communicator and teammate who is eager to learn and collaborate with people from diverse scientific backgrounds.

What You’ll Do

• Design, execute, and analyze robust and reproducible experiments to optimize, validate, and scale up live-cell imaging-based assays for high-throughput screening using Eikon’s proprietary super-resolution microscopy platform.

• Collaborate with computational biologists and software engineers to apply state-of-the-art computational and statistical methods including machine-learning to analyze large datasets.

• Summarize and deliver timely, high-quality and actionable data to drive project team decisions across drug discovery portfolios.

• Exercise good scientific judgment and provide data-driven recommendations to project teams.

• Maintain organized and comprehensive electronic records of experiments, results, and protocols in adherence to company standards and regulatory requirements.

• Work closely with the High-Throughput Biology Operations Team to transfer optimized processes into productionized operations workflows with well-documented standard operating procedures.

• Collaborate and communicate across a diverse team of biologists, chemists, and engineers.

• Contribute to the growth and training of junior scientists.

Qualifications

• Ph.D. or Master’s plus 10 years of relevant experience or Bachelor’s degree plus 12 years of relevant experience in Biology, Bioengineering, Biotechnology, or related field.

• Proficiency in mammalian cell culture with sterile technique.

jobs.description:
US – Seattle only:

This position is open to candidates in the Seattle, WA area. You will have a hybrid remote/in-office schedule where you will work from our casual, pet-friendly office at least 3 days a week (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday).

Trupanion is seeking a Software Architect who is responsible for designing and evolving scalable, secure, and maintainable technology solutions that power Trupanion's Insurance Platform capabilities. This role serves as a technical leader and trusted partner to engineering, product, and business stakeholders, ensuring technology solutions align with business objectives while delivering exceptional customer and operational outcomes.

This is a hands-on architecture role that balances strategic thinking with practical execution. The Software Architect partners closely with Software Development Managers, Principal Engineers, Product Managers, Infrastructure & Cloud, DevOps, development, and business teams to define technical direction, guide implementation, and solve complex business and technology challenges.

Success in this role requires deep technical expertise in modern cloud-native architectures, strong business acumen, the ability to transform existing platforms, and the ability to influence technical decisions while remaining closely connected to implementation, delivery outcomes, and business needs.

Key Outcomes & Impact

The Software Architect will:

• Define scalable architecture solutions that support Trupanion's Insurance Technology strategy and business goals.
• Improve system reliability, performance, maintainability, operations, and security across insurance platforms through influence and direct contribution.
• Accelerate delivery by providing clear architectural guidance, reusable patterns, and technical leadership.
• Leverage AI to both improve time-to-market and quality of software overall. Be an evangelist for effective and secure use of AI to improve business outcomes.
• Reduce technical debt through thoughtful modernization and architectural evolution.
• Ensure technology investments to maximize business value through a strong preference for buy vs. build, integrating, and extending proven solutions before building custom software.
• Enable engineering teams to move faster through pragmatic and actionable architecture decisions.

Core Responsibilities:

Solution & Platform Architecture

• Design architecture solutions that support policy administration, billing, claims processing, payments, customer servicing, underwriting, and partner integrations.
• Define system interactions, integration patterns, data flows, and service boundaries.
• Create and maintain architecture artifacts including solution designs, sequence diagrams, data models, and technical roadmaps.
• Ensure solutions align with established technology standards and architectural principles.
• Design highly available, scalable, and secure distributed systems using modern software architecture practices.
• Promote engineering best practices, including domain-driven design, RESTful API-first development, event-driven architectures, test-gated CI/CD pipelines, observability, and automated testing.
• Define standards for resiliency, performance, maintainability, and operational excellence.
• Collaborate with engineering teams to ensure architecture decisions are successfully implemented.

Technology Evaluation & Innovation

• Stay current with trends in cloud computing, insurance technology, software architecture, and AI-assisted development.

Platform Modernization

• Assess existing systems and identify opportunities for simplification, modernization, and technical debt reduction.

• Lead architectural efforts to decompose existing systems as appropriate and improve platform flexibility.
• Ensure modernization of work aligns with long-term business and technology goals.

Technical Leadership

• Guide engineering teams through architecture decisions, tradeoffs, and implementation challenges.

Collaboration & Communication

• Collaborate effectively with Product Management, Engineering, Security, Data, Infrastructure & DevOps, and Business stakeholders.

jobs.title: Senior Information Security Risk Specialist (GRC)
jobs.description:
Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Senior Information Security Risk Specialist, you will be tasked with understanding and supporting the design of SentinelOne's organizational, procedural, and technological security controls within the context of the security frameworks applicable to SentinelOne, bringing a security-focused mindset that balances risk, business drivers, and timelines. You will identify and test appropriate controls to ensure they are designed, implemented, and operating effectively to mitigate risk, and help implement, automate, document, and maintain those controls while supporting and responding to inquiries from internal and external stakeholders. This role calls for someone who is self-directed and able to work independently and collaboratively.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

• Support the planning and performance of IT risk-based security audits and projects, risk assessments, execution of fieldwork, and communication to stakeholders.

• Help evaluate relevant global standards, compliance frameworks, and regulations to analyze existing controls, identify areas for improvement, and design control growth.

• Collaborate with process and control owners through the audit lifecycle for process documentation updates, testing coordination, remediation of identified deficiencies, and advising on internal control enhancements or process changes, as appropriate.

• Proactively manage audit findings, tracking and documentation of status updates obtained via action owners, and timely execution of remediation activities.

• Participate in internal security and compliance programs and track recurring controls, such as SSAE 18 SOC 2 and ISO 27001/27002, and help support internal and external audits and evidence collection via a GRC tool.

• Provide control consultative support to the business to assist in redesign efforts that improve the control environment, with the objective of mitigating risk and improving compliance and operational performance.

• Document new and update existing policies, procedures, standards, and resources.

• Participate in the security awareness program, training personnel on data security and privacy-related processes and responsibilities.

• Help support customer security reviews, RFPs, and external security and privacy inquiries.

• Participate in defining, collecting, and tracking various security metrics.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

• 5 or more years of experience working in information security, risk, or compliance.

• Experience working with security controls across at least some of the following domains: access management, encryption, risk management, network security, configuration management, patch management, change management, awareness and training, and BC/DRP.

• Ability to perform internal audits with minimal direct supervision, exhibit professional audit judgment, and experience in a broad range of audit projects such as SSAE 16/18 SOC 2, ISO 27001/2, and NIST.

• Strong risk management experience, performing assessments and audits, designing controls, managing enterprise control frameworks, and prioritizing risk.

• Strong project management skills and the ability to manage a variety of projects simultaneously to completion within agreed timelines.

• Excellent collaboration and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate effectively, in writing and verbally, to target audiences at all levels of the organization, including customers, partners, auditors, executive management, vendors, and peers.

• Experience working with both technical and non-technical teams.

• Ability and desire to understand the intent of requirements and provide effective recommendations.

• An advanced degree in computer science, information technology, information security, or a related field is preferred, as are relevant certifications such as ISO 27001 LA/LI, CISA, CISM, CISSP, or CRISC.

• Experience with, and a strong understanding of, common security compliance frameworks, controls, and best practices such as COSO, SOC 2, SOX ITGC, ISO 27001/27002, GDPR, PCI, and NIST is preferred, as is the ability to assess and pragmatically define scope and relevant controls, and a strong desire to continuously develop and deepen technical skills.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.

We invest in our Sentinels with comprehensive, competitive benefits designed to support you and your family:

Equity & Rewards

• Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)

• Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

Time Off & Wellbeing

• Competitive leave benefits

• Gender-neutral parental leave

Insurance & Financial Security

• Private medical, dental, and vision insurance

Work Perks & Flexibility

• Global home office allowance

• Internet or mobile phone allowance

• Hybrid work model with flexible hours

Wellness & Lifestyle

• Wellness programs

Growth & Community

• In-office lunch program

SentinelOne is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

SentinelOne participates in the E-Verify Program for all U.S. based roles.

To learn more about how we use AI in our hiring process, please review our AI in Hiring Candidate Disclosure.

jobs.title: Emergency Veterinary Assistant (Overnight)- Redmond, WA
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the best experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

At VEG, we don’t just hire assistants—we grow future emergency rockstars. As an Emergency Veterinary Assistant, you’ll be in the heart of the action from day one, supporting your team, comforting pet parents, and learning the ropes in real time. You’ll be there for everything—the triage, the treatments, and the tail wags. You’re embarking on a path where careers start, grow, and thrive. Whether you’re on your way to becoming a credentialed technician or exploring where your passion can take you, we’ll say yes to your growth every step of the way.

WHAT YOU’LL DO*

• Be the first warm welcome and a steady support, triaging incoming patients and helping guide them toward care

• Assist with treatments, nursing care, and diagnostics, from bloodwork and imaging to catheter placement and oxygen support

• Work alongside our credentialed veterinary technicians and veterinarians to set up and monitor anesthesia and sedation cases

• Set up and manage IV fluids, blood transfusions, and medication administration

• Assist during every moment of care: outpatient or inpatient, exam room to treatment area

• Join patient rounds and stay close to the clinical picture to ensure continuity of care

• Learn how to perform CPR and become a RECOVER Certified Rescuer (training provided!)

• Grow into more advanced responsibilities, such as anesthesia support, ultrasound, and catheterization through guided training pathways

*As permitted by state law

WHAT YOU NEED

• High school diploma or equivalent required

• Enrolled in an AVMA-accredited veterinary technology program a plus

• 1+ years in a veterinary assistant role (emergency or specialty experience is a bonus!)

• Basic computer skills and an understanding of practice management software and electronic medical record keeping

• Excellent communicator when collaborating with pet parents and your team

• Fine motor skills for handling patients and medical equipment

• Ability to stand for prolonged hours, kneel, and work on the floor as well as ability to lift up to 25 kg on own and able to support up to 40 kg with assistance

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital demands

• Ability to work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation, including base and 401K match: Pay range is $20-$49 per hour, and is based on a leveling system and experience

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, QPR training, and access to free therapy or counseling

• Depending on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave; up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

jobs.title: Staff Maintenance / Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
Vulcan Elements is manufacturing American rare-earth permanent magnets for a secure, resilient future. With a focus on national security and economic resiliency, we serve critical industries such as defense, aerospace, and automotive powering a high-technology future. Vulcan Elements is building a team of ambitious professionals committed to Mission Focus, Technical Excellence and Integrity.

As our Staff Maintenance / Reliability Engineer you will support equipment design, installation, commissioning, and startup while developing maintenance strategies and technical standards that sustain safe, reliable production. Core responsibilities include detailed equipment failure analysis, materials of construction evaluations, engineered seal and gasket selection, and development of preventive and predictive maintenance programs. The role will also help build the site's CMMS, translating OEM requirements and operating experience into accurate asset data and executable maintenance plans.

The ideal candidate combines sound engineering judgment with practical experience troubleshooting complex industrial equipment. They will work directly with technicians, equipment vendors, R&D, Operations, and Engineering to resolve technical problems, capture lessons from the pilot plant, and continuously improve equipment performance.

Responsibilities

• Lead detailed equipment and component failure investigations, including field inspection, teardown, operating-data review, materials evaluation, root cause determination, and verification of corrective actions.

• Identify and evaluate failure mechanisms such as fatigue, corrosion, erosion, abrasion, thermal degradation, chemical incompatibility, mechanical overstress, and premature component wear.

• Apply equipment criticality assessments, FMEA, and reliability-centered maintenance principles to identify risks, prioritize improvements, and define appropriate maintenance strategies.

• Analyze downtime, repeat failures, MTBF, MTTR, and maintenance history to establish reliability priorities and measure the effectiveness of engineered solutions.

• Engage OEMs, component suppliers, and technical laboratories as needed to validate failure mechanisms, specify design improvements, and prevent recurrence.

• Evaluate and recommend materials of construction for equipment components based on temperature, pressure, vacuum service, process chemistry, corrosion, erosion, wear, and mechanical loading.

• Develop component-selection and replacement strategies for gaskets, O-rings, mechanical seals, packing, and other sealing systems, considering chemical compatibility, thermal cycling, leakage risk, operating life, and serviceability.

• Investigate seal and gasket failures, including compression set, chemical attack, extrusion, thermal aging, installation damage, and sealing-surface deterioration; translate findings into improved specifications and maintenance practices.

• Work with Engineering, OEMs, and Procurement to validate component alternatives, standardize approved materials and sealing designs, and establish reliable spare-part specifications.

Maintenance Engineering and CMMS Setup

• Help configure and populate the CMMS from startup, including equipment asset registers, functional locations, hierarchies, equipment criticality, and master data standards.

• Develop asset-specific PM and predictive maintenance content: inspection routines, lubrication requirements, task instructions, frequencies, condition-monitoring points, estimated labor, and initial job plans.

• Establish equipment bills of materials, critical-spares recommendations, component specifications, interchangeability information, and replacement criteria in coordination with MRO and Maintenance leadership.

• Define consistent equipment failure codes, maintenance history requirements, and technical documentation; validate asset data and work-order workflows before equipment handover.

• Use commissioning results, pilot experience, and maintenance history to refine PM strategies, improve CMMS data quality, and eliminate unnecessary or ineffective maintenance tasks.

Pilot Plant Support, Commissioning and Equipment Readiness

• Provide hands-on maintenance and reliability engineering support to the R&D pilot plant, including troubleshooting, equipment inspections, component evaluations, and recurring-failure investigations.

• Capture pilot operating experience, equipment failure modes, wear patterns, and maintenance learnings; translate these into commercial equipment specifications, spare-parts strategies, and maintenance plans.

• Participate in design reviews, equipment installation, FAT, SAT, commissioning, and startup to identify maintainability risks and verify equipment readiness for sustained operation.

• Work with OEMs and project teams to resolve reliability, sealing, materials compatibility, access, and serviceability concerns before equipment turnover.

• Establish equipment baseline condition, maintenance documentation, PM content, special tools, and critical spares required for a disciplined handover to Operations and Maintenance.

Technical Support, Safety and Continuous Improvement

• Partner with Maintenance Managers and skilled trades on complex troubleshooting, precision installation, alignment, lubrication, inspection methods, and post-maintenance verification.

• Support mechanical integrity, equipment inspection, engineering change control, and safe maintenance practices for high-hazard manufacturing equipment and systems.

• Develop technical scopes and justifications for component upgrades, reliability modifications, and capital improvements that reduce downtime and lifecycle cost.

Responsibilities are representative and may change with business needs and the specific role.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field; equivalent technical education and substantial relevant industrial experience may be considered.

• 5+ of maintenance engineering, reliability engineering, or equipment engineering experience in an industrial manufacturing or process environment.

• Strong working knowledge of industrial machinery and manufacturing systems, including mechanical equipment, rotating assets, hydraulic and pneumatic systems, and automated production equipment.

• Demonstrated experience conducting detailed equipment failure investigations and implementing sustainable engineering solutions to recurring reliability problems.

• Practical knowledge of materials compatibility, industrial seals and gaskets, common component degradation mechanisms, and appropriate material selection for process service.

• Experience developing preventive maintenance content, equipment asset data, technical documentation, and CMMS maintenance plans, with strong field troubleshooting and cross-functional communication skills.

• Working knowledge of industrial maintenance safety, including LOTO, stored-energy hazards, and safe work practices around complex industrial equipment.

Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting pilot plants, greenfield facilities, major equipment installation, commissioning, or production ramp-up.

• Background in metals processing, chemical manufacturing, advanced materials, automotive, or other equipment-intensive manufacturing; experience with furnaces, vacuum systems, powder handling, or precision machinery is particularly relevant.

• Familiarity with RCM, condition monitoring, mechanical integrity programs, and reliability certifications such as CMRP or CRE.

Physical and Environmental Requirements

The position requires regular presence on the production floor and the ability to navigate all areas of the facility. Candidates must be able to climb stairs, stand and walk for extended periods, and work in environments that may be hot, humid, or noisy. The role also requires the use of personal protective equipment, including respirators, and adherence to all applicable safety policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements. Employees must be able to complete required fit testing, wear appropriate PPE for the duration of assigned tasks, and respond safely to changing conditions within the production environment.

What You'll Do

As a Behavior Analyst, you'll play an active role in developing and supporting individualized behavioral services that promote independence, safety, and quality of life.

jobs.title: Inventory Control Lead
jobs.description:
We're so happy you're here! Thank you for checking our job out and we hope to have the chance to meet you in our interview process!

About the role

Grüns is growing fast, and inventory accuracy now decides whether orders ship on time and in full. Today, inventory at our Roanoke facility runs mostly through one person. We’re hiring its first dedicated owner, who will make the numbers right, keep them right, and build the system that holds it all together.

This role is on-site at our Roanoke, TX facility, working alongside the warehouse team every day.

In this role, you will:

• Own inventory accuracy at our Roanoke facility from end to end

• Run the daily cycle count program, investigating every variance to root cause and making sure the fix is reflected in the system

• Lead two full physical inventory counts a year, on schedule

• Monitor stock levels and flag shortages, overstock, damaged product, and expiring product before they affect a shipment

• Write the SOPs we don’t have yet: storage, counting, variance investigation, and adjustments

• Report inventory accuracy on a regular cadence, with a target of 98% or higher, along with a recurring view of slow-moving, overstocked, and expiring inventory

• Take day-to-day inventory management off our Warehouse Manager’s plate and drive process improvements that cut errors and add efficiency

We’re looking for someone who:

• Has 3+ years in inventory control, cycle counting, or warehouse operations, ideally in food or supplements

• Has built or improved a cycle count or accuracy process and can show the measurable result

• Has hands-on WMS/ERP experience (Fulfil.io is a plus) and is fluent with barcode scanners

Approach to the role:

• Treats accuracy as non-negotiable

• Takes extreme ownership and doesn’t need to be managed

At Grüns, we’re committed to providing a competitive total compensation package, grounded in market data that considers our size, stage, industry, and location. At Grüns, we believe that foundational nutrition should be simple and convenient for everyone.
