Drive Impact, Urgently: We measure impact, not effort. We work smart and hard, move fast, and use every tool at our disposal - including AI - to focus our energy where it matters most.

Compensation & Perks:

For every role, we aim to have highly competitive compensation and opportunity for impact and career growth.

Everyone at Grüns works hard, but we believe in wellness and balance too. We have super strong benefits coverage -- for you and your family, generous PTO, free Grüns, and a few more perks centered around health and well-being that we can't wait to tell you about!

jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer (Starlink Enterprise)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK ENTERPRISE)

At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

The Starlink Enterprise Software team builds interfaces and systems for Starlink’s largest customers. Starlink powers complex and critical tasks across hundreds of sectors: emergency response, education, transportation, telecommunications, construction, and many more. As an engineer on this team, you’ll build tools to manage thousands of Starlink devices around the world, the core backend systems to serve that data, and the internal interfaces used by our sales and operations teams. You’ll get the chance to work across the stack: from UI/UX design to distributed systems engineering to working with embedded software. We don’t have project managers; engineers on the team are directly responsible for delivering the best internet experience from space for humans everywhere on Earth.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Engineer well-architected, responsive, performant, and reliable software for Starlink customers and internal users

• Deep dive into your users’ problems to find and create efficient solutions

• Build excellent frontends for modern browsers

• Design, build, maintain, and debug complex backend systems

• Work closely with technical and non-technical partners to drive successful outcomes for the business

• Bring your voice to the table in team collaborations on architecture, design, and code reviews

• Collaborate with other engineering teams across Starlink to advance our engineering process and culture

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a STEM discipline and 5+ years of experience building full-stack software; OR 7+ years of professional experience building full-stack software in lieu of a degree (internship experience is applicable)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Programming experience in an object-oriented language

• Strong attention to detail

• A drive to deliver exceptional user experiences for customers and willingness to own all outcomes

• Front-end experience in a Javascript or Typescript framework

• Experience working with relational databases

• Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery concepts

• Experience with large-scale and/or performance-critical application development

• Experience with UNIX-like operating systems and CI/CD tools

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 3: $175,000.00 - $280,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

Interns at IMA are a big deal! We understand how significant your decision on where to spend an internship is and what a positive experience can do to catapult your career. jobs.title: HRIS Analyst
jobs.description:
Step into the innovative world of LG Electronics. As a global leader in technology, LG Electronics is dedicated to creating innovative solutions for a better life. Our brand promise, 'Life's Good', embodies our commitment to ensuring a happier life for all. We have a rich history spanning over six decades and a global presence in over 290 locations.  Our diverse portfolio includes Home Appliance Solutions, Media Entertainment Solutions, Vehicle Solutions, and Eco Solutions.  Our management philosophy, "Jeong-do Management," embodies our commitment to high ethical standards and transparent operations. Grounded in the principles of 'Customer-Value Creation' and 'People-Oriented Management', these values shape our corporate culture, fostering creativity, diversity, and integrity. At LG, we believe in the power of collective wisdom through an inclusive work environment.  Join us and become a part of a company that is shaping the future of technology.  At LG, we strive to make Life Good for Everyone.

Join us and be a part of a team that makes Life Good by valuing innovation, efficiency, and continuous improvement. As an HRIS Analyst, you will support Human Resources Information Systems (HRIS) and related technology platforms that enable HR operations across the organization.

In this role, you will assist with maintaining HR systems, supporting system users, producing reports, ensuring data integrity, testing system changes, and contributing to process improvement initiatives. You will work closely with HR, Payroll, Benefits, Talent Acquisition, and other business stakeholders to ensure HR technology solutions effectively support business needs.

As part of the North America HR Center of Excellence, you will help drive operational excellence by leveraging HR technology, supporting system enhancements, and improving the employee experience through efficient and reliable HR processes. This role provides an excellent opportunity to develop expertise in HR systems, analytics, and HR operations while contributing to meaningful business initiatives.

Essential Responsibilities

HRIS Administration & Support

• Support daily administration and maintenance of HR systems and related platforms.

• Assist users with HR system inquiries, troubleshooting, and issue resolution.

• Monitor system functionality and escalate complex issues when necessary.

• Maintain and update employee and organizational data to ensure accuracy and completeness.

• Assist with user access management and security administration processes.

System Enhancements & Testing

• Participate in system upgrades, enhancements, implementations, and configuration changes.

• Prepare and execute system testing plans and validate results.

• Document business requirements, system processes, and standard operating procedures.

• Identify opportunities for improving system functionality and user experience.

Reporting & Analytics

• Create, maintain, and distribute standard HR reports and dashboards.

• Support HR data analysis and audits to ensure data quality and compliance.

• Assist in gathering metrics and workforce data to support business decision-making.

• Collaborate with stakeholders to develop ad hoc reports and reporting solutions.

Data Integrity & Compliance

• Perform routine audits and validation reviews to maintain HR data accuracy.

• Assist in ensuring compliance with company policies, HR procedures, and applicable regulations.

• Support data governance initiatives and maintain documentation standards.

Process Improvement

• Participate in HR process improvement projects and workflow automation initiatives.

• Recommend efficiencies and technology solutions to reduce manual work and improve service delivery.

• Support training efforts and help educate end users on HR systems and processes.

• Assist with identifying recurring user issues and contributing to long-term solutions.

Qualifications

Required Education & Experience

• Bachelor's degree in human resources, Information Systems, Business Administration, Computer Science, or a related field.

• 0–3 or more years of experience supporting HR systems, HR operations, data analytics, payroll, benefits administration, or related business functions.

• Internship or project experience involving HR technology, reporting, or systems administration is highly desirable.

Knowledge & Skills

• Foundational understanding of HR processes, HR systems, and employee lifecycle management.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work with large datasets while maintaining attention to detail and accuracy.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including data analysis and reporting functions.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Low Code Agents
jobs.description:
LIFE AT UIPATH

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?




YOUR MISSION

We're seeking a Principal Product Manager to help advance our Agentic Automation vision by making UiPath the best place to build agents without writing code. You'll shape how builders create two kinds of agents. Autonomous agents carry out tasks inside business processes. Conversational agents work directly with people. Your scope covers Agent Builder end to end and the agent experiences inside our Maestro canvases. It also covers AI assisted features built into these experiences: Autopilot, our platform-native coding agent, and Agent Reviewer, an agentic validator that checks an agent's quality and suggests improvements before it ships. You'll bring all of this together by turning shared platform capabilities like tools, context, memory, guardrails, and evals into a setup experience that feels effortless.

This is a high-agency, AI-native role. You won't be running status meetings. You'll be deep in the product: building agents, prototyping with coding agents, talking with customers and FDEs, and turning what you learn into crisp direction for the engineers who build it. Influence, not headcount, will be your default leverage.

Your north star is simple. Builders should go from idea to production-ready agent faster on UiPath than anywhere else. Their agents should be capable enough for real business processes and dependable enough that enterprises trust them with non-deterministic work.

#LI-MH1




WHAT YOU'LL DO AT UIPATH

 - Set the multi-year vision for low-code agent building on UiPath, across autonomous and conversational agents, in Agent Builder and across our Maestro canvases.

 - Own Agent Builder end to end. That covers how builders define an agent's goal, instructions, tools, context, and outputs, and how they test, debug, and publish it.

 - Shape Autopilot's agent-building experience: what it can build from a description, how it reasons about a process, and how it hands its work back to the builder for review.

 - Lead Agent Reviewer, which tells builders whether an agent is ready for production and what to fix first. Partner with the governance, evals, and ML teams on how agents are scored.

 - Design how builders set up shared capabilities (tools, context, memory, guardrails, evals) inside the builder, working alongside the teams that own each engine.

 - Define how low-code agents fit into complex business processes alongside deterministic workflows, with clear contracts for when to use each.

 - Partner with our largest and most demanding customers on production deployments. Go deep enough to know which step failed and what would fix it.

 - Use the platform as a builder. Stand up agents, wire them into real processes, and use coding agents aggressively to prototype and ship reference implementations. If a point needs a working example, build one.

 - Translate the fast-moving landscape of agent builders, conversational AI, and AI-assisted development into a coherent UiPath point of view and a shipping product.

 - Define the metrics that matter, such as time from idea to published agent, the share of agents that pass review on the first attempt, task success in production, and builder retention. Then prioritize ruthlessly against them.

 - Represent UiPath's low-code agent story to customers, partners, and industry forums.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - 6+ years in technical product management or engineering, with an emphasis on low-code or no-code platforms, builder tools, conversational AI, or applied agentic AI. You have a proven record of shipping products that builders love and rely on.

 - Hands-on experience building low-code platforms, agent builders, or conversational AI products. You've made powerful systems simple without hiding what matters.

 - Deep fluency in agentic AI: models, tool calling, MCP and A2A, coding agents, agent design patterns, memory, guardrails, evals, and observability. You can read an agent trace and see right away what went wrong.

 - A clear view of how deterministic automation and non-deterministic agents should compose, and where each belongs in a real business process.

 - A builder's posture and a bias for action. You use coding agents to test ideas and ship prototypes rather than writing specs and waiting.

 - A first-principles mindset and comfort with ambiguity. You can reach a defensible direction in days, not quarters.

 - Sharp communication: a position doc that inspires bold decisions, a technical explanation a skeptical architect trusts, a demo that closes the room.

 - Comfort working in regulated, on-prem, and hybrid environments.




IDEAL BACKGROUND

 - Built low-code, agent-building, conversational AI, or automation products at a frontier lab, hyperscaler, or automation vendor, or as an early PM at a startup in the space.

 - Has taken a product from 0 to 1 and felt the weight of it. Startup or founding PM experience is strongly preferred.

 - Has a point of view, with receipts, on how non-developers will build agents over the next 24 months.

Maybe you don’t tick all the boxes above—but still think you’d be great for the job? Go ahead, apply anyway. Please. Because we know that experience comes in all shapes and sizes—and passion can’t be learned.

Many of our roles allow for flexibility in when and where work gets done. jobs.title: In-Store Demo Specialist
jobs.description:
🟣 ABOUT AIRGOODS

Airgoods is building the future of food and beverage distribution.

Today, we help thousands of independent grocers and specialty food stores (like Butterfield Market https://www.instagram.com/butterfieldnyc/?hl=en, Happier Grocery https://www.instagram.com/happiergrocery/?hl=en, and Meadow Lane https://www.instagram.com/meadowlanenyc/?hl=en) discover, order and sell gourmet and emerging brands (like Fishwife https://www.instagram.com/fishwife/?hl=en, David https://www.instagram.com/davidprotein/?hl=en, and Sourmilk https://www.sourmilk.com/).

We started in January 2023 and have since raised $7M from top investors like Y Combinator and Initialized Capital. Our office is near Madison Square Park in New York City.




🏗️ ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

Getting a great product onto the shelf is only half the battle. Shoppers have to try it. Airgoods runs in-store demos for emerging food and beverage brands at some of the best specialty grocers in Manhattan and Brooklyn.

As a Demo Specialist, you're the face of the brand for the day. You set up a tasting table, tell shoppers what makes the product special, and turn samples into sales. You choose which demos you take and when, and you earn more the more you sell.



What a demo looks like

 - Arrive at the store and set up the demo table with the materials provided

 - Sample the product, share the brand's story, and help shoppers find something they love

 - Take photos of your table and setup with your smartphone

 - Note what shoppers say: favorite flavors, questions, reactions

 - Break down and send a quick recap (shopper feedback and photos)



How it works

 - You're an independent contractor (1099). We share open demos and you accept the ones that fit your schedule.

 - Demos are mostly on weekends and weekday evenings. Most demos run 3 hours on the floor, plus a short setup and breakdown.

 - There's no minimum and no cap. Many specialists take around 2-3 demos a week. This works best if you can take more than one demo per month.

 - Product information is provided ahead of each demo so you know what you're sampling.




💰 COMPENSATION

 - $75 per 3-hour demo + 20% of the retail price of every unit sold during your demo, based on the store's sales data

 - The better you sell, the more you earn. For example, sell 10 bottles of $30 olive oil during a demo and you earn $75 + $60 commission = $135




🚀 WHO YOU ARE

 - You're comfortable starting conversations with strangers and genuinely enjoy it

 - You get excited about specialty food and beverage, the kind of person who browses the shelves of a trendy gourmet grocer for fun

 - You're reliable: when you accept a demo, you show up on time and ready




🛠️ WHAT YOU BRING

Must haves

 - Availability for at least a few hours on weekends or weekday evenings

 - A smartphone for photos and recaps

 - Ability to get to stores in Manhattan and Brooklyn



Bonus points

 - Prior sales or brand ambassador experience

 - Experience in retail, food service, or hospitality

 - Interest or experience in startups or CPG




🎁 BEYOND THE DEMOS

 - Optional monthly networking events with startup founders, operators, and CPG brand owners

 - Access to startup resources (readings, lectures, and more) if you’re curious about working at a startup

 - Optional 1:1s with the Airgoods founders and team

 - Get to know our team, and be the first to hear when we’re hiring full-time



Don't see a perfect fit?

Reach out anyway. Exceptional talent always has a home at Airgoods.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
Welcome to Planet. We believe in using space to help life on Earth.

Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company all rolled into one.

Customers and users across the globe use Planet's data to develop new technologies, drive revenue, power research, and solve our world’s toughest obstacles.

As we control every component of hardware design, manufacturing, data processing, and software engineering, our office is a truly inspiring mix of experts from a variety of domains.

We have a people-centric approach toward culture and community and we strive to iterate in a way that puts our team members first and prepares our company for growth. Join Planet and be a part of our mission to change the way people see the world.

Planet is a global company with employees working remotely world wide and joining us from offices in San Francisco, Washington DC, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, and The Netherlands.

About the Role:

Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company rolled into one.

In this role, you will join Planet's Direct Access Service Infrastructure team, directly contributing to our next-generation Constellation as a Service platform. This platform represents a major new offering to our customers that goes beyond traditional cloud-based platforms and supports on-premises deployments.

You will be responsible for building, deploying, and operating critical compute software that supports end-to-end imaging operations within customer on-premises and/or cloud environments. You will use your understanding of internal compute requirements as well as customers' environmental-specific constraints to help design, implement, and support a robust system for reproducible deployments across operating environments, to guarantee the reliability, scalability, and availability of our services. To do this, you will partner closely with cross-functional engineering teams to enable and empower the integration of software solutions and the troubleshooting of distributed systems.

This is a full-time, hybrid role which will require you to work from our San Francisco office 3 days per week.

Impact You'll Own:

• Build and deploy computing services and infrastructure in customer environments for a next-generation satellite operations and image processing end-to-end platform

• Operate in a high-impact, tight knit team to architect novel systems for air-gapped deployments at scale

• Clarify and surface requirements from ambiguous use cases defined by cross-functional stakeholders, including internal users and external customers

• Responsible for operations such as deployments, service orchestration, and documentation for cross platform stakeholders

• Scale architecture while ensuring availability of services

• Improve reliability and scalability by resolving edge cases, studying failure modes, and writing tests

• Participate in on-call rotations to ensure operational excellence

What You Bring:

• 4+ years of experience building services that leverage cloud-native infrastructure and tooling

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or similar

• Experience deploying and maintaining bare-metal and cloud kubernetes through tools such as Talos, RKE2, Proxmox, or k3s

• Proficiency with Terraform, Ansible, Helm, Kustomize, and/or similar IaC / GitOps tooling

• Experience with CI/CD tooling, such as Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, Argo CD, or CircleCI

• Experience successfully building, releasing, and supporting highly available, consistently performant services

• Knowledge of hardware and network level implications of on-prem compute

• Experience with platform optimization, particularly resource optimization, management, and cluster tuning in a constrained environment

• Ability to observe and troubleshoot distributed systems with tools such as Alloy, Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry

• Advanced skills in Python, Bash, and other tooling as appropriate to build services and meet product goals

• Excellent communication skills and the ability to work through collaboration with cross-functional engineering teams

• Experience working with Jira for task management and progress tracking

What Makes You Stand Out:

• Experience with CUDA-based GPU programs

• Security expertise in sensitive environments, including implementing zero-trust architectures, hardening Kubernetes clusters, conducting security audits, and deploying workloads in air-gapped environments

jobs.description:
sweetgreen is on a mission to build healthy communities by connecting people to real food. We passionately believe that real food should be convenient and accessible to everyone. Every day in each sweetgreen, team members make food from scratch, using fresh ingredients and produce delivered that morning. And in our local communities, we're committed to leaving people better than we found them. We're in the business of feeding people, and we're out to change what that means.

The Photographer & Content Specialist sits on the creative team and brings our creative vision to life through photo and short-form content across social and brand channels. This is a hands-on, multidisciplinary role for a photographer who is just as comfortable shooting polished hero imagery as they are capturing low-fi, culturally relevant content for our social platforms. You will partner closely with our art director to protect the sweetgreen identity while finding fresh ways to push it forward, and you will help us show up in culture in real time.

You will:

• Shoot food, product, lifestyle, and people photography that brings sweetgreen’s menu, partnerships, and campaigns to life, from hero imagery for launches to everyday brand content

• Concept, shoot, and edit short-form, lo-fi content for social (IG, TikTok, and similar), including lighting, styling, and composition, plus editing, music direction, color, and finishing

• Capture behind-the-scenes content in our restaurants and at events, partnerships, and team moments that show the people and food behind the brand

• Edit, color-correct, and lightly retouch your own work on occasion

• Keep our brand image library organized by tagging, naming, and filing what you shoot so the team can easily find and reuse it

• Steward the sweetgreen brand guidelines and visual systems, ensuring every image and video reflects our identity

• Drive ideation to support overall creative concepts

• Collaborate closely with the art director to find new ways of elevating the sweetgreen identity

Desired traits:

• A visual storyteller who understands brand voice and consistency

• A self-starter with a constant desire to improve and stay innovative in an ever-evolving marketplace

• Strong creative judgment, able to articulate ideas

• Highly collaborative and comfortable partnering with creative leads and cross-functional teams

• Organized and adaptable, able to manage high-volume work without losing quality

• A passion for photography, culture, food, sustainability, products, and trends

Desired experience:

• 5+ years of photography and content creation experience, preferably in-house

• A strong portfolio demonstrating food, product, lifestyle, and people photography

• Proven ability to concept, shoot, and edit short-form, lo-fi content for social (IG, TikTok, and similar)

• Fluency in Lightroom, Photoshop, and video editing software (Premiere or similar)

• Comfort shooting on location in restaurants, at events, and in a studio or kitchen setup

• To live the sweetlife and celebrate your passion + purpose

• A collaborative team of people who live our core values and have your back

• A clear career path with opportunities for development, both personally and professionally

Come join the sweetlife!

Sweetgreen is a national restaurant brand dedicated to building healthier communities by connecting people to real food. jobs.description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

Robinhood is looking for a Director of Corporate Development to help accelerate our roadmap by identifying, vetting, and executing acquisitions, strategic investments, and other transactions. In this role, you will develop a deep understanding of Robinhood's strategic priorities and market landscape, and partner with GMs and senior leadership to identify high-potential opportunities across our existing and future product verticals and geographies. You will help build Robinhood's network of founders, investors, and bankers, and develop relationships that may lead to acquisitions or strategic investments.

You will work closely with deal sponsors and cross-functional leaders across Robinhood on all aspects of M&A, including business case construction, valuation analysis, deal structuring, negotiation, due diligence, execution, and post-close integration. You will present opportunities to company leadership and the Board of Directors, facilitate key decisions, and provide post-acquisition performance updates. The ideal candidate is strategic, relationship-oriented, analytical, and results-oriented, and thrives at a public company that still operates like a startup.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA or New York, NY offices, with in-person attendance expected 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

• Analyze Robinhood's strategic landscape, gather competitive and industry intelligence, and develop the business case and rationale for key M&A opportunities, advocating for them internally.

• Manage transactions end to end, including sourcing, valuation, negotiation, diligence, and closing, and partner with integration teams to deliver a seamless post-close transition.

• Lead deal evaluation meetings and drive decision-making with objectivity, diplomacy, and effectiveness.

• Cultivate relationships with founders, venture capital firms, and investment banks to build a proactive pipeline of future acquisitions and strategic investments.

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Financial Platform
jobs.description:
BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

This role requires being full-time onsite at our Palo Alto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

Why this role exists

Every product BitGo ships eventually becomes a number: a balance, a fee, a statement, a journal entry, a regulatory filing. As a public company and a federally chartered trust bank, we have to prove those numbers are right every period, across many products, legal entities, and jurisdictions.

You will own the product strategy for the financial and accounting platform that makes those numbers right by construction, as we add products, entities, and asset types. You will turn accounting requirements into scalable, auditable, self-service platform capabilities that product, engineering, finance, and compliance can build on.

Digital assets make this harder, and more interesting, than it is at a traditional bank. On chain activity, custody structures, staking, tokenized assets, and settlement each move through our systems differently, and each has to land correctly on the books. The industry is still writing the playbook for much of this. You will help write it.

Level

We are hiring at Senior or Principal level, depending on experience. The core scope is the same at both. At Principal, you have already set platform strategy and standards that multiple teams adopted, and you will own the cross-product standards and the working relationship with finance and audit leadership with more independence from day one.

What you will own

• The financial data and accounting platform roadmap: Define and deliver the shared capabilities that make financial data trustworthy by construction: ledger and sub-ledger integrity, balance and activity reconciliation, fee and revenue calculation, client reporting, and the feeds into the general ledger and the financial close.

• Controls built into the product: Partner with finance, internal audit, and external auditors to turn SOX and internal control requirements into product capabilities instead of manual procedures. When a control needs a build, you own the requirements, the plan, and the timeline, delivered in step with the audit calendar.

• Platform standards across products and entities: Make sure new products, new asset types, new legal entities, and acquisitions plug into the platform instead of creating bespoke accounting workarounds. You set the standards, interfaces, and data contracts that product teams build against.

• Regulatory and audit readiness: Work with compliance, legal, and risk so the platform supports regulatory reporting, books-and-records requirements, and examiner and auditor requests. You run dated plans against external deadlines and flag early when a timeline is at risk.

• Close, reporting, and operational efficiency: Reduce the manual effort, elapsed time, and risk in month-end and quarter-end close. Establish the metrics that show whether the platform is working: reconciliation breaks, close duration, audit adjustments, manual journal volume, and time to onboard a new product.

What success looks like in the first two quarters

• A documented map of how each major product's financial activity reaches the general ledger, with manual steps and gaps identified and prioritized.

• A dated platform roadmap agreed with finance, engineering, and compliance, with external deadlines (audit, regulatory, and reporting) built into the plan.

• One high-impact capability shipped end to end, such as automated reconciliation for a key product, that measurably reduces manual work or control risk.

Who you will partner with

• Finance and accounting leadership own accounting policy and judgment. You translate their requirements into platform capabilities and make the product the system of record.

• Engineering leadership owns architecture, estimates, and delivery. You partner on sequencing, platform design, and tradeoffs without positional authority. Product managers across custody, trading, staking, and financing need the platform to support their products without becoming a bottleneck.

• Compliance, legal, and risk own regulatory judgment. You build the delivery process behind it.

• Internal and external audit rely on you to plan control-related work clearly and deliver it on schedule.

• Commercial and client teams need accurate statements, reporting, and billing that clients can trust.

What we're looking for

• 6+ years of product management experience (typically 9+ for Principal), including 3+ years building or scaling platform products used by multiple internal or external teams. At Principal, you have set platform strategy and standards that other teams adopted.

• An accounting or finance foundation: a CPA or equivalent, an accounting degree, or hands-on experience in financial reporting, audit, controllership, or accounting systems. You can read a trial balance, follow a journal entry through a ledger, and discuss revenue recognition or reconciliation with a controller without a translator.

• Experience building scalable platforms such as ledgers, billing, payments, reporting, or data infrastructure. You think in data models, interfaces, and reuse, and you know when a one-off fix will cost us later.

• Experience in a regulated financial environment. You have worked with auditors, examiners, SOX controls, or control programs, and you understand how public company obligations change how products are built and shipped.

• Technical credibility with engineers. You can follow an architecture discussion, pressure-test an estimate, and write precise requirements for data-heavy systems. Familiarity with SQL and financial data pipelines is a plus.

• Crypto or digital-asset experience is a requirement. If you do not have professional experience, passion projects with breadth and depth across digital assets could be a good fit.

• A writing-first approach: your default artifacts are clear specs, data flow maps, and decision documents.

What will make you fail here

• Building bespoke solutions for each product or blockchain instead of platform capabilities that scale.

• Needing positional authority to get things done. Engineering, finance, and compliance sit on separate reporting lines, and you will coordinate across all three every day. You need to find ways to unblock yourself.

• Optimizing for process over outcomes. We have little patience for ceremony. Here, a control built into the product is an outcome; a new manual review step usually isn't.

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

• Competitive base salary, bonus, and stock options

• 100% company-paid health insurance for employee, partner, and dependents

• Up to 4% 401k company match

• Paid parental leave, Paid vacation

• Free commuter/parking pass

• Free custom lunches and snacks

• Computer equipment and workplace furniture to suit your needs

• Great colleagues and an inspiring environment

Benefits may vary based on location.

Pay Transparency Notice:

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $230,000 and $260,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

Cryptocurrencies are the most disruptive change the financial services industry has seen in years. Join us and you'll be able to look back and say you were part of the team that transformed investing.

jobs.title: Senior Controls Engineer
jobs.description:
Parallel Systems is pioneering autonomous battery-electric rail vehicles designed to transform freight transportation by shifting portions of the $900 billion U.S. trucking industry onto rail. Our innovative technology offers cleaner, safer, and more efficient logistics solutions. Join our dynamic team and help shape a smarter, greener future for global freight.

Senior Controls Engineer

Parallel is seeking a Senior Controls Engineer with deep expertise in control systems development to join our engineering team. This role focuses on modeling, simulating, and designing the software that controls the electrical and mechanical systems on our rail vehicles, and on proving that software out in simulation before it reaches hardware. The ideal candidate has a strong foundation in control systems theory, extensive experience using simulation to develop and verify controllers, and a proven track record of delivering high-quality, real-time control software.

Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain plant models of vehicle dynamics, powertrain, and braking systems, and use them to analyze, simulate, and tune controllers in tools such as MATLAB/Simulink or Python

• Design and implement control algorithms for vehicle systems, validating them in simulation before deployment to embedded targets

• Build and own simulation infrastructure, including model-in-the-loop (MIL), hardware-out-of-the-loop (HOOTL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) environments, used to verify control software ahead of vehicle testing

• Use modeling and simulation to derive sensor and actuator requirements that meet system performance needs

• Correlate simulation results against test and field data to validate and improve model fidelity

• Support system integration and vehicle testing, using simulation to reproduce and debug issues observed on hardware

• Ensure high reliability, safety, and performance in all control software implementations

What Success Looks Like

• In 30 days: You have defined requirements and an architecture for the platooning simulation suite. You have run the existing code and have developed a feature roadmap to achieve the analysis goals required for the project

• In 60 days: You have implemented the simulation MVP and are running real test cases. You have evaluated the baseline assumptions of our platooning model and have identified improvements to the controls stack to achieve better performance.

• In 90 days: You have used the HOOTL simulation to drive performance upgrades in the controls stack and have implemented the onboard features required for real-world testing. You are running a test campaign using real Parallel vehicles to validate the outputs of the model and ground our software stack

Basic Qualification

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Software Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field

• 5+ years of experience developing control software for physical systems, with substantial time spent in modeling and simulation

• Strong understanding of control theory, including PID, state-space, observers, system dynamics, and system identification

• Proficiency in C/C++, Python, or similar languages used in both simulation and embedded systems development

• Proficiency with modeling and simulation tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, Isaac Sim or equivalent Python-based frameworks, and with MIL, SIL, and HIL testing workflows

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience building simulation infrastructure, digital twins, or automated simulation-based regression testing for control software

• Distributed or multi-agent control: string stability, cooperative adaptive cruise control (CACC), or similar.

• State estimation (Kalman filtering, sensor fusion) and system identification from field data.

• Robust control, or hybrid systems that combine continuous dynamics with discrete events like contact and impact.

• NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Omniverse, or similar simulators such as Gazebo, MuJoCo, or Drake.

• Familiarity with embedded platforms (e.g., ARM Cortex, DSPs, RTOS-based systems)

• Exposure to the automotive, aerospace, or robotics industries

• Experience developing with Rust, especially in embedded platforms

• Experience modeling and simulating vehicle dynamics, braking systems, electric powertrains, or sensor fusion

• Prior ownership of a controls project from modeling and simulation through implementation, testing, and deployment

jobs.title: Data Scientist II
jobs.description:
At Public Storage, data science sits right next to the decisions. Prices move every day across thousands of locations, and our models help decide them. As a Data Scientist II, you’ll be the go-to data scientist for one part of the business: customer and revenue, capital allocation (acquisitions, development and finance), or operations. You’ll be part of their planning, shape the questions, and build the models they rely on.

We’re a small, senior team that works like a startup inside an S&P 500 company. Ideas get to production quickly, you own your work, and it shows up in the business rather than in a slide deck.

What you’ll do

• Build and own production models. Pricing and elasticity, promotions, marketing effectiveness, demand forecasting, retention, lifetime value and recommendation. You’ll write production-grade Python and SQL, and use LLMs, embeddings and RAG where they’re the right tool.
• Be the data science partner for your business area. Join their planning, turn ambiguous questions into well-scoped problems, and present results as decisions and dollars, not model metrics.
• Run experiments that change what we do. Design and analyze A/B tests, holdouts and quasi-experiments. Set the success metric before launch and report the honest result after it.
• Build once, reuse everywhere. Work from our shared customer and real estate data and certified metrics, and add reusable models to a shared catalog so the next problem starts faster.
• Grow the team around you. Mentor analysts and junior scientists through code review and pairing, and back up a teammate’s business area when needed.
• Own the full model lifecycle. Versioning, retraining, drift monitoring and documentation, meeting our model governance standards before anything goes live.

What success looks like

• Business partners depend on your models every week.
• Your experiments change what the company does, not just what it knows.
• Junior scientists get better because of your code reviews.

• Bachelor’s degree in a STEM or quantitative field, such as statistics, computer science, economics, engineering or applied mathematics.
• 3+ years in a production data science role, or 2+ years with a Master’s, or 1+ year with a PhD.
• Strong SQL and Python in production settings, not notebooks alone.
• Applied statistics in both frequentist and Bayesian frameworks, plus experimental design and causal inference.
• A track record of shipping models that drove measurable business outcomes.
• Experience with a cloud data platform. Google Cloud and BigQuery preferred; Snowflake, AWS or Azure considered.
• Able to turn an ambiguous business question into a scoped problem, and explain uncertainty and trade-offs to non-technical partners.

Preferred

• 5+ years of production data science in pricing, revenue management, marketing, real estate, retail or consumer analytics.
• The modern ML stack: scikit-learn, XGBoost/LightGBM, PyTorch, PyMC, Prophet, and experiment tracking with MLflow or Vertex AI.
• MLOps experience: model registries, CI/CD, scheduled retraining and monitoring.
• dbt and orchestration tools such as Airflow or Cloud Composer.
• Hands-on experience with LLM applications, vector search, RAG or agentic AI workflows.

Workplace

• One of our values pillars is to work as One Team and we believe that there is no replacement for in-person collaboration but understand the value of some flexibility. Public Storage teammates are expected to work in the office five days each week with the option to take up to three flexible remote days per month.

Public Storage is an equal opportunity employer and embraces diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected status. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Sales Enablement
jobs.description:
ABOUT STUUT

Stuut is the AI coworker that runs order-to-cash for the world’s leading enterprises. Across order management, credit, collections, payments, cash application, disputes and deductions, Stuut does the work end to end and keeps going until the cash hits the bank.


Over 150 companies, spanning the mid-market to the Fortune 50, including Honeywell, ZoomInfo and PerkinElmer, use Stuut to unlock up to 40% more cash flow and cut DSO by 47%. More than $3 billion has moved through the platform to date.


Founded in New York by Tarek Alaruri and Ben Winter, Stuut has raised $93 million from Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, M12, Microsoft’s Venture Fund, and others. Learn more at stuut.ai http://stuut.ai. 




THE ROLE 

Stuut is seeking its first Sales Enablement hire to build the function for our Account Executive and BDR teams. Our sales org is growing quickly and selling a product that rapidly evolves to finance buyers. This role owns how sellers ramp, how they tell the Stuut’s story, and how they get better every quarter.

This is an individual contributor role, reporting to our CRO. It is hands-on: you will set the strategy and also write the onboarding curriculum, record the demo, build the battlecard, and run call reviews. You will partner closely with Sales leadership, Product, Product Marketing, Revenue Operations, and Finance.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

Onboarding and ramp

 - Design and run a repeatable onboarding program for new BDRs, andAEs, with a defined bar for what "ramped" means at each role and clear ramp-time targets

 - Own the first 30/60/90 for every new seller, including product certification, pitch and demo certification, tooling proficiency, and territory readiness

 - Build in feedback loops so every cohort improves the next one

Messaging, pitch, and demo

 - Codify the Stuut pitch into a single, current, opinionated narrative that every seller can deliver the same way

 - Build and maintain the standard demo flow for each product surface and keep it current as the product ships

 - Partner with Product Marketing on positioning, use cases, buyer personas, and vertical narratives

Ongoing enablement and coaching

 - Run a regular enablement cadence (weekly rep-facing sessions, monthly deep dives, quarterly kickoffs) driven by what the field actually needs

 - Build a live call-review and coaching program with Sales leadership, using recorded calls to reinforce what good looks like and surface where reps are getting stuck

 - Own the enablement content library — playbooks, talk tracks, discovery questions, objection handles, competitive battlecards, ROI framing — and keep it usable, current, and findable

Product-to-field translation

 - Sit close to Product to translate each release into "what this means for the field": what to say, who to say it to, when to bring it up, and what proof to lean on

 - Build a launch process that turns product updates into field readiness quickly and consistently

Sales methodology and skill development

 - Partner with Sales leadership to select and operationalize the qualification and deal-management framework that fits Stuut's motion — training, reinforcement, coaching, and inspection

 - Build role-specific skill programs (discovery, multi-threading, negotiation, executive presence, technical selling to CFOs)

Measurement and iteration

 - Define what enablement is accountable for: ramp time to first deal, pitch and demo certification pass rates, win rate on contested deals, content adoption, and manager coaching consistency

 - Report against those metrics and kill programs that do not move them




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 6+ years in sales enablement, sales training, sales operations, or a quota-carrying / sales-adjacent role at a B2B software company, with clear ownership of a program you built end to end

 - A track record of building or scaling enablement from zero or near-zero — you have been the first or second enablement hire before, or you have owned a function that ran like one

 - Strong instincts for sales messaging and translating a complex, fast-moving technical product into a story that sellers can tell and buyers can act on

 - Fluency running coaching and call reviews with sellers and Sales leadership — you can spot what a rep needs from listening to five minutes of a call

 - Ability to work cross-functionally with Sales leadership, Product, Product Marketing, Revenue Operations, and Finance

 - Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

 - Willingness to be in the San Francisco or New York office four days per week




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at a Series A–D company selling a fast-changing product to a mix of technical and business buyers

 - Background enabling direct sales with an enterprise motion

 - Experience selling or enabling into AI, finance, or accountanting

 - Familiarity with modern enablement and revenue tooling (CRM, LMS, conversation intelligence, content management)

 - Previous time as an AE, SDR, or SC before moving into enablement

US Compensation

 - Top-of-market salary and equity package

 - Benefits (for U.S.-based full-time employees)

 - Medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you

 - Equity

 - Flexible PTO

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
Title: Senior Program Manager

Location: South San Francisco

Type: Full-time / On-Site

Ohalo is hiring a Senior Program Manager (PM) to lead strategic programs across the organization. You will run cross-functional programs that span Biotech R&D, engineering, and operations. You will take complex initiatives from concept to delivery.

This is a full-accountability leadership role. You will act as general manager for a set of high-impact programs. You will own outcomes, set strategy, and direct work across technical and business teams.

This role requires strong program management fundamentals and a track record of leading complex, cross-functional initiatives. You should be a strong leader and systems thinker who is motivated to build AI apps and agents that keep work running continuously.

The ideal person thrives in a high-ownership, fast-moving environment and is excited by leading complex, high-stakes initiatives from ambiguity to execution. AI is changing how biological discovery and development get done. We want someone who will lead that change, not wait for it.

Responsibilities:

Program General Management & Accountability

• Own program success for one or more strategic, cross-functional programs.

• Design and implement scalable processes and methods for planning, execution, and tracking.

• Drive alignment with stakeholders and executive leadership. own decisions, escalations, and accountability.

• Own budgeting, forecasting, and analytics of managed programs.

Cross-Functional Execution & Communication

• Build and maintain integrated program plans that connect workstreams across teams. Make dependencies and critical paths explicit, and manage them.

• Define how each program fits together: workstreams, interfaces, handoffs, and validation. Keep teams executing to one integrated schedule.

• Make the call on trade-offs and escalations; drive alignment across scientists, operators, and executive leadership without waiting for consensus.

• Spot bottlenecks early and unblock teams through clear priorities and fast follow-through.

• Translate technical complexity into clear artifacts for audiences ranging from scientists to Ohalo’s board.

• Use AI as a force multiplier that runs program work, continuously (tracking, reporting, follow-ups), not one-off analyses or reports. Hold a high bar for accuracy and traceability.

• Hold the team to the same standard and help each member build AI into how they work.

Qualifications:

• 8+ years of experience leading cross-functional programs in R&D, Engineering, technology, operations, or a related field.

• Strong engineering fundamentals, with experience taking technical work from design through deployment.

• Hands-on with AI and eager to go further: you use AI tools in your daily work and want to build apps and agents that run work continuously, not just one-off analyses or reports.

• Strong systems thinker. Comfortable working across disciplines and turning ambiguity into executable plans.

• Track record of leading cross-functional teams and delivering on timelines and commitments.

• Proven ability to influence without authority and build alignment between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• High-ownership leader who is energized by mission-driven work and follows through.

• First-principles thinker who questions “how it’s always been done” and isn’t afraid to redesign a process.

• A Bachelor’s degree is required, ideally in a technical discipline. An advanced degree is preferred

• Experience in a scientific, technical, or engineering environment is required.

The anticipated base pay range for this role is $180,000 - $220,000 per year for our South San Francisco location. The pay offered to a selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the qualifications of the selected candidate, budget availability, internal equity, geographic location and external market pay for comparable jobs.

About Ohalo:

Ohalo™ aims to accelerate evolution to unlock nature's potential. Founded in 2019, Ohalo develops novel breeding systems and improved plant varieties that help farmers grow more food with fewer natural resources, increasing the yield, resiliency, and genetic diversity of crops to sustainably feed our population. Ohalo's breakthrough technology, Boosted Breeding™, will usher in a new era of improved productivity to radically transform global agriculture. For more information, visit www.ohalo.com.

jobs.title: Agent Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
BUILDING HEALTHCARE THAT REMEMBERS 

Every time you call a doctor's office, the system forgets you the moment you hang up. You wait on hold, explain everything from scratch, get bounced between lines, and hope someone follows up. Everyone has felt this. No one should have to. 

At Assort Health, we're building one continuous conversation for every patient. An AI agent that knows who you are, remembers how you like to be reached, and carries that context from your first symptom to your full recovery. What began as the first voice AI agent to schedule a specialty appointment has become the largest proprietary specialty dataset in healthcare: 285 million patient interactions, 62,000 care protocols, 1.6 million decision pathways. 

We went from 15 people in 2025 and will cross 250 by the end of 2026. Revenue is up 20x in 15 months and we've raised $222 million, including a recent $120 million Series C https://www.assorthealth.com/blog/assort-health-raises-120-million-series-c-to-scale-largest-deployment-of-ai-agents-for-the-patient-journey at a $1.2 billion valuation. We've also been named to the Forbes Cloud 100 and the 2026 Enterprise Tech 30 as the only healthcare AI company on the list!

Healthcare spends $1.1 trillion a year on administration instead of care. If you want to help change that, apply below.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Assort’s Agent Strategy team helps healthcare providers get meaningful results from our AI products. We work with executives, operations teams, and frontline staff to make their jobs easier and improve how patients access care.



You’ll join a growing team that takes the time to understand each customer, solve problems, and help them get lasting value from Assort.




THE ROLE

We’re hiring an Agent Strategy Manager to manage healthcare customer relationships from the time they sign a contract through renewal and growth.



You’ll learn how each customer works, agree on clear goals, and use data and feedback to understand what’s working and what needs to improve. You’ll work with Implementation, Sales, Product, and Engineering to solve problems and keep commitments to customers.



You’ll own your customer relationships and daily priorities, with support from your manager on more difficult situations. You’ll also help improve team processes and share what you learn with colleagues.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build trust with executives, operations leaders, and frontline staff, and stay involved as customers launch, use, and grow with Assort.

 - Review performance data, identify problems, and create practical plans to improve results. Explain the value Assort delivers, such as time saved or better call handling.

 - Make sure questions and requests receive timely responses. Address concerns early and work with your manager on plans to get struggling accounts back on track.

 - Help customers understand the results they’re getting and where other Assort products could help. Work with Sales to support contract renewals and additional purchases.

 - Build your knowledge of Assort’s products, recommend options that fit customer needs, and give Product and Engineering clear feedback.

 - Find ways to reduce repetitive work, improve processes, and make useful changes that can benefit several customers.

 - Document what works, share lessons from your accounts, and guide colleagues on products and tasks you know well.

 - Travel occasionally to customer sites.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 2–5 years of experience working directly with customers in Customer Success, Account Management, Technical Account Management, Implementation, Management Consulting, or a similar role.

 - Experience managing a group of customer accounts, with examples of helping customers use a product successfully, see its value, renew contracts, and grow their relationship.

 - You use data to understand problems, recommend solutions, and check whether those solutions worked.

 - You explain results, recommendations, and next steps in a way that makes sense to both senior leaders and the people using the product.

 - You manage competing priorities, coordinate with other teams, and keep customers updated.

 - You ask thoughtful questions, learn new products, and use feedback to improve your work.

 - You’ve improved a process, tool, document, or customer program and can explain how it helped.

 - You can make progress when the answer isn’t obvious, take responsibility for your work, and ask for help when needed.

 - Interest in or experience helping organizations put AI tools to use.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience at an early-stage startup or a growing software company.

 - Interest in improving healthcare and the patient experience.

 - Experience working with healthcare providers or healthcare technology.

 - Familiarity with electronic health record systems such as Epic, athenahealth, or eClinicalWorks.




BENEFITS & PERKS FOR ASSORTIES

 - 💸 Competitive Compensation – Including salary and employee stock options so you share in our success.

 - 📚 Lifelong Learning – Annual budget for professional development, plus training opportunities to help you grow.

 - 💻 Office Setup Stipend – We’ll outfit your in-office workspace so comfy as it's productive.

 - 🩺 Top-Tier Health Coverage – Medical, dental, and vision insurance, because your health comes first.

 - 🏖 Flexible PTO – We trust you to take the time you need to recharge and come back ready to crush it.

 - 🥗 Meals & Snacks – Lunch, dinner, and snack breaks that fuel great ideas.

 - 💪 Fitness Stipend – Your wellness matters. We reimburse monthly membership costs to support your health.

 - 🚆 Commuter Benefits – We cover eligible transportation costs to make your trip to work easier.

 - 👵 401(k) – Build your retirement savings.
   
   


HOW WE WORK & WHAT WE VALUE

Our team at Assort Health moves fast, stays focused, and is fueled by a desire to serve our customers and patients. Our company values guide how we work—they are present in how we show up, make decisions and work together to move our mission forward. We bring a Day One Drive, relentlessly striving to improve, keep a 5-Star Focus, as our customers are our lifeblood, always Answer the Call, remembering that ownership and accountability are paramount, and show up with One Pulse, because we are one team, with one rhythm and one result. Our team is growing and we are looking for motivated, hardworking, and passionate talent. If you want to make healthcare accessible for everyone, we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Tutor
We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.
Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
Why this role exists
At Tutor, we believe that we must innovate across the entire business to deliver on our mission. This means we’re constantly rethinking how we develop, sell, manufacture, deploy, and support our rapidly-growing fleet. As a member of our technical staff, you’ll rethink how we manufacture robots with process and software.
You will work closely with our manufacturing engineering leadership to determine the process you will codify. They will have opinions, and you must be willing to push back to find the right ideas to build on. You will build the tools with the support of production engineering and a centralized builder cohort, and you are responsible for building tools that get used. The floor will work differently month over month because of what you build, and your success will show up in build quality and punctuality.

jobs.title: Lead, Test & Launch Operations Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

NEUTRON

Neutron is a medium-lift launch vehicle being developed by Rocket Lab, a publicly traded end-to-end space company. The rocket can deliver the mega constellations of tomorrow, enable interplanetary payloads, and support human spaceflight. As a reusable platform, Neutron will deliver a very cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab's proven history with Electron – the second most launched rocket, worldwide, in 2024. If you're interested in joining an incredible team in a fast-paced and rewarding environment, this is your opportunity.

HASTE

HASTE (Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron) is a specialized variant of Rocket Lab's proven Electron launch vehicle, designed to support hypersonic flight testing and research missions. Operating from Rocket Lab's Launch Complex 2 at Wallops Island, Virginia, Electron HASTE provides a unique capability to deliver hypersonic test vehicles to the required flight conditions for cutting-edge aerodynamic and propulsion research. The program represents an exciting evolution of the Electron platform, supporting critical national defense and aerospace research objectives while maintaining Rocket Lab's commitment to rapid, reliable launch operations.

Lead Test & Launch Engineer – Launch Pad

Based out of Rocket Lab’s Launch Complex 3 in Wallops Island, VA, the Lead Test and Launch Operations Engineer are responsible for the end-to-end testing, launch, and mission operations of Electron and Neutron launch vehicles, including the configuration and operation of related facilities and infrastructure. As a senior operational leader, you will oversee teams of engineers, manage operational projects, and ensure the readiness and capability of your discipline area. You will develop training programs, conduct operational readiness reviews, and serve as the primary technical authority for your systems during mission-critical operations. In this role, you will coordinate across disciplines to resolve complex issues, drive process improvements, and ensure operational procedures and infrastructure scale to support an increasing launch cadence. The Lead Test and Launch Operations Engineer balances time between Mission Control operations, team leadership, and strategic planning for future operational capabilities.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:

• Lead and manage a team of Engineers responsible for launch pad ground systems, fluid systems, and infrastructure for Electron and Neutron launch operations

• Work in Mission Control as the console operator for launch pad systems during test campaigns, rehearsals, and launch operations

• Develop and maintain Concept of Operations (CONOPS) for launch pad systems and ground support equipment

• Create and continuously improve test plans, operational procedures, and checklists for ground systems operations

• Design and implement Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs) for ground systems monitoring and control

• Lead operational readiness reviews, training simulations, and mission rehearsals for ground systems operations

• Perform real-time troubleshooting and data analysis during live operations to resolve ground systems anomalies

• Conduct post-test and post-launch data analysis to identify trends, anomalies, and improvement opportunities

• Develop comprehensive training programs and qualification matrices to ensure operators are prepared for console positions

• Lead structured root-cause analysis and corrective action programs for ground systems anomalies

• Drive the development of Neutron ground systems operations procedures and testing campaigns

• Responsible for leading teams of engineers, managing operational projects, and ensuring the overall readiness and capability of their discipline area.

• Develop training programs, conduct operational readiness reviews, and serve as the primary technical authority for their systems during mission-critical operations

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, electrical, chemical engineering, or other technical field

• 5+ years of engineering experience in ground systems, industrial controls, fluid systems, or launch operations

• Proficiency with ground support equipment, industrial control systems (including PLCs and automated sequencing), and launch pad systems

• Experience with cryogenic systems, pressurization systems, propellant handling, and launch vehicle tanking operations

• Experience in high-reliability ground systems design, testing, or operations

• Demonstrated leadership competencies, including change management, conflict resolution, escalation, and effective team management

• Understanding of hazardous operations and safety protocols for ground systems

• Experience developing operational procedures, test plans, and conducting mission simulations

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Experience working in Mission Control or similar operational control environments

• Aviation, aircrew, or flight test experience as an alternative background

• Hands-on experience with launch vehicle ground operations at an active launch site

• Experience leading ground systems testing programs or static test campaigns

• Track record of leading teams

• Solid understanding of fluid systems and high-pressure gas systems

• Experience developing HMIs for operational monitoring and control systems

• Background in real-time data analysis and troubleshooting during live operations

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans, dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, and other discounts and perks.

The expected salary range for the position is displayed in accordance with the state of Virginia’s pay transparency requirements. Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity)

$149,000—$174,000 USD

Base Salary

$107,000—$147,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.
