jobs.title: Research Engineer, Benchmarks & Evaluation
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT RAMP LABS

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Every model decision at Ramp Labs runs through a benchmark. Which model to route to. Whether a post-training run worked. Whether an agent is ready to post a corrective journal entry to a customer's ledger without a human in the loop.

You'll own Ramp's benchmarking effort. You'll turn real finance work (expense policy review, invoice coding, month-end close, spreadsheet Q&A) into benchmarks and RL environments, build the graders, and tell the team what is actually improving.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build benchmarks from real workflows: turn agent traces, customer edge cases and expert labels into versioned benchmark suites for long-horizon agents that run for hours across tools and systems, plus tool use, multi-step reasoning and financial judgment

 - Own the benchmarking effort: decide what we measure, run benchmark suites across models and agent versions, and report results the team makes decisions on

 - Design graders: rubrics, programmatic checks and llm-as-judge, calibrated against human agreement, with a clear view of where each one breaks

 - Close the loop with post-training: turn evals into reward functions and RL environments, and catch reward hacking and contamination before they ship

 - Publish external benchmarks and write-ups on how models perform at real finance work




WHAT YOU NEED

 - Hands-on experience building LLM benchmarks or evals that people used to make real decisions

 - Strong Python and software engineering; your eval code is reproducible and fast

 - Statistical judgment: variance, confidence intervals, sample size, inter-rater agreement, and knowing when a delta is noise

 - Working knowledge of post-training (SFT, RL with verifiable rewards) and how evals feed into it

 - Comfort with SQL and large datasets; you'll work directly from production traces

 - Taste for what is worth measuring




NICE-TO-HAVE

 - Industry experience on an eval, benchmarking or post-training team

 - Built RL environments or verifiers for agentic tasks

 - Published benchmark or evaluation research (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICML, ACL)

 - Built or contributed to eval frameworks (verifiers, lm-evaluation-harness, HELM or similar)

 - Familiarity with accounting, finance or other expert-domain work

 - Public work we can look at: a benchmark, an eval suite, a failure-analysis write-up

jobs.title: Manager, Catholic Sales
jobs.description:
About the Role

The Manager, Catholic Sales is responsible for leading Pushpay’s Catholic sales team and driving consistent new-logo revenue growth, with a primary focus on parish-level sales and supporting diocesan sales efforts alongside the Senior Manager, Business Development.

This hands-on leader directly manages and develops a team of four Account Executives, with dotted-line leadership of 5–6 Sales Development Representatives (SDRs), establishing a high-performance culture built on accountability, coaching, and disciplined sales execution. The role owns the team’s day-to-day operating rhythm, including pipeline management, forecasting, deal progression, territory management, and performance management, within an account-based sales model covering territories across the US.

Working closely with the GM of the Catholic Business Unit, the Senior Manager of Business Development, Revenue Operations, and other cross-functional partners, the Senior Manager translates go-to-market priorities into actionable sales plans and predictable revenue results.

Supervisory Responsibilities

• Recruit, lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Catholic Account Executives, and provide dotted-line direction and coaching to the SDRs supporting the team.

• Establish clear performance expectations, individual goals, and accountability for revenue results.

• Oversee the team’s daily workflow, activity standards, and sales operating cadence.

• Conduct regular one-on-ones, performance reviews, and coaching to improve seller effectiveness.

• Proactively address performance gaps through development plans and performance management, in accordance with company policy.

• Foster a culture of customer focus, ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Named as one of BuiltIn ‘Best Places to Work’ in Seattle, Denver and Dallas for 2025; ranked number 10 by Seattle Business Magazine in the ‘Washington’s 100 Best Companies to Work For’ list in the large companies category for 2024; named as a 2025 'Best Places to Work for Women' by Best Companies Group.

Benefits and Compensation

We have a passion for making all employees feel supported. In addition to having a genuine interest in helping you do your best work and drive your career, we offer:

• 100% employer-paid premiums for Medical HDHP Plan, Dental, and Vision for employee

• 70% employer-paid premiums for Medical PPO Plan for employees, and Medical, Dental, and Vision for dependents

• 401K match

• Hybrid work model - 3 days in the office / 2 days remote each week - COS location only

• Remote - approved remote locations only

• 12 paid Company Holidays

• 2 paid Volunteer Time Off days

• 20 days PTO to start, increases with tenure and seniority.

• Paid parental and adoption leave

• Compensation Range: OTE: $210k-230k (OTE = Base + Commission), depending on location.

Compensation ranges are determined by role and location. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the pay range for the position across all US locations. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

The following states are approved as remote work locations for this position: AR, AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, IA, IL, IN, MD, MI, MN, MO, NC, OH, OK, PA, SC, TN, TX, VA, WA. - All other states are not in consideration for this role at this time.

What You'll Do

Sales Leadership & Revenue Performance

• Own execution of Pushpay’s Catholic sales strategy, with primary accountability for parish-level revenue performance and achievement of the team’s monthly, quarterly, and annual targets. This role carries the team number, not a personal quota.

• Develop growth strategies, tactics, and action plans that expand Pushpay’s Catholic customer base, and translate them into individual goals and clear performance expectations.

• Establish a disciplined sales operating cadence, including pipeline reviews, forecasting, deal inspection, and performance management.

• Drive improvements in pipeline creation, conversion rates, win rates, deal progression, and overall sales productivity.

• Identify performance gaps early, diagnose root causes, and implement measurable improvement plans.

• Support diocesan sales efforts in partnership with the Senior Manager, Business Development, who owns diocesan sales and the Diocesan AE team.

Sales Management & Talent Development

• Provide hands-on coaching to Account Executives across prospecting, discovery, qualification, demonstrations, objection handling, negotiation, and closing.

• Conduct regular deal reviews, call coaching, and opportunity strategy sessions to improve individual and team performance.

• Reinforce consistent application of Pushpay’s sales methodology, qualification standards, and sales processes.

• Partner with Recruiting and Enablement to hire, onboard, and ramp new Account Executives effectively.

• Develop and retain sales talent through ongoing feedback, targeted coaching, and professional development.

• Participate directly in complex or strategic sales opportunities to support deal progression and improve outcomes.

Sales Operations, Forecasting & Territory Management

• Own accurate and timely sales forecasting, maintaining clear visibility into pipeline health, opportunity progression, and performance against plan.

• Establish strong pipeline inspection and Salesforce discipline, ensuring accurate opportunity data, close dates, next steps, and forecast categories.

• Run the parish team’s account-based sales model, including account prioritization and coverage of target parishes. Assist the GM, who owns the territory process, and the Senior Manager, Business Development, in creating and updating US territories.

• Align SDR activity with AE priorities so leads are worked, qualified, and converted against agreed standards.

• Monitor leading performance indicators, including pipeline coverage, sales activity, conversion, and seller productivity.

• Report to leadership on market and account trends, including shifts in parish and diocesan budgets, buying priorities, and the strategic direction of key accounts.

• Partner with Revenue Operations to improve Salesforce reporting, dashboards, and sales processes, identify performance trends, and drive data-informed decisions.

• Provide input on AE compensation plans and quotas through the GM, Catholic Business Unit.

• Evaluate territory coverage, seller capacity, and team effectiveness to improve consistency and predictability of revenue performance.

Go-to-Market & Customer Engagement

• Partner with the GM, Catholic Business Unit, to execute go-to-market priorities and identify opportunities for growth.

• Collaborate with Marketing, Business Development, and SDRs to improve lead generation, conversion, and pipeline development.

• Support Catholic conferences, diocesan events, and strategic customer engagements that generate or advance sales opportunities.

• Maintain a strong understanding of Catholic parish and diocesan structures, buying processes, customer needs, and the competitive landscape.

• Partner with Product, Customer Success, and Enablement to improve sales effectiveness, competitive positioning, and the customer experience.

• Represent the voice of the Catholic sales team, sharing frontline market insights and customer feedback to inform business priorities.

What You'll Bring

Education & Experience

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant professional experience required.

• 7+ years of B2B sales experience, preferably within SaaS or technology, including 4+ years of direct sales management experience.

• Proven track record of achieving revenue targets and developing high-performing Account Executives.

• Strong experience in sales forecasting, pipeline management, territory and account planning, Salesforce (CRM) discipline, and performance analytics.

• Demonstrated ability to coach consultative sales motions involving multiple stakeholders and complex buying decisions.

• Experience selling into churches, faith-based organizations, nonprofits, or the Catholic market strongly preferred.

• Ability to operate in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment with a strong emphasis on accountability and execution.

Key Leadership Attributes

The successful Senior Manager, Catholic Sales will be:

• Results-oriented — Owns revenue outcomes and drives accountability for consistent performance.

• Coaching-focused — Develops sellers through hands-on coaching, feedback, and skill development.

• Operationally disciplined — Establishes predictable sales rhythms, manages territories and pipeline with rigor, and uses data to improve execution.

• Customer-focused — Understands the unique needs and buying dynamics of Catholic parishes and dioceses.

• Hands-on and action-oriented — Moves effectively between coaching, pipeline inspection, and direct deal support.

• Collaborative and adaptable — Works across functions and responds quickly to changing business priorities.

Physical Requirements

• Prolonged periods working at a computer.

• Ability to travel approximately 50% of the time for customer meetings, Catholic conferences, company events, and team development.

Work Environment & Physical Demands:

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer will be required. This role consistently operates standard office equipment such as computers and phones. This is largely a sedentary role but may occasionally require lifting up to 50 pounds, walking, bending, or standing as necessary. This description reflects management's assignment of essential functions, it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned.

If you require a modification to your work equipment or furniture please contact the People Team - peopleteam@pushpay.com

Pushpay is committed to equal opportunity. We value and embrace diversity and inclusion of all Team Members. Pushpay uses E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility. Head to our career page to learn more.

If you have a disability under the Americans with Disabilities Act or similar law, or you require religious accommodation, and you wish to discuss potential accommodations related to applying for employment at Pushpay, please contact peopleteam@pushpay.com.

About Pushpay

Pushpay helps organizations and communities come to gather & stay connected, strengthening community, connection, and belonging through our suite of mobile apps, management software, and giving technology. Our 550 Pushpay teammates support 10,000+ customers as they drive social good, and we’re honored to have processed over $15 billion in charitable giving. We’re growing fast, including some exciting acquisitions in recent years, and we need driven talent. Join Pushpay and grow with us!

Applications will be taken on an ongoing basis.

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist - Central Operations and Telemetry, Full Time, Variable shifts
jobs.description:
• 20 hours per week
• 8 hour variable shifts rotating days and evenings

The Clinical Pharmacist PNE reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Clinical Pharmacist PNE is responsible for identifying, preventing, and/or resolving medication related problems; for providing authoritative  information to other health care professionals, patients, and the public; and for assuring that the informational, clinical, and drug distribution components of pharmacy services function as an integrated system to provide patient centered care to the patients and staff of Northwestern Medicine.

The mission of the Department of Pharmacy is to deliver the safest, highest quality, most effective and efficient patient care while developing the best people, advancing research, and integrating pharmacy services to successfully coordinate care across the Northwestern Medicine enterprise.

The vision of the Department of Pharmacy is to be a recognized as a national leader in advancing the pharmacy enterprise through excellence, innovation, education and research.

Meets the professional exemption under FLSA; but works an irregular schedule.

Responsibilities:

• Interprets medication orders to ensure safety and proper use of medications and is alert to compatibilities, incompatibilities, medication duplication, medication allergies, and potential medication administration errors. Coordinates the solving of medication related problems between pharmacy, nursing, and prescribers, demonstrating initiative and sound judgment.
• Monitors medication therapy for significant drug-drug, drug-diet, or drug-laboratory test interactions. Intervenes in circumstances of significant interactions, therapeutic duplications, and other occasions where pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic expertise is warranted.
• Evaluates and documents that the medication(s) selected are appropriate for achieving the desired therapeutic outcome. Communicates potential problems and likely solutions to the prescriber.
• Acts as a consultant in the areas of pharmacokinetics and adverse reactions to physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals. Participates in all therapeutic drug monitoring or intervention programs; adjusting therapy as indicated by patient condition and laboratory results.
• Processes all medication order information into the Electronic Health Record to ensure accuracy of records regarding past, current and future dispensing and charging.
• Maintains a comprehensive pharmacy patient profile. The profile should include age, maturation, weight, allergies, diagnosis, estimated and actual pharmacokinetic parameters, and pertinent information which may affect medication therapy decisions.
• Oversees the packaging labeling, and distribution of medications for all patients and employees according to established policies, procedures, and guidelines. Monitors the use of scheduled medications on the nursing units and maintains controlled inventories of medication in the dispensing areas.
• Compounds and dispenses pharmaceuticals including sterile products, chemotherapy and parenteral nutrition products.
• Verifies medication orders before delivery to patient care areas and ensures accuracy and completeness. Resolves discrepancies as necessary.
• Reviews all laboratory data for appropriateness of medication use and recommends changes when needed. Including microbial culture and sensitivity data, toxicology, therapeutic drug monitoring, etc.
• Develops and presents orientation, education and training programs for medical, nursing, hospital and pharmacy staff, as well as assisting in the educating of pharmacy students, residents, and fellows.
• Educates patients and their families about specific medications.
• Responds to emergency situations to assist with medication management (e.g. response to cardiac arrests)
• Provides accurate and timely medication information and or teaching to healthcare professionals or patients.
• Maintains the hospital formulary and acts to limit medication usage to formulary items when appropriate
• Documents all clinical activities and interventions performed. Collects data, maintains logs, records and other documentation as required by the department
• Communicates professional knowledge effectively in both oral and written forms to patients and other health professionals.
• Participates in quality improvement and medication use review activities of the department.
• Organizes, prioritizes, and plans workload within given time constraints. Works cooperatively with fellow pharmacists to oversee and direct the activities of the work area, to assign work to technicians, and to assure that the established department objectives are accomplished
• Reviews restocking automated dispensing cabinets (ADC’s) throughout the hospital and resolves any problems.
• Ensures compliance with hazardous waste collection and disposal procedures.
• Maintains proficiency and expertise in area/s of practice through continuous professional development.
• All other job duties as assigned.

Required

• Active Clinical Pharmacist license in the state of Illinois (IDFPR)
• Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy or a Doctor of Pharmacy Degree

Preferred

• Training and knowledge of specialty areas (neonatology, critical care, oncology, etc.)
• Completion of a pharmacy residency program or equivalent hospital pharmacy experience

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

Background Check

Northwestern Medicine conducts a background check that includes criminal history on newly hired team members and, at times, internal transfers. If you are offered a position with us, you will be required to complete an authorization and disclosure form that gives Northwestern Medicine permission to run the background check.  Results are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and we follow all local, state, and federal laws, including the Illinois Health Care Worker Background Check Act.

Artificial Intelligence Disclosure

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used in some portions of the candidate review process for this position, however, all employment decisions will be made by a person.

Benefits

We offer a wide range of benefits that provide employees with tools and resources to improve their physical, emotional, and financial well-being while providing protection for unexpected life events.

Click on or copy and paste URL to your browser to view detailed benefits information https://jobs.nm.org/benefits

Please refer to the Benefits Eligibility by Employment Classification to determine benefits eligibility for job postings.

If sign-on bonus is included in a job posting eligibility is as followed: Internal employees and rehires who left Northwestern Medicine within 1 year are not eligible for the sign-on bonus. Exception: New graduate internal employees seeking their first licensed clinical position as a Registered Nurse at NM may be eligible.

jobs.title: Senior Art Director
jobs.description:
We’re looking for a Senior Art Director with a great eye, sharp conceptual instincts, and a deep foundation in design. At sweetgreen, you’ll take an idea from first thought to a fully realized visual world, one that makes real food feel craveable, current, and unmistakably ours. You’ll shape how the brand looks and feels across our restaurants, our menu launches, our partnerships, and the culture we show up in.

You should be as comfortable developing a campaign concept as you are adjusting type by three points. You care about the big idea and the craft that makes it land.

What you’ll do

• Develop original concepts and visual ideas for brand and campaign work, from seasonal menu launches to chef and brand partnerships

• Translate ideas into ownable visual worlds across film, photography, social, digital, OOH, print, and the restaurant experience itself

• Establish visual direction across typography, composition, color, photography, illustration, and motion, and protect the sweetgreen identity while pushing it forward

• Design and art direct hands-on, from early explorations and moodboards through final execution, building comps, layouts, storyboards, and presentations that bring the thinking to life

• Partner closely with copywriters so concept and visual execution feel inseparable

• Art direct photo and film shoots, working with our in-house Photographer & Content Specialist as well as directors, stylists, and external partners, and make sure the food always looks real, fresh, and appetizing

• Extend campaign ideas into cohesive systems that flex across channels and markets without losing their point of view

• Manage, mentor, and give clear, thoughtful feedback to designers and junior creatives, raising the craft bar across the team

• Present and defend creative thinking clearly to internal teams and senior stakeholders

• Stay close to culture, food, art, design, fashion, photography, film, and emerging visual languages, and bring what you see back to the work

What we’re looking for

• 6-7+ years of art direction and design experience, ideally at a leading creative agency or a highly regarded in-house creative team

• A portfolio that shows exceptional taste, conceptual thinking, and visual craft

• Deep understanding of typography, layout, hierarchy, composition, color, and image-making

• Strong graphic design skills and the ability to execute your own ideas at a high level

• Experience creating integrated campaigns across multiple channels and formats

• Strong understanding of photography and film, with experience directing shoots from concept through post

• Experience leading or mentoring designers or junior creatives

• Advanced proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite and Figma

• An understanding of motion and how visual systems behave beyond static design

• Strong presentation skills and the ability to explain the thinking behind your decisions

• The ability to work independently, self-edit, and push an idea further without constant direction

• A collaborative, low-ego approach and a genuine desire to make the work better

• A passion for food, sustainability, and culture is a plus

The person

You have taste, and you can explain why something works. You’re conceptual, but you’re also a maker. You can see the world of a campaign before it exists, then work through every detail required to make it real. And you make the people around you better.

What you'll get:

• Highly competitive pay + bonus plan

• Three different medical plans to suit your and your family's needs

• Dental and Vision insurance

• Flexible PTO plan

• 401k program

• Employee HSA and FSA

• Complimentary greens

• An opportunity to make a real impact on the people around you, both by growing them and by connecting them to real food

• To live the sweetlife and celebrate your passion + purpose

• A collaborative team of people who live our core values and have your back

• A clear career path with opportunities for development, both personally and professionally

• Free sweetgreen swag

Come join the sweetlife!

About sweetgreen

Sweetgreen is a national restaurant brand dedicated to building healthier communities by connecting people to real food. Since 2007, Sweetgreen has reimagined fast food to be fresh, flavorful, and rooted in relationships with farmers and communities. As we grow, we are committed to developing our people in our restaurants and at our support center, so that everyone can be part of the movement. When you join Sweetgreen, you not only invest in your own future but help create spaces where food, people, and purpose come together

Salary range for this role:

Starting salary range based on experience

$100,000—$119,000 USD

jobs.description:
Position/Job Title: Caregiver (Full Time)

Location: Brandywine Living at Upper Providence

Employment Type: Full-Time (3pm-11pm and 11p-7a)

Pay Range: $20.00 $21.00 per hour

Final compensation will be based on experience and qualifications.

Reports To : The Care Manager will report to the Health and Wellness Director and/or Designee.

FLSA Classification:  This position is classified as non-exempt and is an hourly position.

Job Overview

Assists residents in all aspects of their daily life as indicated in the resident’s care plan, including personal care, food service, housekeeping, laundry, behavior management, socialization, and activities.

Responsibilities and Duties

• Provide resident care to residents that include bathing, dressing, toileting, and feeding, as outlined in their care plan. • Respects the needs of team members and residents by adhering to schedule and documenting attendance properly.

• Maintain the safety, comfort, dignity, and confidentiality of all residents.

• Encourages and escorts (when needed) residents to meals and activities.

• Ensures all assigned residents are clean, neatly dressed, groomed, safe, and fed during assigned shifts.

• Document all services provided in EHR for your assigned residents during your shift.

• Monitors and reports any change of condition in a resident immediately to your supervisor.

• Appropriately utilizes and keeps electronic documentation “devices” safe and secure within the community; efficiently documents care/services provided during the shift.

• Participates in and attends all in-service trainings as scheduled.

• Ensures compliance with all Federal, State, and local regulations, as well as community policies and procedures.

• Provides basic housekeeping and/or laundry services when needed.

• May be asked to obtain weights and vitals of residents and document per RN or designee request (LPN in MA &PA).

• Assist with self-administration of prescribed medication to residents and maintain related medical records, by way of queuing, prompting, and/or reminding; under the supervision of the RN and/or LPN (CT and MA ONLY). Rev. 10.02.26

• Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

• High School Diploma or GED.  At least 1 year resident care experience required.

• CPR Certification  • Certified Nursing Assistant or Certified Home Health Aide or Direct Care Staff Competency exam (PA ONLY).  • Knowledge and experience in working with the elderly population, preferred dementia experience. • Able to speak, read and write in English.

• Able to work weekends & holidays.  Physical Abilities

• While performing the duties of this job, the associate is often required to stand, walk, sit, use fine and gross motor skills, reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, hear, and smell.

• An individual in this position will be required to lift or carry weight in up to 50 lbs. Intermittent

Physical Activity

includes lifting and supporting residents. The associate must use proper body mechanics.

• Ancillary Benefits: Life Insurance/AD&D, Short Term Disability and Long-Term disability
• Basic Life & Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance
• FSA (Commuter/Parking)
• Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

• Paid Time Off (PTO) and Holidays

jobs.title: Seed Production Agronomist
jobs.description:
Supports execution of all phases of seed production for assigned growers, from contracting through delivery, to provide a high-quality, reliable, and timely seed supply to the facility. Operates within an HSE-first culture and contributes to continuous improvement in production quality and field practices.

Accountabilities:

• Support grower recruitment, onboarding, and contract administration under guidance of senior agronomists.
• Conduct regular field scouting and crop monitoring; document observations and report findings to the production lead.
• Assist detasseling, rouging, and pollination-management planning and coordination where applicable.
• Collect accurate field data, including stand counts, disease/pest observations, purity inspections, and yield estimates.
• Support harvest planning and logistics coordination with growers and site personnel.
• Assist parent-seed inventory allocation and variety distribution to seed producers.
• Execute agronomic production plans developed by senior team members and communicate directed adjustments to growers.
• Coordinate with growers on agronomic inputs in line with production specifications.
• Support bin-sampling activities in accordance with QMS requirements and maintain field records compliant with WPS and EPA requirements.
• Assist grower contract execution, field mapping, state seed certification management, and production-system data entry.
• Use agronomic technology to record and track field activity; support continuous improvement and mentor Production Technicians.
• Build AI literacy while applying governance, data protection, quality controls, and human accountability.

• High school diploma or equivalent required; Advanced degree preferred in Agronomy, Crop Science, Plant Science, or related field.
• Less than 3 years of experience in seed production, agronomy, or field crop management.
• Basic corn, soybean, and field-crop production and crop-physiology knowledge.
• Ability to identify common pests, diseases, and nutrient deficiencies.
• Accurate data collection and documentation.
• Grower communication.
• WPS/HSE awareness.
• Precision-agriculture, GPS mapping, and production-data platform proficiency.
• Adaptability to changing field conditions.
• Maintains accurate, timely field documentation while responding effectively to dynamic growing conditions.
• Builds constructive grower relationships and executes direction with disciplined attention to quality, safety, and specifications.
• Develops agronomic judgment and reliable field practices through active coaching and continuous learning.

Physical demands / working conditions:

• Ability to walk seed production fields in varied terrain and all weather conditions, including dusty and hot environments.
• Availability to work up to 7 days per week during planting, detasseling, inspection, and harvest.
• Extensive vehicle travel during peak seasons.
• Field-based work predominates during the growing season.
• Ability to lift up to 70 lbs.

• A culture that celebrates belonging and collaboration, promotes professional development and strives for a work-life balance that supports the team members. Offers flexible work options to support your work and personal needs.
• Full Benefit Package (Medical, Dental & Vision) that starts your first day.
• 401k plan with company match, Profit Sharing & Retirement Savings Contribution.
• Paid Vacation, Paid Holidays, Maternity and Paternity Leave, Education Assistance, Wellness Programs, Corporate Discounts, among other benefits.

jobs.title: Test and Launch Operations Engineer I
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

NEUTRON

Neutron is a medium lift launch vehicle capable of delivering the mega constellations of tomorrow, high assurance payloads, and human spaceflight. As a highly reusable launch platform, Neutron will deliver a highly cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab’s proven execution history with the Electron program. If you’re interested in joining a high performing team, pushing the boundaries with a clean sheet development of re-usable liquid launch vehicle, this is your opportunity!

TEST & LAUNCH OPERATIONS ENGINEER I

Test and Launch Operations Engineers are responsible for taking years of design and manufacturing to flight in the operation of launch vehicles. As a member of Rocket Lab's Test & Launch Operations team, you will be directly responsible for operating the Electron HASTE and Neutron launch vehicles from the control room throughout all phases of integrated systems testing and launch operations. You will execute complex test sequences, monitor real-time avionics data, make critical go/no-go decisions, and command Avionics systems during countdown and flight operations.

This role is within the Avionics discipline, responsible for Avionics Hardware and software, Radio Frequency (RF) systems, Ground Segment, Telemetry, Networking and all Avionics operations that enable launch.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO

• Operate Electron and Neutron Avionics as a launch console operator during tests, rehearsals, and launches.

• Support development, integration, and testing of Avionics systems.

• Lead and execute testing campaigns, including Avionics Integrated Systems testing and readiness checks.

• Manage configuration and verification of Avionics hardware and systems.

• Develop operational procedures, test plans, and emergency response protocols.

• Design and improve HMIs for Avionics systems to enhance operator efficiency.

• Troubleshoot and resolve real-time issues during test and launch operations.

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS TEST & LAUNCH OPERATIONS ENGINEER I

• Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (preferably Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, or Mechatronic Engineering)

• 1+ years of experience in engineering design, test and/or operations, electrical/software engineering

• 2+ years of relevant experience will be considered in lieu of a degree

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE

• 2+ years of experience in engineering design, test, and/or operations

• Background in Avionics equipment design/operations

• Solid understanding and hands-on experience working with Avionics Hardware/Software, RF systems, Ground Segment, Telemetry Tracking and Command

• Good understanding and practical experience conducting real-time hazardous operations with Avionics Systems

• Experience developing operational procedures, test plans, CONOPS documentation, or emergency response procedures

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans, dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, and other discounts and perks.

The expected salary range for the position is displayed in accordance with the state of Virginia’s pay transparency requirements. Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity)

$100,000—$113,000 USD

Base Salary

$76,000—$95,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

jobs.title: Sr. / Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure (Autonomy)
jobs.description:
About the Company

DiDi's autonomous driving unit was established in 2016 with the mission of developing Level 4 autonomous driving (AD) technology to make transportation safer and more efficient. In August 2019, the unit became an independent company, DiDi Autonomous Driving, dedicated to advanced AD R&D, product application, and business expansion. We believe integrating AD technology into a shared-mobility fleet will generate immense social value. By leveraging DiDi's specialized technology, operational expertise, and integrated ecosystem, we are positioned to build and operate a highly efficient, user-oriented autonomous fleet.

About The Role

We are seeking an experienced Sr. Software Engineer / Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure to lead the architecture and evolution of the core platform powering our autonomous driving software stack. In this role, you will define the technical roadmap for our high-performance middleware, custom compiler infrastructure (including ccatch), onboard toolchains, and large-scale simulation frameworks (ezsim and automated crash triage). As a technical leader, you will collaborate closely with Autonomy and Simulation teams to maximize platform stability, enforce systemic engineering standards, and accelerate cross-team developer productivity at scale.

Responsibilities

• Lead the architectural vision, design, and implementation of next-generation, low-latency, high-throughput IPC messaging middleware and runtime execution engines for onboard systems.

• Own end-to-end build infrastructure, toolchains, and compiler execution strategies (including ccatch and distributed build caching) to optimize developer velocity and software deployment pipelines.

• Architect robust, deterministic simulation platforms (ezsim) and build automated post-mortem diagnostic toolchains for rapid simulator crash triaging, core dump analysis, and systemic fault isolation.

• Drive cross-functional performance profiling, memory optimization, and latency reductions across the full autonomous driving software stack on embedded hardware platforms.

• Act as a crucial infrastructure domain expert for onboard teams, guiding software design for maximum efficiency, flexibility, scalability, and reliability across our evolving autonomy stack.

• Continuously elevate internal development tools, diagnostic systems, and engineering workflows to maximize developer velocity while maintaining tight control over system complexity and runtime stability.

• Technical leadership: Mentor engineers, set high engineering standards, lead technical design reviews, and establish foundational architecture guidelines across cross-functional teams.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s or higher degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a closely related technical field.

• 6–10+ years of software engineering experience designing, architecting, and maintaining complex real-time systems, Linux systems infrastructure, or autonomous driving platforms in C++.

• Proven track record of technical leadership, system architecture, and driving complex, multi-team engineering initiatives from inception to production deployment.

• Expert-level understanding of C++, system programming, multi-threading, concurrency models, and low-latency IPC/middleware architectures.

• Deep knowledge of compiler internals (Clang/GCC, LLVM), build systems (Bazel/CMake), and compilation optimization tools (including caching systems like ccatch).

• Proven capability in debugging complex system-level faults, kernel/user-space crashes, memory corruption, and race conditions.

Preferred Qualifications

• Prior experience architecting or extending core simulation execution platforms (ezsim), evaluation frameworks, and automated crash triaging pipelines for robotics or autonomous driving.

• Recognized domain expertise in embedded systems, cross-compilation target setups (e.g., QNX, Linux RT, NVIDIA Orin), and hardware acceleration layer integrations.

• Deep experience in low-level systems profiling (e.g., eBPF, gperf), customized memory allocators, or custom IPC protocol design.

• Demonstrated history of building developer productivity tools, developing quantitative software evaluation metrics, and driving root-cause analysis in complex robotic environments.

The base salary range for this full-time position is $169,783 - $338,694 annually in addition to bonus, equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

jobs.title: Community Lead (6 Month Contract)
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Most AI is frozen in place - it doesn't adapt to the world. We think that's backwards. Our mandate is to build efficient intelligence that evolves in real-time. Our vision is AI systems that are flexible, personalized, and accessible to everyone. We believe efficiency is what makes this possible - it's how we expand access and ensure innovation benefits the many, not the few. We believe in talent density: bringing together the best and most driven individuals to push the boundaries of continual adaptation. We're looking for builders and creative thinkers ready to shape the next era of intelligence.




THE ROLE

Our vision is AI systems that are flexible, adaptable, and accessible to everyone. We believe efficiency is what makes this possible - it's how we expand access and ensure innovation benefits the many, not the few. Part of that commitment is to engage with a wider ecosystem of early adopters, researchers and developers, and make sure we engage deeply with our mission of building progress at the edge of what is possible.

You authentically care about our mission of empowering builders globally to have more control over AI. Your core strength is bringing people together. You craft and organize experiences that allow users to connect with Adaption, our team, and with each other.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Establish our overall strategy for supporting developers, researchers and enterprises who want to have more control over their AI.

 - Build and maintain Adaption's developer community spaces (Discord server, forums) from the ground up, answer questions, capture feedback, and turn it into actionable issues for the team

 - Develop, manage, and run Adaption's ambassador program, from recruiting and onboarding ambassadors to equipping them with the resources, recognition, and support to represent Adaption in their own communities.

 - Organize and lead meetups, hackathons, office hours, and live streams that introduce Adaption to new developer audiences

 - Collaborate with developer groups, universities, accelerators, and open-source communities to co-host and amplify high-quality events

 - Spotlight user projects and design partners (case studies, writeups, guest talks).

 - Build automations and systems that make community operations scale - when you do something twice, you figure out how to do it better the third time

 - Work closely with technical and marketing teams on cross-functional projects and feedback loops

 - Stay connected with community members over time, keeping a mental map of who's doing interesting work, who should meet who, and what people are building




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 2–3 years in a community lead role or start up ops role, with a track record of engaging technical users

 - Strong operations instincts - you've built scalable processes from scratch and driven cross-functional initiatives to completion

 - Strong written communication and experience engaging with communities over socials (Discord, X)

 - Proven experience organizing developer events end-to-end, from small meetups to large-scale hackathons

 - Genuine empathy for developers and curiosity about what they're building - you care about individuals, and about changing the status quo of who can shape AI. Energized by people - social situations charge you up, you're the first to say hello, and you follow up

Above all, we're looking for great teammates who make work feel lighter and aren't afraid to go out on a limb with bold ideas. You don't need to be perfect, but you do need to be adaptable. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check every box.




BENEFITS

 - Flexible work: In-person collaboration in the Bay Area, a distributed global-first team, and team offsites.

 - Adaption Passport: Annual travel stipend to explore a country you've never visited. We're building intelligence that evolves alongside you, so we encourage you to keep expanding your horizons.

 - Lunch Stipend: Weekly meal allowance for take-out or grocery delivery.

 - Well-Being: Comprehensive medical benefits and generous paid time off.

jobs.title: Vice President, Insights & Analytics
jobs.description:
Join our Mission to Protect Humankind!

Vaxcyte is a clinical-stage vaccine innovation company engineering high-fidelity vaccines to protect humankind from the consequences of bacterial diseases, which have serious and costly health consequences when left unchecked. Working to eradicate or treat bacterial infections such as invasive pneumococcal disease, Group A Strep, and Shigella is just the beginning. Our path to success is clear and well-defined, and Vaxcyte is set up to go the distance.

WHAT we do is every bit as important as HOW we do it! Our work together is guided by four enduring core values:

*RETHINK CONVENTION: We bring creative and intellectual diversity to every facet of the work we do in order to innovate and re-innovate the way vaccines are delivered.

*AIM HIGH: We embody our collectively audacious goal to courageously make the most complex biologics ever attempted to protect humankind.

*LEAD WITH HEART: Everyone leads at Vaxcyte with a kindness-first, inclusive approach to collaboration and vigorous debate that advances our business objectives.

*MODEL EXCELLENCE:  The magnitude of our challenge requires our shared commitment to demonstrating integrity, accountability, equality and clarity across communications and decision making.

Summary:

The Vice President, Insights & Analytics (I&A) is a newly created role responsible for building Vaxcyte’s commercial insights, analytics, and forecasting capabilities, beginning with the U.S. adult launch of VAX-31. This leader will oversee the existing Market Research and Competitive Intelligence team while establishing new commercial analytics capabilities, bringing these functions together into an integrated organization that informs strategic and operational decision-making across the Commercial organization.

The VP, I&A will translate market research, customer insights, competitive intelligence, claims data, and commercial performance data into actionable insights that inform strategy, resource allocation, forecasting, and execution. As a trusted advisor to commercial and executive leadership, this role will provide a clear, integrated view of market dynamics, customer needs, competitive developments, and business performance to identify risks and opportunities and support confident, data-driven decisions.

This role sits within the Commercial organization and will partner closely with the Commercial Leadership Team, including the Launch Lead and leaders across Marketing, Sales, Market Access, and Digital Enablement, as well as Finance, Medical Affairs, and Scientific Affairs. The role will own the business questions, analytical priorities, interpretation, and communication of insights, while partnering with Digital Enablement, which owns the systems, platforms, and AI-enabled tools that support data access and analytical capabilities at scale.

Essential Functions:

Insights & Analytics Strategy and Organizational Leadership

• Define and execute the I&A strategy, operating model, and phased capability build to support pre-launch, launch, and commercial growth, including organizational design, talent, budget, and external partnerships.

• Build and lead a high-performing team spanning market research, competitive intelligence, forecasting, and commercial analytics, establishing I&A as a trusted center of excellence and source of actionable insights across the organization.

• Establish data acquisition, governance, and utilization priorities in partnership with Digital Enablement to support integrated, reliable, and timely decision-making.

Market Insights, Competitive Intelligence, and Forecasting

• Lead market research and competitive intelligence to deepen understanding of healthcare professionals, patients, payers, and the evolving competitive landscape, translating findings into implications for positioning, segmentation, targeting, and go-to-market strategy.

• Oversee commercial forecasting, ensuring assumptions are informed by qualitative and quantitative evidence and that key risks, opportunities, and market uncertainties are clearly communicated to leadership.

Commercial Analytics and Performance Management

• Establish the commercial measurement and reporting framework, including performance metrics, dashboards, and executive-level reporting, to monitor launch progress and inform business decisions.

• Deliver actionable analyses and recommendations across sales, marketing, and market access, including account targeting, sales and marketing effectiveness, investment optimization, return on investment, and sales force incentive compensation in partnership with Sales and Finance.

• Leverage advanced and AI-enabled analytics in partnership with Digital Enablement to improve analytical efficiency, generate timely insights, and support continuous optimization of commercial execution.

Cross-Functional Partnership and Executive Advisory

• Partner with commercial leaders to align research, forecasting, and analytics priorities with launch milestones and strategic decisions, ensuring insights are available when needed.

• Collaborate with Market Access, Medical Affairs, Scientific Affairs, and other cross-functional partners to integrate relevant perspectives while maintaining appropriate functional independence and compliance boundaries.

• Serve as a trusted advisor to the Chief Commercial Officer and executive leadership, clearly communicating business implications, surfacing emerging risks and opportunities, and informing commercial strategy and expectations.

Requirements:

• BA/BS degree in a scientific discipline, business, or a quantitative field required. MBA or other advanced degree highly desired.

• Minimum of 15+ years of industry-related experience, with 7+ years in insights, analytics, forecasting, or market research leadership roles within pharmaceutical, biotech, or vaccine organizations, including direct exposure to vaccine product launch.

• Demonstrated experience building an Insights & Analytics function from the ground up, or serving as one of the first I&A hires in a pre-launch or early-launch commercial-stage company.

• Deep understanding of vaccine commercial data and analytics ecosystem, including: Syndicated sales and claims data (e.g., IQVIA, Symphony, Komodo) Primary and secondary market research methodologies (HCP, patient, and payor) Forecasting methodologies for complex biologics and vaccines Competitive intelligence frameworks and tools Commercial analytics and BI platforms (e.g., Tableau, Power BI)

• Working familiarity with AI-enabled analytics tools (predictive modeling, automated insight generation) and the judgment to know when human analysis should lead.

• Experience launching U.S. vaccines and/or specialty biologics (highly preferred).

• Familiarity with GPO, P&T committee, and payor contracting timelines and how they shape forecast assumptions and research sequencing.

• Proven ability to translate complex data into a clear, decision-ready narrative for commercial and executive leadership.

• Ability to travel 20% of the time for commercial and cross-functional team engagements.

• Other combinations of education and/or experience may be considered.

Reports to: Chief Commercial Officer

Location: US - Philadelphia, PA

Work Arrangement (may be adjusted based on business needs, job responsibilities, or changes to company policy):

Hybrid (minimum of 3 days per week onsite)

Compensation:

The compensation package will be competitive and includes comprehensive benefits and an equity component.

Salary Range: $325,000 - $385,000. Salary ranges for non-California locations may vary.

This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.

Equal Opportunity

Please be aware of fraud or scams from individuals, organizations and/or internet sites claiming to represent Vaxcyte in recruitment activities. jobs.title: Global Consular Lead (Global Business Travel Visas)
jobs.description:
ABOUT MANIFEST

Manifest Law is one of the first AI-native corporate immigration firms, and one of the fastest-growing — proof that immigration professionals want to work this way. We handle sophisticated, high-stakes matters for global companies, with technology that removes the busywork rather than replacing the people who do the work.

Manifest was built to offer the best of both worlds: the scale of a larger firm with the quality client service of a boutique. Manifest OS — the technology that powers the firm — carries much of the operational load, so our consular team spends its time where expertise matters most.

We think great business visa and consular work is a craft. Knowing how a particular post actually operates, when an emergency appointment is realistic, and where the line sits between a permissible business meeting and unauthorized work takes years to master, and the people who’ve mastered it deserve a practice built around that expertise. Here, you’ll shape how that knowledge gets captured in our platform, working directly with product and engineering to turn hard-won judgment into workflows that scale.

This is a role for consular leaders who want to build, not just maintain: real ownership of a global practice, the mandate to develop the processes, work the cases, design a partner network, and a front-row seat in defining what modern consular/business travel services can look like.

We’re here to raise the bar, and we’re looking for the leader who will raise it with us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

This role leads and scales Manifest's consular services for business travelers across our global immigration practice. You'll own business visa and travel authorization filings at embassies, consulates, and visa application centers worldwide — and serve as the firm's authoritative voice on post-specific requirements and business visitor rules. As we grow country coverage, service capacity, and our partner network, you'll be the senior leader who makes that expansion happen. You'll also collaborate with our global immigration team on multi-country travel needs tied to market entry and acquisitions.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Manage end-to-end consular filings for business, visitor, and transit visas worldwide

 - Develop filing strategies by nationality, residence, and destination, including emergency processing

 - Advise clients on business visitor permissibility and permitted activities to reduce compliance risk

 - Serve as the escalation point for HR, mobility, and travel management clients on timelines and requirements

 - Hire, train, and manage consular specialists and coordinators; set quality and turnaround standards

 - Build and manage a global network of in-country counsel, visa agents, and couriers

 - Partner with product and engineering to automate consular workflows in Manifest's platform




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Must-haves:

 - 7+ years of consular or business visa experience at a global immigration firm, mobility provider, or in-house team

 - 3+ years leading people or a consular/visa function

 - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical work experience

 - Hands-on knowledge of business visa requirements across Europe/Schengen, UK, Asia-Pacific, Middle East, Latin America, and Africa

 - Experience managing in-country counsel and vendor networks

 - Clear written communication skills for non-expert audiences



Nice-to-haves:

 - Exposure to business travel compliance programs or market entry advisory

 - Experience scaling a global consular or visa services function

 - Background working at an embassy, consulate, or visa application center

 - Additional language proficiency




THIS IS FOR YOU IF...

You want to build and own a global consular practice, not just maintain one. You thrive managing high-volume, deadline-driven work across multiple jurisdictions and time zones. You're energized by combining deep visa expertise with operational and team-building responsibilities.




THIS IS NOT FOR YOU IF...

You prefer a narrowly scoped role without cross-functional or advisory demands. High-volume, time-sensitive caseloads feel draining rather than motivating. You're not ready to hire, develop, and hold a team accountable to clear standards.

jobs.title: Deployment Strategist
jobs.description:
About us

Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence

PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.

Who we are looking for

As a customer-facing Deployment Strategist (internally we call these Delivery Engineers), you are a relationship builder and technical guide who is passionate about growing strategic accounts by transforming AI solutions into lasting customer partnerships. Due to the deep technical nature of the environment we work in, you are someone who can understand advanced engineering concepts across multiple industries and excel at working directly with customers to understand their challenges, ambitions, and evolving needs while serving as their primary point of contact.

We welcome diverse technical backgrounds that bring valuable perspectives to our product. You may come from a Data Science/Machine Learning background with deep understanding of the end-to-end AI/ML product lifecycle, enabling you to explain complex technical concepts to stakeholders and identify new areas of application. Alternatively, you may have an engineering profile bringing domain-specific engineering understanding that helps connect our solutions to real industry challenges. In either case, you bring a unique perspective and you help customers bridge the gap between advanced AI capabilities and practical engineering applications. Note that your current role might not leverage your technical background - for example you might have left the field of engineering but are interesting in returning! You are a keen learner who will become up-to-speed with our core technology stack, cloud/software deployment, and product features, allowing you to support customers with guiding activities and technical requests.

With 4+ years industry experience in a commercial, customer-facing environment, you're ready to take ownership of the complete customer journey, from onboarding and change management to roadmap planning and contract preparation. You excel at strategic planning, time management, and problem-solving, with natural organizational skills that enable you to manage sprint planning, deliverables alignment, and smooth project delivery. Experience in industrial or advanced manufacturing sectors—such as automotive, semiconductors, or materials—is preferred.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll work closely with both customers and our Simulation Engineers, Software Engineers, Machine Learning Engineers and Data Scientists to understand and define the engineering and physics challenges we are build solutions for. You will:

• Build and maintain relationships with users and senior decision-makers at our customers

• Run the account operating rhythm: executive reviews, account reporting, and tracking of delivery progress and value

• Own the customer onboarding journey and drive change management, making sure what we build gets adopted and creates measurable value

• Track adoption and engagement, working side-by-side with customers to collect signal and feedback

• Build AI-enabled tooling to make account operations faster and more scalable

• Support new business development on the account and in adjacent semiconductor opportunities, including identifying problems and stakeholders, preparing proposals, and supporting contracting

• Translate customer industry challenges into product feedback for the product team

Our delivery teams drive innovation to turn AI models into practical solutions - read our blog to learn more about how you’ll contribute to this exciting journey! https://www.physicsx.ai/newsroom/how-delivery-makes-physical-ai-work-in-the-real-world

What we offer

• 5% 401(k) contribution – invest in your future.

• Flexible working – balance your work and life in a way that works for you.

• Hybrid setup – enjoy our Manhattan office while keeping remote flexibility.

jobs.description:
The Clinical Pharmacist PNE reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Clinical Pharmacist PNE is responsible for identifying, preventing, and/or resolving medication related problems; for providing authoritative  information to other health care professionals, patients, and the public; and for assuring that the informational, clinical, and drug distribution components of pharmacy services function as an integrated system to provide patient centered care to the patients and staff of Northwestern Medicine.

The mission of the Department of Pharmacy is to deliver the safest, highest quality, most effective and efficient patient care while developing the best people, advancing research, and integrating pharmacy services to successfully coordinate care across the Northwestern Medicine enterprise.

The vision of the Department of Pharmacy is to be a recognized as a national leader in advancing the pharmacy enterprise through excellence, innovation, education and research.

Meets the professional exemption under FLSA; but works an irregular schedule.

Responsibilities:

• Interprets medication orders to ensure safety and proper use of medications and is alert to compatibilities, incompatibilities, medication duplication, medication allergies, and potential medication administration errors. Coordinates the solving of medication related problems between pharmacy, nursing, and prescribers, demonstrating initiative and sound judgment.
• Monitors medication therapy for significant drug-drug, drug-diet, or drug-laboratory test interactions. Intervenes in circumstances of significant interactions, therapeutic duplications, and other occasions where pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic expertise is warranted.
• Evaluates and documents that the medication(s) selected are appropriate for achieving the desired therapeutic outcome. Communicates potential problems and likely solutions to the prescriber.
• Acts as a consultant in the areas of pharmacokinetics and adverse reactions to physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals. Participates in all therapeutic drug monitoring or intervention programs; adjusting therapy as indicated by patient condition and laboratory results.
• Processes all medication order information into the Electronic Health Record to ensure accuracy of records regarding past, current and future dispensing and charging.
• Maintains a comprehensive pharmacy patient profile. The profile should include age, maturation, weight, allergies, diagnosis, estimated and actual pharmacokinetic parameters, and pertinent information which may affect medication therapy decisions.
• Oversees the packaging labeling, and distribution of medications for all patients and employees according to established policies, procedures, and guidelines. Monitors the use of scheduled medications on the nursing units and maintains controlled inventories of medication in the dispensing areas.
• Compounds and dispenses pharmaceuticals including sterile products, chemotherapy and parenteral nutrition products.
• Verifies medication orders before delivery to patient care areas and ensures accuracy and completeness. Resolves discrepancies as necessary.
• Reviews all laboratory data for appropriateness of medication use and recommends changes when needed. Including microbial culture and sensitivity data, toxicology, therapeutic drug monitoring, etc.
• Develops and presents orientation, education and training programs for medical, nursing, hospital and pharmacy staff, as well as assisting in the educating of pharmacy students, residents, and fellows.
• Educates patients and their families about specific medications.
• Responds to emergency situations to assist with medication management (e.g. response to cardiac arrests)
• Provides accurate and timely medication information and or teaching to healthcare professionals or patients.
• Maintains the hospital formulary and acts to limit medication usage to formulary items when appropriate
• Documents all clinical activities and interventions performed. Collects data, maintains logs, records and other documentation as required by the department
• Communicates professional knowledge effectively in both oral and written forms to patients and other health professionals.
• Participates in quality improvement and medication use review activities of the department.
• Organizes, prioritizes, and plans workload within given time constraints. Works cooperatively with fellow pharmacists to oversee and direct the activities of the work area, to assign work to technicians, and to assure that the established department objectives are accomplished
• Reviews restocking automated dispensing cabinets (ADC’s) throughout the hospital and resolves any problems.
• Ensures compliance with hazardous waste collection and disposal procedures.
• Maintains proficiency and expertise in area/s of practice through continuous professional development.
• All other job duties as assigned.

Required

• Active Clinical Pharmacist license in the state of Illinois (IDFPR)
• Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy or a Doctor of Pharmacy Degree

Preferred

• Training and knowledge of specialty areas (neonatology, critical care, oncology, etc.)
• Completion of a pharmacy residency program or equivalent hospital pharmacy experience

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

• Work within site policies & procedures while performing proceduralized operations safely and efficiently.
• Troubleshoot equipment with assistance and solve problems; provide feedback and corrective actions when processes during the shift do not meet cycle time.
• Operate forklift and perform hand additions to formulation vessels.
• Maintain and improve safety, environmental and housekeeping standards.
• Interpretation of planning documentation, carrying out and recording quality checks.
• Operate various information systems associated with F&P technology.
• Carry out basic maintenance activities on the filling lines and associated plant

• Minimum High school diploma or equivalent.
• Technical background is preferred.

• Demonstrates keen attention to detail in all tasks.
• Embraces continuous learning and quickly applies new knowledge.
• Works effectively in teams to achieve common goals.
• Manages time efficiently to meet production deadlines.
• Prioritizes safety and maintains high quality standards in all operations.
• The role requires a propensity for production activities, with particular dedication to compliance with safety and quality regulations.
• Ability to analyze deviations from the standard is required to be reported to the shift manager. The ability to relate with a positive attitude towards colleagues is fundamental.

What We Offer:

• Full Benefit Package (Medical, Dental & Vision) that starts your first day.

• Paid Vacation, Paid Holidays, Maternity and Paternity Leave, Education Assistance, Wellness Programs, Corporate Discounts, among other benefits.

About Uber Freight & the Role

At Uber Freight, we are transforming the world's supply chains through innovation, reliability, and operational excellence. We are looking for an Associate Manager, Operations to lead the day-to-day execution and performance of our dedicated account operations team at our Center of Excellence in Rogers, Arkansas.

In this role, you will own the tactical playbook, drive continuous improvement, and manage a team of dedicated Logistics Specialists. Success requires strong leadership, problem-solving, self-governance, and a passion for customer relationship management. You will collaborate closely with internal operations teams (including 3PL partners, Accounts Payable, OS&D, and our Dray team), dedicated carrier managers, and key client stakeholders to ensure service excellence and operational efficiency.

This position is hybrid (2 days remote, 3 days in-office) and based in Rogers, Arkansas, with standard business hours (7:30 AM – 4:30/5:00 PM). Please note: During peak surge seasons, higher volumes require longer days and occasional weekend or after-hours support.

What You Will Do

• Lead the daily execution of transportation operations for the dedicated account, running the tactical playbook daily and remaining self-sufficient.

• Ensure key operational activities—including load coverage, 95% on-time service, dray team load building, and delivery updates—are completed accurately and on time.

• Monitor team performance and hold team members accountable for service expectations, operational execution, and company policies.

• Train, coach, and develop your team through regular 1:1s, performance reviews, mentoring, and ongoing feedback while actively encouraging team morale.

• Maintain strong relationships with client stakeholders, dedicated carrier managers, 3PL teams, and internal partners through proactive communication and issue resolution (being an over-communicator).

• Proactively identify, communicate, and resolve issues related to service, process execution, customer satisfaction, and operational performance.

• Review payment processing and collaborate with Accounts Payable and OS&D teams to ensure timely approvals and execution.

• Develop, maintain, and enhance daily/weekly reporting and documentation to ensure operational processes are roadmapped, repeatable, and transparent.

• Strategically identify opportunities to reduce costs and operational waste for the customer.

• Utilize Transportation Management Systems and reporting tools—including all TMS Modules (Execution, Error Correction, Financials, Dock Scheduler), the BNSF website, Retail Link, Excel/Google Sheets, and Tableau—to support daily execution and continuous improvement initiatives.

Basic Qualifications

• High school diploma or equivalent.

• 5+ years of relevant transportation, logistics, or supply chain experience.

• 3+ years of leadership experience.

• Proficiency with Transportation Management Systems (TMS).

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace applications.

• Strong self-motivation with exceptional organization, time management, and self-governance skills.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field.

• Previous experience supporting large-scale CPG manufacturing supply chains.

• Familiarity across major transportation modalities (Intermodal, Truckload, LTL, and Rail), plus Dock Scheduler.

• Working knowledge of specialized reporting and logistics tools

• Demonstrated strengths in analytical problem-solving, process optimization, and customer relationship management.

Benefits & Compensation for U.S. Employees

Employees working more than 30 hours in the US at Uber Freight are eligible for benefits like a company sponsored health plan, dental and vision benefits, 401k match, financial and mental wellness benefits, parental leave, short- and long-term disability coverage, life insurance and more.  US based employees may also be eligible for a performance or sales incentive bonus program, participation in Uber Freight equity awards, and other types of compensation depending upon the role.

About Uber Freight

Uber Freight helps companies move goods more reliably and efficiently. We bring together the technology, people, and transportation capacity they need, using real‑time data from millions of shipments to guide smarter decisions. That helps customers spot issues early, avoid costly surprises, and deliver on time. Uber Freight works with 1 in 3 Fortune 500 shippers across North America and manages over $17B in freight. Learn more at www.uberfreight.com.
