jobs.title: Audio Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT DAVID AI

David AI builds and licenses high-quality voice and audio datasets to the world's leading AI labs. We're a ~50-person Series B team running data collection across ~20 language markets, spanning conversational, expressive/emotional TTS, and transcription data.


The Role

You'll be David AI's in-house audio expert. When a contributor's recordings sound off, a program needs a recording spec, or we're setting up a studio session, you're the person who knows exactly what's wrong and how to fix it. You'll set the audio standards everyone else works from, help contributors and vendors get their setups right, and run the hardware and studio side of our in-person recording work. You'll report to the Head of Operations.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Be the go-to audio authority for Ops, Engineering, and ML, answering the "why does this sound wrong?" questions that nobody else can

 - Define audio quality standards and recording specs (noise floor, clipping, reverb, levels, mic placement, sample rate/format) for each program

 - Help contributors diagnose and fix their home recording setups, including mic choice, placement, gain staging, room treatment, and interface/software settings

 - Write clear setup guides, onboarding checks, and troubleshooting docs that non-experts can follow in any of our ~20 language markets

 - Lead a team and calibrate them to the company's audio standards. Listen to problem batches, identify root causes (environment, hardware, settings, processing), and recommend fixes

 - Define acoustic targets for processed, synthetic, or AI-generated audio, and judge whether output meets them




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Work with ML researchers to identify and define audio events and acoustic quality issues (What counts as “muffled” audio? How do we define “robotic artifacts”?).

 - Turn these definitions into actionable guidelines for our expert audio QAs to label internal audio data.

 - Manage the QA team in a rapid iteration loop of labeling audio samples, getting feedback from ML researchers, and refining the annotation process to deliver high-quality training and eval sets.

 - Conduct quality audits on annotation and post-processing models before they land in production.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 7+ years in audio engineering, recording, or production (studio, broadcast, podcast, post, or voice work)

 - A highly trained ear for subtle differences across voices, mics, rooms, and signal chains

 - Deep hands-on knowledge of mics, interfaces, preamps, acoustics, and room treatment

 - Strong DAW skills and fluency with loudness/metering, EQ, dynamics, noise reduction, and restoration tools (e.g., iZotope RX)

 - Ability to troubleshoot remotely and explain fixes clearly to non-technical people

 - Comfortable in a fast-moving startup: ambiguous problems, shifting priorities, high ownership
   

Nice to have

 - Experience with speech or voice data for AI (TTS, ASR, SFT projects) at a lab or data vendor

 - Experience recording voice actors or directing dialogue sessions

 - Experience supporting remote or distributed recording at scale

 - Scripting basics (Python, ffmpeg, SoX) for batch checks or processing

 - Multilingual

jobs.title: Director Product Management
jobs.description:
ABOUT BRALE

Brale is the infrastructure layer that helps clients launch, manage, and use stablecoins in everyday applications. We support payments, embedded finance, and financial institutions running compliant stablecoin programs. We’ve built the trusted foundation for how businesses move, store, and use stablecoins at scale, and now we’re scaling it.


THE OPPORTUNITY

Brale has established product-market fit. Now we’re turning that foundation into distinct product lines that make stablecoin infrastructure easier for businesses to adopt, use, and scale. You’ll lead product management through this next stage, shaping how our platform brings together stablecoin issuance, money movement, wallets, tokenization, and integrations.

You’ll drive hands-on execution: working directly with customers, building functional prototypes, and partnering closely with Engineering to turn ideas into shipped improvements. Reporting to the CEO, you’ll connect customer needs and company priorities to product decisions that drive adoption, revenue, and operating efficiency.

Alongside that work, you’ll lead and develop a small, high-leverage product team with clear ownership and measurable outcomes. This is an opportunity to shape both the products we build and how we build them.




YOUR MISSION

 - Translate company goals, customer needs, and market opportunities into a strategic roadmap with explicit tradeoffs, clear ownership, and achievable sequencing.

 - Stay close to customers and internal operators, turn ambiguous problems into clear requirements, and carry initiatives through launch, adoption, and iteration.

 - Lead product work on pricing, packaging, and billing in partnership with Finance and commercial teams, connecting the value customers receive to what we sell and reliably bill.

 - Improve the journey from initial interest to live usage across APIs, documentation, onboarding, integrations, and operational handoffs.

 - Establish product measures and reporting that help customers and internal teams understand usage, performance, and outcomes.

 - Partner with Finance, Operations, Compliance, and Engineering to improve reserve-related workflows, reporting, and internal tooling, reducing manual work while preserving controls and reliability.

 - Keep leadership and delivery teams aligned on priorities, dependencies, capacity, and risks. Surface decisions and blockers early through concise written updates.

 - Set clear expectations, coach product managers, and recruit as needed while retaining direct ownership of important initiatives.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (6 MONTHS)

 - A focused roadmap with clear product ownership and explicit tradeoffs.

 - Customer-facing improvements shipping rapidly, with measurable gains in adoption, revenue, or operating efficiency.

 - Priority activation, billing, and operational friction materially reduced.

 - A product team that owns decisions and delivery.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years of product management with hands-on ownership of blockchain, B2B fintech, payments, or money movement infrastructure. You’ve shipped both blockchain and fiat money products and understand their intersecting customer, technical, and regulatory considerations.

 - Comfortable working in code, using APIs, and building functional prototypes to validate ideas. Prior software engineering experience is a strong plus.

 - A track record of turning ambiguous initiatives into shipped products with measurable customer or business impact, delivering small improvements and iterating on customer feedback and usage data.

 - Ability to coach product teammates, establish clear ownership, and improve execution while continuing to own substantive product work yourself.

 - Strong customer discovery and commercial judgment: distinguish individual requests from broader opportunities and connect product decisions to adoption, pricing, revenue, retention, or operating efficiency.

 - Excellent written communication across decision memos, product briefs, requirements, and leadership updates. High agency, intellectual honesty, and a willingness to learn, make decisions with incomplete information, and revise them as evidence changes.

 - Practical AI fluency for research, synthesis, analysis, prototyping, and execution, with sound judgment about verification and sensitive data.

 - Bonus: experience with stablecoin issuance, custody, treasury, or reserve systems.


WAYS OF WORKING

 - Partner directly with the CEO and COO and work closely with Engineering, Design, Finance, Compliance, Operations, and customer-facing teams.

 - We’re an anti-deck culture. Decisions and updates happen in clear written artifacts in Notion, with direct access to leadership and regular in-person offsites.

 - We ship small improvements daily and learn directly from customers. You’ll build to validate ideas, sweat the details of the customer experience, and partner with a CEO who is deeply involved in the product and code.

 - Tools: Notion, Linear, and AI tools used practically to improve speed, quality, and leverage.


WHY BRALE

 - Lead the product management function at a regulated fintech building the infrastructure for how stablecoins actually work.

 - Shape both the customer experience and the operational systems that make programmable money reliable at scale.

 - Work directly with experienced operators in a fast-moving, low-bureaucracy, low-ego remote team.

 - Build a product organization where success is measured by what customers can do and the outcomes we deliver, not the volume of process we create.

jobs.title: Build Your Robotics Career - Explore the Country as a Robotics Field Service Engineer or Technician
jobs.location: Chicago || Bolingbrook, IL, San Francisco || Oakland, CA
jobs.description:
Who we are:

Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.

We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.

Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.

Ready for a new adventure? Build your career at the forefront of robotics and industrial automation while exploring the country! Bring your technical skills, curiosity, and sense of adventure. We'll bring the robots, the challenges, and the opportunity to explore somewhere new.

As Formic's customer base and robot fleet expand nationwide, we're looking for talented, adventurous Robotics Field Service Engineers (FSEs) and Field Service Technicians (FSTs) who are excited to go wherever opportunity takes them. We'll help you relocate to a market where your skills are needed, with the possibility of moving again as our fleet grows and new opportunities emerge. Whether you're an experienced technician ready for bigger challenges or an accomplished engineer looking for your next chapter, you'll work with cutting-edge robotics, solve meaningful technical problems, and help transform manufacturing across America.

Apply today to join our nationwide Field Service talent pipeline and be considered for opportunities as they open across the country. Your next adventure might be somewhere you've never been!

About the team:
The Fleet Operations Team drives uptime and operational performance across Formic’s growing fleet of deployed robotic systems. Working inside live manufacturing environments, the team diagnoses issues, restores production, and continuously improves system reliability at scale. Fleet Operations operates at the intersection of robotics, controls, and real-world factory execution, ensuring Formic’s automation delivers consistent, measurable performance across diverse industrial applications.

About the role:
As a Robotics Field Service Technician, you are a hands-on member of Formic’s Fleet Operations Team. Working closely with Engineering and senior field staff, you will execute preventive maintenance, carry out directed corrective repairs, and represent Formic directly within customer facilities in your assigned region / territory.

This is a hands-on, safety-focused role in uptime-critical environments. Success requires disciplined execution of established procedures, calm work during production interruptions, and clear documentation. Your work directly supports fleet performance, customer satisfaction, and long-term system reliability.

In this role, you will:

• Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on industrial robotic systems and automated manufacturing cells

• Troubleshoot and resolve mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, PLC, and robotic control system issues, independently or with support depending on technical complexity and experience

• Respond to customer service calls, diagnose production interruptions, and restore equipment to reliable operation

• Work hands-on with industrial robots, sensors, motors, drives, conveyors, and other automation equipment

• Diagnose robotic faults, perform system recovery, and support programming, configuration, and controls troubleshooting as appropriate to your expertise

• Monitor fleet performance, identify anomalies, and proactively address reliability concerns

• Investigate recurring failures, participate in root cause analysis, and implement or recommend corrective actions

• Collaborate with Engineering, senior field personnel, and other cross-functional teams to resolve technical challenges and improve system performance

• Document service activity, troubleshooting findings, repairs, and spare parts requirements using maintenance management systems

• Provide technical guidance and hands-on support to customer operators and maintenance personnel

• Build strong, trusted relationships with plant managers, maintenance teams, and customer stakeholders

• Follow rigorous industrial safety standards, including lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that increase equipment uptime, reliability, and service efficiency

• Continue developing your technical expertise across robotics, industrial controls, networking, and automation systems

• Travel throughout your assigned region, and support other markets as needed

What makes you a great fit:

• 2+ years of hands-on experience in industrial maintenance, field service, robotics, or automated manufacturing, with more extensive experience and independent troubleshooting capabilities expected for Field Service Engineer opportunities

• Strong mechanical and electrical aptitude, with practical experience diagnosing and repairing industrial equipment

• Experience troubleshooting electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, PLC, or robotic control systems

• Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical documentation

• Experience performing preventive maintenance, corrective repairs, and structured troubleshooting

• Familiarity with industrial automation components such as sensors, motors, drives, safety circuits, and control systems

• Ability to independently diagnose complex equipment failures and perform root cause analysis for more advanced engineering-level opportunities

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including clear technical documentation and customer interaction

• Commitment to safety, disciplined execution, and working effectively in active manufacturing environments

• Resourcefulness, adaptability, and the ability to work independently while knowing when to collaborate or escalate

• Willingness to relocate anywhere within the United States

• Comfort with regional travel up to 80% and overnight travel up to 50%

• Genuine enthusiasm for learning, exploring new places, and building a long-term career in robotics and automation

Bonus points if you have:

• Hands-on experience with industrial robots from FANUC, KUKA, Yaskawa, ABB, or Universal Robots

• PLC programming or advanced troubleshooting experience, particularly with Allen-Bradley or Siemens

• Experience with industrial networks, HMIs, VFDs, robotic safety systems, or industrial communication protocols

• Familiarity with palletizing, case packing, pick-and-place, machine tending, or conveyor systems

• Experience in food, beverage, packaging, CPG, or other high-speed manufacturing environments

• Experience using CMMS platforms to track maintenance activity, repairs, and equipment history

• Prior customer-facing field service experience

• Spanish language proficiency

• Openness to relocate to future relocations as Formic's fleet and customer base grow

Our Total Rewards:

At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:

• Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors

• Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles

• Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available

• Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most

• Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave

• Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan

• Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup

• Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses

• Paid Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it. 15 days of paid time off, in addition to company holidays

Compensation Philosophy

Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.

This role is paid hourly with a posted range of $25–$32 per hour. Based on the nature of field service work - which consistently runs approximately 50+ hours per week including travel, site activity, and documentation - total annualized earnings typically range from $71,500 - $91,520, depending on experience, hourly rate, and actual hours worked. Overtime is paid in accordance with applicable federal and state law for all hours worked over 40 in a workweek.

Hourly Rate:

$25—$44 USD

What we look for:

We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!

• Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.

• Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.

• Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.

• Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.

jobs.title: Assistant Teacher (Float) (Part-time): Federal Way, WA (limited term through April 2027)
jobs.description:
As a part-time Assistant Teacher (Float) at Bezos Academy (internally titled Assistant Teacher I), you share our passion for early childhood education and commitment to creating nurturing, high-quality learning environments for all children. While exact responsibilities will vary from school to school, you may assist in classrooms, serve and supervise mealtimes, and support the overall operations of the school. Drawing on your organizational skills, professionalism, and commitment to children, you will support high quality Montessori-inspired programs that enable every child to thrive in our growing network of preschools in under-resourced communities.

LOCATION

We are actively hiring for a limited-term, part-time Assistant Teacher (Float) to support our preschool in Federal Way – Lakeland (3600 S 344th Way, Federal Way, WA 98001).

This role is expected to last through April 30, 2027.

SCHEDULES, BENEFITS, AND COMPENSATION

• This is a part-time, non-exempt/hourly position requiring a minimum of 20 hours per week, with occasional opportunities to work additional hours based on school needs.

• This is a limited-term position anticipated through April 30, 2027.

• You will work a four-hour shift, Monday through Friday, totaling 20 hours per week. Specific school schedules are determined by school leaders when considering all staff, classroom, and community needs and are currently set at 11:00am-3:00pm.

• This role includes paid care (sick) time, accrued based on hours worked, and a 401(k) plan with a 4% employer contribution match.

• The full compensation range for this position is $26-$29 per hour. The starting pay for all new employees is $26 per hour.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

• Age 18 with high school diploma or GED

• Ability to pass background checks, clear tuberculosis screenings, and (upon hire) successfully complete trainings required by the state of Washington to supervise children independently

• Ability to independently supervise, communicate effectively with, and care for young children safely, including ability to lift a minimum of 40 lbs

• Access to reliable transportation to and from work and ability to consistently attend work as scheduled to ensure proper staff-to-child classroom ratios and support smooth school operations

• Must have a valid Food Handler’s Permit or be willing to obtain one upon hire

• Ability to complete 20 hours of onboarding by your seventh day of employment

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Prior experience supporting or teaching children ages 3–5 in a Montessori or early childhood classroom setting

• Experience working effectively across lines of difference and fostering an inclusive, welcoming environment for all children and families

• Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to manage daily operational tasks such as classroom setup, safety checks, and basic clerical responsibilities

• Demonstrated reliability and flexibility in supporting school operations, including meal service, playground supervision, assisting with classroom coverage as needed, and lead after-school activities

RESPONSIBILITIES

*NOTE: The combination of responsibilities may vary based on the needs of the school site, students, and prior experiences of the Assistant Teacher.

Instructional

• Serve as a floating assistant teacher, providing support wherever and however the school most needs it each day

• As needed, independently supervise children throughout the day in classrooms and a variety of other situations, including but not limited to arrival/departure, transitions, outside time, rest/nap time, and (if offered) extended hours

• Assist in maintaining accurate child and family records

• Complete Montessori basics training and credentialing/licensing requirements within seven days of hire

Operational

• Support Bezos Academy classrooms by following regulations and guidelines in the day-to-day operation of the classroom and school (e.g. cleaning/preparing materials, meal prep and cleanup, nap time transitions, laundry, bathroom supervision, etc.)

• Support school leadership and teachers to foster a nurturing, safe, and stimulating, non-competitive school environment

• Support children’s increasing independence with daily living skills (i.e., washing hands, using the bathroom, eating meals and snacks, cleaning up, etc.)

• Maintain licensing and credentialing requirements and complete required ongoing professional development trainings in a timely manner

• Attend staff meetings and family events as schedule allows

• Assume postures at low levels (e.g., kneeling, stooping, bending, and sitting on the floor) as needed to communicate effectively with children

• Provide support to nearby Bezos Academy schools, as needed, at the direction of your Head of School or District School Leader

Other

• Attend staff meetings and family events as schedule allows

jobs.title: Director, Business Development - Europe
jobs.location: Arlington, Virginia, United States; United States
jobs.description:
At Zone 5 Technologies, we're redefining what's possible in precision weapons and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS). Our team of engineers and innovators are developing cutting-edge autonomous solutions to deliver affordable and scalable precision weapons, interceptors, and UAS.

We're building the next generation of munitions and unmanned systems for the United States and its allies. If you're driven by hard problems, energized by rapid innovation, and ready to make an impact on defense technology, you belong here.

Zone 5 Technologies is seeking a seasoned Director of Business Development to lead Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and Direct Commercial Sales (DCS) pursuit activities across Europe, with primary emphasis on the RUSTY DAGGER (AGM-188) precision deep strike weapon for allied European air forces and the WHITE SPIKE counter-UAS interceptor and ground and surface-attack missile for North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) eastern-flank and Nordic-Baltic forces, and with PEACEMAKER and ECLIPSE counter-UAS and multi-mission UAS as the broader portfolio. This senior role serves as the Zone 5 Technologies primary interface with U.S. interagency partners, partner-nation Ministries of Defense, armaments agencies, military services, and NATO bodies, driving engagement from initial country contact through to actionable FMS and DCS milestones. Prior military operational experience in strike aviation, air defense, or counter-UAS in the last five years is strongly desired.

The Director will leverage deep expertise in the FMS and DCS processes and an established network across U.S. Department of State (DoS), Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA), the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for War (OUSW(P)), U.S. European Command (EUCOM), the U.S. Mission to NATO, and relevant foreign embassies to open doors, shape requirements, and advance Zone 5 Technologies opportunities toward Letter of Request (LOR) for Pricing and Availability (P&A) and LOR for Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOA). The role requires a working command of the alliance initiatives shaping European long-range strike and counter-UAS procurement, including NATO capability targets, European Sky Shield Initiative (ESSI), and European Union (EU) defense-industrial instruments.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Business Development, the Director is the Zone 5 Technologies executive lead for Europe: the accountable owner of the regional pipeline, country engagement plans, and partner-nation relationships, with direct access to executive leadership and the authority to recommend in-region presence, teaming, and industrial participation strategy. The Director is expected, in short order, to advance RUSTY DAGGER and WHITE SPIKE pursuits toward accepted LORs for LOA and signed DCS contracts with European partner nations and to build a qualified pipeline across the priority countries.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

FMS and DCS Business Development and Pipeline

• Identify, qualify, and develop FMS and DCS opportunities for RUSTY DAGGER, WHITE SPIKE, PEACEMAKER, and ECLIPSE across Poland, Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Italy, and Greece, or other nations as required.

• Build and sustain a robust opportunity pipeline from initial country engagement through LOR for P&A and LOR for LOA, coordinating with Zone 5 Technologies portfolio program leadership and marketing throughout, and maintaining probability of win (Pwin) and milestone discipline in the enterprise customer relationship management (CRM) system.

• Develop tailored country-level engagement plans that align Zone 5 Technologies capabilities with identified requirements, partner-nation budget cycles, and U.S. security cooperation priorities.

• Represent Zone 5 Technologies at key industry events, defense exhibitions, and bilateral forums relevant to security cooperation markets in Europe, including DSEI, Eurosatory, MSPO, ILA Berlin, the Paris Air Show, and NATO industry forums.

Partner-Nation Stakeholder Engagement

• Establish and sustain senior-level relationships with partner-nation Ministries of Defence, armaments and procurement agencies, military service headquarters, and, where required, Ministries of Commerce and Finance.

• Engage foreign embassies and defense attachés assigned to the United States, and the U.S. corollaries inside partner nations, to build awareness of Zone 5 Technologies capabilities and facilitate early case development.

• Guide sovereign stakeholders through the FMS and DCS processes from requirements identification through case initiation, acting as a trusted advisor on U.S. government procedures, timelines, and Technical Assistance Agreement (TAA), Manufacturing License Agreement (MLA), and export license sequencing.

U.S. Interagency Engagement and Advocacy

• Serve as the Zone 5 Technologies primary advocate within the U.S. interagency, with particular focus on the DoS Bureau of Political-Military Affairs and Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs, DSCA, and OUSW(P) International Security Affairs (ISA) for Europe and NATO.

• Build and maintain working-level and senior relationships with Country Directors, Regional Affairs Officers, EUCOM J5, and the in-country Offices of Defense Cooperation (ODCs) and Security Cooperation Organizations (SCOs) to support responsive case processing.

• Engage the U.S. Mission to NATO, NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA), and NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) on multinational procurement and framework opportunities for RUSTY DAGGER and WHITE SPIKE.

• Support Ukraine-related pursuits through Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative (USAI), Presidential Drawdown Authority (PDA), and coalition mechanisms as directed by executive leadership.

• Track and interpret evolving security cooperation policy, Congressional notifications, Third Party Transfer and re-export decisions, end-use monitoring requirements, and European defense-industrial policy, including the European Defence Fund (EDF), Security Action for Europe (SAFE), and ESSI, that may affect FMS and DCS timelines or case viability.

Market Intelligence and Strategic Planning

• Provide leadership with timely intelligence on partner-nation defense budgets, procurement priorities, political developments, alliance initiatives, and competitor activity across Europe.

• Contribute to Zone 5 Technologies long-range strategic planning by identifying emerging requirements, shifts in security cooperation policy, and new market entry opportunities in Europe, including recommendations on in-region presence, teaming, and industrial participation.

• Monitor legislative and regulatory developments, including Arms Export Control Act (AECA) Section 36(b) notifications and Congressional holds, that may affect FMS and DCS case progress.

Internal Coordination

• Partner with capture, proposal, and program teams to develop FMS- and DCS-compliant offerings and technically credible solutions tailored to partner-nation requirements.

• Coordinate with contracts, pricing, legal, and trade compliance teams to ensure positions are consistent with FMS regulations, International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Export Administration Regulations (EAR), offset and industrial participation obligations, and partner-nation procurement regulations.

• Report regularly to executive leadership on pipeline status, country engagement progress, decisions required, and interagency relationship health.

Export Control and Compliance

• Conduct all partner-nation and foreign-national engagement in strict compliance with ITAR (22 CFR Parts 120 through 130), EAR, and the AECA, including obtaining Directorate of Defense Trade Controls (DDTC) marketing and technical data authorizations before disclosure, adhering to approved TAA and MLA scopes, and reporting fees, commissions, and political contributions under ITAR Part 130.

• Comply with the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions, anti-boycott regulations, and Zone 5 Technologies policies on gifts, hospitality, agents, and consultants; conduct due diligence on in-country representatives and teaming partners.

• Protect classified, controlled unclassified, and proprietary information in accordance with National Disclosure Policy, program security guidance, and clearance obligations, including foreign contact and foreign travel reporting; maintain a clean record of export compliance across all pursuits.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in International Relations, Political Science, Business, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree strongly preferred.

• 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in defense business development, security cooperation, or government service directly supporting FMS or DCS, including at least one director-level or equivalent leadership role.

• Demonstrable experience with and network within partner nations – not just with U.S. agencies or commands.

• Demonstrated expertise across the FMS life cycle (case initiation, P&A, LOA development, and case execution) and the DCS licensing process.

• Established, verifiable relationships with DoS, DSCA, and OUSW(P) personnel at working and senior levels.

• Proven ability to engage and build trust with senior officials in European Ministries of Defence, armaments agencies, and national air force, air defense, and strike commands.

• Working knowledge of NATO capability development, the NATO Defence Planning Process (NDPP), ESSI participation, and allied air force weapons integration and certification roadmaps.

• Experience operating in or alongside foreign embassies, with U.S. or foreign defense attachés, and with in-country SCOs.

• Exceptional writing skills: demonstrated ability to produce clear, precise, and persuasive technical prose, including proposal volumes, white papers, capability statements, and correspondence for general officer, flag officer, and Senior Executive Service (SES) audiences, with minimal editing. Writing samples will be requested.

• Demonstrated ability to work across the priority countries for this role (Poland, Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Italy, and Greece), with the understanding that country prioritization may be adjusted based on evolving security cooperation policy, country team guidance, and emerging opportunities, and that the Director must maintain engagement awareness across all of them.

• Working knowledge of and demonstrated adherence to ITAR, EAR, AECA, FCPA, and OFAC requirements and foreign disclosure procedures in prior international defense roles; no history of export compliance violations.

• Active U.S. Secret clearance required; U.S. citizenship required for clearance eligibility and for access to ITAR-controlled technical data.

• Ability to travel 25 to 50 percent, primarily international with some domestic travel; valid U.S. passport required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Prior U.S. military (uniformed or civilian), Foreign Area Officer (Europe and Eurasia), DoS Foreign Service, or DSCA service in roles directly supporting European security cooperation or FMS case management.

• Prior assignment on a NATO staff, at EUCOM, or in an in-country ODC or SCO.

• Professional proficiency in one or more European languages, including German, Polish, French, Dutch, Danish, Norwegian, Swedish, Finnish, Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Romanian, Italian, or Greek, and cultural familiarity with the region.

• Prior experience living or working abroad in Europe, including in-country military assignments, embassy, ODC, or SCO tours, NATO staff duty, or industry postings.

• Existing relationships with the Polish Armament Agency, German Federal Office of Bundeswehr Equipment, Information Technology and In-Service Support (BAAINBw), UK Ministry of Defence Defence Equipment and Support (DE&S), Netherlands Defence Materiel and IT Command (COMMIT), the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV), the Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA), the Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organisation (DALO), or the Finnish Defence Forces Logistics Command.

• Experience with industrial participation, offset, and co-production arrangements in European procurements.

• Prior operational military experience employing or defending against precision strike weapons, UAS, or counter-UAS systems is strongly desired in addition to the security cooperation background described above.

• Direct experience managing or supporting high-value FMS cases (greater than $100M) from P&A through LOA signature.

• Familiarity with U.S. arms transfer policy, including the Conventional Arms Transfer (CAT) policy, AECA Section 3, and related Security Assistance Management Manual (SAMM) provisions.

• Experience with DCS structures complementary to FMS programs, including hybrid case structures.

CORE COMPETENCIES

• Strategic relationship management: cultivates and sustains influence at senior government and military levels across both U.S. and partner nations.

• FMS and DCS process expertise: thorough command of the security cooperation life cycle from requirements generation through case closure.

• Political acumen: navigates complex U.S. interagency dynamics, alliance politics, and partner-nation sensitivities with skill and discretion.

• Executive communication: synthesizes complex security cooperation issues for senior internal and external audiences, in writing and in person.

• Exceptional writing: produces clear, precise country plans, pursuit summaries, and executive correspondence with minimal editing.

• Initiative and autonomy: self-directed, capable of managing a complex multi-country portfolio with limited day-to-day oversight.

• Integrity and discretion: operates with the highest ethical standards in a sensitive, export-controlled, government-adjacent environment.

This role is eligible for performance bonuses in addition to the base salary.

Pay range for this role (base salary)

$138,000 — $178,000 USD

Pay range with eligible performance bonuses

$241,500 – $311,500 USDUSD with eligible performance bonuses. Bonus components are variable and not guaranteed.

What's in it for you:

Benefits:

• Competitive total compensation package

• Comprehensive benefit package options include medical, dental, vision, life, and more.

Why Join Zone 5 Technologies?

• Innovative Environment: Work on cutting-edge technology that is shaping the future of defense and aerospace.

• Collaborative Culture: Join a team of passionate professionals dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

• Career Growth: Opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

If you are passionate about unmanned aircraft technology and want to be a part of a dynamic and growing company, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and join the Zone 5 Technologies team!

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Ability to use measuring instruments of all types

• Experience working in cutting or machining operations

• Experience in a high-mix, low-volume (job shop) manufacturing environment

jobs.title: Régisseur - ECHO | Stage Manager - ECHO
jobs.description:
Régisseur  - Spectacles de tournées
Soutien artistoque

* Il s’agit d’un poste à temps plein impliquant des tournées internationales. La personne retenue travaillera et voyagera dans plusieurs pays au sein d’une compagnie de tournée internationale où l’anglais est la langue de travail de la production — une maîtrise parfaite de l’anglais est donc requise pour exercer les fonctions liées à ce poste.*
 
Nous recherchons un régisseur compétent et motivé pour rejoindre l'équipe de régie de l'un des spectacles en tournée du Cirque du Soleil. Sous la responsabilité du directeur artistique et sous la supervision du régisseur général (GSM), ce poste consiste à soutenir les opérations artistiques quotidiennes du spectacle, en garantissant les plus hauts standards de continuité, de qualité et d'intégrité tout au long des répétitions, des représentations et des sessions de formation.
Le régisseur joue un rôle essentiel tant sur le devant de la scène qu’en coulisses, en soutenant les artistes, en coordonnant la communication entre les départements et en assurant le bon déroulement du spectacle dans un environnement de tournée internationale au rythme effréné.
 
Le régisseur aura l'occasion de :
Régie et gestion des entrées en scène
Gérer les entrées en scène lors des représentations et des répétitions selon les instructions, en veillant à la précision des signaux techniques et artistiques.
Gérer les déplacements en coulisses pendant les spectacles, en aidant les artistes lors des changements rapides de costumes, des signaux et des transitions.
Appliquer et superviser les protocoles d'urgence tant sur scène qu'en coulisses.
Participer aux enregistrements audio et vidéo des représentations, des séances d'entraînement et des répétitions, selon les besoins.
Soutien artistique
Apporter un soutien quotidien aux artistes, au directeur artistique et à l'équipe artistique.
Gérer la programmation des spectacles en collaboration avec les équipes de coaching et de médecine du spectacle (PMed), en veillant à communiquer en temps utile les changements aux services techniques et aux artistes.
Soutenir l'intégration et la réintégration des artistes dans le spectacle.
Tenir à jour la documentation relative aux artistes dans Aurora et gérer les registres de présence à des fins de paie et de planification.
Contribuer à garantir la propreté et la disponibilité des loges et des coulisses en coordination avec les équipes de costumes, de PMed, techniques et de site.
Coordination et documentation
Élaborer, tenir à jour et mettre à jour la documentation relative à la régie de scène, notamment les fiches de repères, les calendriers de répétition et les rapports de représentation.
Coordonner les ressources artistiques et techniques pour les répétitions, les sessions de formation et les représentations.
Consigner et communiquer les modifications apportées aux numéros, aux artistes ou aux programmations, en veillant à l'exactitude des registres et au respect des procédures internes.
Organiser et archiver les supports vidéo et audio afin de répondre aux besoins en matière de formation, de retour d'expérience et de création.
Tournées et collaboration
Participer aux réunions artistiques et de production.
Participer aux opérations de montage, de démontage et de transfert d’une ville à l’autre, y compris l’emballage et le déballage des caisses de transport et la préparation du matériel pour l’expédition.
Favoriser un environnement de travail collaboratif, respectueux et sécuritaire, conforme aux valeurs du Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group.
Accomplir toute autre tâche connexe assignée par le régisseur général ou le directeur artistique.
 
Le candidat idéal devra posséder les qualifications suivantes :
Obligatoire : être disponible pour effectuer des tournées internationales à temps plein et travailler à l'étranger.
Diplôme universitaire en théâtre, en régie de scène ou dans un domaine connexe ; ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
Au moins 4 ans d'expérience professionnelle en régie de scène sur des productions de moyenne à grande envergure.
Expérience dans la gestion de spectacles complexes, y compris des acrobaties aériennes, tant en répétition qu'en représentation.
Solides compétences en organisation, en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, y compris une sensibilité interculturelle.
Maîtrise de la suite Microsoft Office ; la connaissance d'Aurora ou d'autres logiciels de régie est un atout.
De solides compétences en communication en anglais, à l'oral comme à l'écrit, sont indispensables ; la maîtrise d'une ou plusieurs autres langues, à l'oral et/ou à l'écrit, est un atout.
Capacité à accomplir les tâches essentielles du poste, notamment : s'accroupir, s'agenouiller, rester debout, soulever des charges, parfois pendant de longues périodes. Des aménagements raisonnables peuvent être mis en place pour permettre aux personnes en situation de handicap d'accomplir les tâches essentielles.
 
Le Groupe Cirque du Soleil s’engage à créer et maintenir un milieu de travail accessible et inclusif. Fièrement ambassadeur de l’égalité en emploi, Le Groupe Cirque du Soleil s’est engagé à enrayer la discrimination fondée sur l’âge, la couleur de la peau, les origines, la religion, le sexe, l’orientation sexuelle et toute autre caractéristique. La rédaction neutre et inclusive est dorénavant privilégiée pour tous les nouveaux affichages de postes.

jobs.title: Sr. Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Applications
jobs.description:
Senior Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Applications

Enterprise Platform Group · Commercialization (Quote-to-Cash) · Mountain View, CA

As a Senior Staff Software Engineer on the Agentic Applications team, you will be the hands-on technical lead for how Databricks quotes, orders, bills and recognizes revenue. Your core function is to build bespoke first-party, agents-first applications built on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. You will own the technical architecture end to end, from quote to cash. You will design agents that work reliably inside revenue-critical workflows, set the engineering standards the team builds on, and make sure every agent-assisted decision can be observed, audited and trusted by Finance, Deal Desk and Sales.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role, not a people-management role. You will write code, review designs, and be the most senior technical voice in a domain that touches every dollar Databricks books.

The impact you'll have

• Own the agentic architecture for Quote-to-Cash. Define and lead the target technical architecture across Configure-Price-Quote, deal management, ordering, subscriptions, investments, billing and revenue recognition. Drive the move from vendor-configured workflows to first-party, AI-native applications built on Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Unity Catalog and Mosaic AI.

• Build production agents that sellers and Deal Desk trust. Design and ship LLM-powered agents for deal guidance, quote generation and summarization, multi-option proposals, approval insights, and pricing and discount recommendations. Work directly with sales, Deal Desk and Finance to define what "good" looks like for each workflow.

• Make agent reliability a core system property. Own the eval and quality system for this domain: per-workflow quality criteria, offline eval suites, LLM-as-judge and human-labeled benchmarks, behavioral regression testing in CI/CD, online tracing, and feedback loops that improve agents based on what users approve, edit and reject.

• Design human-in-the-loop controls for revenue-critical decisions. Build the separation between what an agent proposes and what gets committed, plus diff-based review, approval routing, audit logging, and policy guardrails. Together these decide when an agent can act on its own and when a person has to approve, especially for pricing, discounting, contract terms and order creation.

• Treat systems of record as agent tools. Architect tool-calling and MCP-style interfaces that give agents governed, run-time access to pricing, product catalog, order, contract, subscription and billing data. Follow single-source-of-truth principles across CRM, ERP and billing systems.

• Protect financial integrity at scale. Make sure agent-assisted quoting and ordering produce accurate, compliance-grade outputs downstream: order validation, billing, invoicing and revenue recognition, where errors directly affect financial reporting.

• Lead the migration path. Act as the bridge between today's production quoting platform and the target agentic architecture. Sequence the migration so the business keeps scaling without disruption, and decide what to retire, rebuild or wrap.

• Raise the engineering bar. Lead architecture reviews, establish design patterns for agents (orchestration, memory, retrieval, tool use, multi-agent coordination), and mentor senior and mid-level engineers on production-grade agentic engineering.

• Earn cross-functional credibility. Partner with Finance, Deal Desk, Sales Ops, Legal and the broader Platform engineering org. Turn complex commercial processes into clear technical roadmaps and measurable business outcomes.

What we look for

• 12+ years of software engineering experience, with a clear track record of technical leadership and ownership of large-scale production systems.

• 3+ years of hands-on experience building and running LLM-powered or agentic applications in production, such as agents, RAG pipelines, tool use, multi-agent orchestration (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, DSPy or equivalent), and evaluation frameworks for generative outputs.

• Strong backend and distributed-systems skills: API and service design, data modeling, idempotency, consistency and transactional integrity, and observability.

• Proven experience designing human-in-the-loop systems: approval workflows, review interfaces, audit trails, and guardrails for probabilistic systems operating in regulated or high-stakes domains.

• Experience leading technical architecture for complex business domains, ideally Quote-to-Cash, Order-to-Revenue, billing, pricing or other revenue-critical enterprise systems.

• Full-stack fluency. You are comfortable across modern web frameworks (React/TypeScript), backend services (Python, Java, Scala or Go), and data platforms.

• Ability to work directly with non-engineering stakeholders and turn ambiguous business workflows into clear agent and system architecture.

• Experience mentoring engineers and improving technical execution across a team, without relying on positional authority.

Nice to have

• Domain experience with CPQ, deal management, subscription management, or revenue recognition in a high-growth SaaS or consumption-based business.

• Experience building first-party applications on top of, or as replacements for, enterprise SaaS platforms (e.g., Salesforce CPQ/Revenue Cloud, NetSuite, Zuora). Platform-specific configuration expertise is a plus but not a requirement.

• Experience with the Databricks platform (Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Unity Catalog, Mosaic AI Agent Framework, MLflow tracing and evaluation).

jobs.title: Senior Research Associate, Biophysics, Mechanism of Action
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

As a key member of our dynamic Mechanism of Action team within Discovery Biology under the Biomedical Discovery Research (BDR) department, you will have responsibilities including, but not limited to:

• Perform label-free biophysical assays (BLI, SPR) to inform the mode of action of small molecule and tri-complex inhibitors.

• Assist in the development and troubleshooting of SPR methods for novel applications.

• Assist in the transfer of established methods for routine screening.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

This role is responsible for the design, build, and activation of infrastructure, facilities improvements and large capital projects. This includes owning tasks/projects from start to finish, with the goal of making the SpaceX campus a world-class facility that can support the mission of enabling life beyond Earth. This position is based in McGregor, TX area.

• Keep accurate records of daily logs, progress reports, and financial reports

jobs.title: 11th Grade Program Manager
jobs.description:
Title: Program Manager, 11th Grade

Department: SEO High School Scholars, San Francisco

Report to: Assistant Director, Programs

Compensation: $70,304 - $73,000

FLSA: Exempt

Employee Type: Full-Time, Regular

Location: San Francisco, CA

Work Arrangement: Hybrid - 3 days/week in the SEO office at Three Embarcadero Center Promenade Level, Suite P-1 San Francisco, CA 94111

Location/Hours:

• The typical weekly schedule is as follows: Fall Term: Tuesday through Saturday (3x a month); Monday through Friday (1x month). Spring Term: Tuesday through Saturday (3x a month); Monday through Friday (1x month). Summer Term: Monday through Friday.

• In-person attendance is required for all Saturday programming dates and four days a week during the Summer Term.

• Work requires local travel beyond the office for Saturday programming at the following location (subject to change): UC Law San Francisco, 200 McAllister St, San Francisco, CA 94102

ABOUT SEO

We Propel Human Potential. SEO is an educational non-profit focused on improving outcomes for students that come from underserved and historically underrepresented backgrounds. For over 50 years, SEO has been an innovator in education, mentorship, and creating educational programs and opportunities that maximize the full potential of our students. We are on a mission to create an ecosystem of excellence for the students we serve!

SEO Scholars provides motivated, low income public high school students with a rigorous out-of-school supplemental academic curriculum, college guidance and the leadership development necessary to gain admission to, and succeed at, competitive colleges and universities. SEO Scholars San Francisco is the first expansion region for this program and aims to replicate for Bay Area students the stellar outcomes that the program has delivered in New York City. (Learn more here: SEO Scholars)

POSITION OVERVIEW

With a portfolio of operational, strategic, and student-facing responsibilities, the Program Manager role provides the opportunity to make an impact both organization-wide and in direct service.

The Program Manager is responsible for advising and managing a cohort of up to 60 high school Scholars in their third year in the SEO Scholars program (rising 11th grade summer through end of 11th grade spring). This includes (1) building and maintaining a culture of high achievement and a supportive, family-like community that ultimately drives student performance in high school, and (2) leading students through programming (including mentoring and advisory curriculum) that will directly contribute to superior high school performance, in preparation for successful admission to competitive four-year colleges and universities. It is our goal to send 100% of our high school graduates to competitive four-year colleges and universities for free.

Responsibilities:

• Lead and implement SEO Scholars programming on Saturdays, after school, and during the summer. This includes designing and delivering Opening Circles and Advisory lessons, collaborating with instructional staff who serve your assigned cohort of Scholars. and co-facilitating the 11th Grade Mentor sessions.

• Monitor the performance and engagement of all Scholars in assigned cohort; track and analyze Scholar attendance, assignment completion, assessments and grades in SEO Scholars classes, high school courses, community college courses, and standardized test scores. Use data to drive advising discussions with Scholars

• Create and nurture an inclusive environment that encourages intellectual curiosity, academic excellence, and college readiness.

• Collaborate with co-11th Grade Program Manager on college advising curriculum creation and adaptations to meet overall 11th Grade advising strategy

• Provide data-driven academic advising and appropriate psychosocial guidance to all Scholars in cohort; monitor student attendance, participation, and performance at SEO and in high school; consult with Associate Director of Program to refer out to other agencies as necessary

• Support Manager of Mentoring and Enrichment Programs in managing mentor program- recruit, select and pair volunteer mentors with 11th Grade Scholars

• Collaborate with co-11th grade Program Manager and Manager of Mentoring and Enrichment Programs to ensure successful application cycle and strong Enrichment Program placement for all 11th graders

• Manage dual enrollment partnership opportunities for cohort through communication and collaboration with relevant staff.

• Serve as primary parent contact for 11th grade students in your cohort and their families; leverage data and learning partnerships to conduct individual and group parent meetings to foster Scholar’s successful completion of the program.

• Facilitate instructor check-in meetings to gather information about Scholar performance and advise on action plans to support Scholars.

• Collaborate with 10th and 12th grade staff to transition Scholars into and from the 11th grade each summer.

• Foster and maintain relationships with parents, school partners, volunteers, and corporate partners.

• Assist with the planning, coordination, and supervision of occasional trips (e.g. college tours).

• Effectively manage data in alignment with 11th grade goals and outcomes.

• Other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree required

• Direct experience working with high school-age students. 2+ years’ public teaching/counseling experience strongly preferred.

• Experience in student coaching and advising, including interfacing with parents and families.

• Evidence of progressive career growth within roles increasing in responsibility and autonomy.

• Strong work ethic and commitment to growth mindset

• Ability to guide students toward ambitious goals

• Highly adaptable and solutions-oriented with an ability to solve complex problems

• An uncompromising commitment to the highest quality work and exceptional results

• Experience in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment

• Ability to work a Tuesday through Saturday schedule and some nights as dictated by programming needs.

CORE COMPETENCIES & SKILLS

• Demonstrated passion for closing the opportunity and academic achievement gap at the high school and college level for first-generation and historically marginalized student populations.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including an ability to clearly and effectively present content in a public forum, engage in active listening, and command the attention of large groups of students.

• Excellent interpersonal skills. Must be practiced building professional relationships and delivering constructive, honest and productive feedback to Scholars and family members.

• Intermediate to advanced Excel and reporting skills with an affinity towards data-driven outcomes. Experience with Salesforce preferred.

• A proven background working with families and within communities reflective of SEO’s scholar population with the combined lived and learned experience to effectively apply a genuinely empathic, intentional, and inclusive lens to both relationships and work product.

• Bilingual Spanish/English is highly preferred; other languages skills are welcome!

COMPENSATION

The compensation listed in this posting reflects what SEO believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting. Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on the skills, qualifications, and experience of the applicant along with the requirements of the position, and SEO reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

EEOC Policy

At SEO we are committed to cultivating a team that embodies the backgrounds and experiences of the constituencies we serve and the communities we live in, and a workplace that reflects the impact we make in the world. Candidates from historically excluded and underrepresented communities – including people of color, women, members of the LGBTQIA+ Community, veterans, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

Equal Employment Opportunity is not just the law, it is our commitment.

Sponsors for Educational Opportunity is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer – M/F/D/V. We will consider all qualified applicants for employment regardless of race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy, parental status, genetic information or characteristics, or any other legally protected status.

If you need accommodation while applying for a role with SEO, due to a disability, please email SEO Talent.

THE ORGANIZATION

Established in 1963 by Michael Osheowitz, SEO (Sponsors for Educational Opportunity) is an educational non-profit founded on the belief that talent is everywhere; but opportunity is not. Our programs are designed to educate, train, mentor, and amplify the voices of our participants to give them a seat at the table – every table. We propel human potential.

SEO is an innovator in education, mentorship, and creating educational career opportunities that maximize the full potential of our participants. Each year SEO serves 7,000+ participants nationally, and the organization is widely recognized for developing best-in-class programs with exceptional results.

Not every SEO participant is on the same journey, but all are hungry for opportunity and SEO creates an ecosystem of excellence. Learn more about SEO's programs here: https://www.seo-usa.org/our-programs/.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure Engineering

The Infrastructure Engineering team enables Reddit to deliver Reliability, Performance, and Efficiency, with a single opinionated technology stack. We empower Reddit developers by delivering a reliable, scalable, and automated foundation - unifying compute, seamless deployments, robust storage, and high-performance messaging to maximize developer velocity and system resilience.

This centralized role hires across several high-impact teams, including:

• Messaging: Delivers a reliable, performant, and efficient platform to support asynchronous communication across all products and services at Reddit.

• Site Defense: Builds platforms that detect and mitigate bots, scraping, and abusive traffic while preserving a reliable experience for legitimate users across Reddit.

• Infrastructure Security: Builds platforms for service identity, secrets management, and secure access that make Reddit’s infrastructure secure by default.

What You’ll Do

jobs.title: Spanish Lead Teacher
jobs.description:
Inspire curiosity. Build independence. Shape a lifelong love of learning.

At Guidepost Montessori, our Lead Spanish Guides empower children ages 1.5–3 to grow into confident, capable learners through thoughtfully prepared environments and respectful, individualized guidance.

If you’re passionate about early childhood education and excited to lead a classroom where independence and joy take center stage, we’d love to meet you.

Your Role

As a Lead Spanish Guide, you’ll lead a mixed-age preschool classroom in a Montessori environment designed to nurture concentration, confidence, and deep learning.

Montessori guides carefully prepare their classrooms to spark curiosity and independence. Through close observation, individualized lessons, and intentional language, you’ll support each child’s academic, social, and emotional development meeting them where they are and helping them grow.

Children in Montessori classrooms have the freedom to choose meaningful work, repeat activities until mastery, and take pride in their accomplishments. Your guidance helps every child develop focus, confidence, and a strong belief in their own abilities.

What You’ll Do

• Observe each child closely to understand and support their physical, intellectual, and emotional development

• Prepare and maintain a beautiful, orderly classroom that fosters concentration and independence

• Encourage self-confidence by supporting children as they learn to “do it themselves”

• Provide individualized and small-group lessons in practical life, literacy, math, and beyond

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
About the Job:

LaunchDarkly is hiring a Chief of Staff to report to the CEO and partner with the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) as the company continues to scale. This is a senior, individual contributor role for a strategic operator and trusted advisor who thrives at the intersection of strategy, execution, communication, and data.

As Chief of Staff, you’ll help translate company strategy into action, shape executive-level planning and decision-making, and ensure leadership discussions are grounded in clear insights and high-quality materials. You’ll operate with significant autonomy, exercise wide latitude in how work gets done, and act as a thought partner to senior leaders across the organization.

This role is ideal for someone with deep experience navigating complex, cross-functional environments and a strong executive presence who is excited to have broad influence without people management responsibilities.

Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership & Cross-Functional Execution

• Partner with the CEO to drive company-wide strategic initiatives from conception through execution. Help align the Executive Leadership Team and broader organization around priorities, tradeoffs, and outcomes. Proactively identify risks, dependencies, and gaps across critical initiatives and surface insights to leadership. Act as connective tissue across executives and teams to ensure strategy translates into coordinated action.

Operating Cadence & Company Planning

• Shape and support LaunchDarkly’s operating rhythm, including owning OKRs and leadership planning processes.

• Design and evolve planning frameworks that enable effective executive decision-making.

• Support annual and long-range planning cycles, synthesizing inputs and highlighting strategic implications.

Executive & Company Communications

• Lead the preparation and refinement of executive-level materials, including Board meeting materials and ELT presentations. Ensure executive content is clear, concise, decision-oriented, and aligned with company strategy.

Data, Insights & Analysis

• Partner on executive dashboards and reporting, ensuring metrics are accurate, consistent, and actionable.

• Analyze and understand data to inform strategic decisions and evaluate proposed initiatives.

• Translate analysis into clear recommendations for senior leadership audiences.

Executive Meetings & Offsites

• Design agendas and content for executive meetings and off-sites with a focus on alignment and outcomes.

• Capture key decisions, clarify next steps, and support follow-through across the organization.

Qualifications:

• Typically requires a minimum of 15 years of related experience, preferably in senior-level roles involving strategy, operations, consulting, finance, product operations, or executive advisory work.

• Demonstrated success partnering closely with executive leaders and influencing at the highest levels of an organization.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complexity into clear, compelling narratives.

• Strong analytical capabilities and comfort working with SaaS metrics and executive-level data.

• Ability to manage multiple, high-impact workstreams with sound judgment and prioritization.

• High degree of discretion, integrity, and emotional intelligence.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. jobs.title: Senior Manager, Engineering Operations
jobs.location: Albuquerque, NM and Oak Ridge, TN
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

Job Summary

Kairos Power is seeking a dynamic and experienced Senior Manager, Engineering Operations to lead and scale our engineering operations and test execution capabilities within a 24/7 environment. This senior leadership role is responsible for selecting, training, developing, and directing multi-disciplinary engineering support teams, operators, and technical staff engaged in the execution of high-temperature testing campaigns and commissioning of complex experimental systems. The role will expand to include activation and operations for Kairos Powers’ operational nuclear reactors.

The ideal candidate brings a proven track record in industrial operations, nuclear or chemical plant environments, or advanced energy systems. This individual will provide strategic oversight of operations management, systems integration, process development, training, and safety compliance. The Senior Manager, Engineering Operations will be a critical voice in shaping how experimental and operational facilities are designed, operated, and evolved to support the mission of deploying transformative energy technologies.

This role will work out of our Albuquerque, NM location for approximately for the first 12 months and then transition to Oak Ridge, TN thereafter.

Responsibilities

• Provide vision and direction for 24/7 engineering operations, ensuring alignment with company objectives and milestones.

• Develop and execute long-term strategic plans to expand operations capabilities, streamline execution, and enhance reliability across test platforms.

• Establishes and reinforces operational standards, practices, and expectations that promote continuous improvement, safety, technical rigor, and operational excellence.

• Identify, evaluate, and mitigate operational, technical, regulatory, safety, and organizational risks.

• Lead a diverse team of managers, operators, and engineers; develop high-performing leaders at all levels.

• Develops organizational capability through employee development, succession planning, performance management, and recognition programs.

• Provide senior oversight of all test campaign planning, including readiness reviews, execution protocols, and post-test analysis.

• Establish and maintain a strong nuclear safety culture, conservative decision-making practices, procedural compliance, and high standards of operational excellence.

• Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of site operating programs, procedures, work controls, and management processes.

• Ensure the facility is appropriately staffed, trained, qualified, and prepared to support commissioning, initial criticality, startup, and sustained operations.

• Oversee operational readiness activities, including organizational readiness, procedure readiness, training and qualification, staffing, equipment readiness, and emergency preparedness.

• Develop and implement a progressive program to staff and operate next generation Small Modular Reactors that is safe, effective, and compliant.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, such as Engineering, Environmental Health and Safety (EHS), R&D, Operations, Quality, and others to establish and refine test procedures and operating envelopes.

• Ensure data integrity and reliability of operational and test systems, including SCADA, instrumentation, and data acquisition systems.

• Establish and refine standard operating procedures (SOPs) and shift operations frameworks across all testing and operational facilities.

• Implement reliability-centered maintenance (RCM) and root cause analysis (RCA) methodologies for recurring issues.

• Oversee system upgrades, change control processes, and integration of new technologies or designs into operations.

• Ensure all operations are performed in strict compliance with EHS and Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) policies and licenses.

• Lead collaboration with EHS to develop and approve Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs), permitting procedures, Risk Management Plans, and emergency response planning.

• Serve as an escalation point for all safety and operational incidents, ensuring robust corrective actions are implemented.

• Interface with senior leaders, program managers, and technical directors to communicate operational readiness, risk posture, and strategic recommendations.

• Represent engineering operations in cross-organizational working groups and governance forums.

• Support regulatory and audit preparation efforts as required by industry standards or internal review bodies.

• Oversee commissioning and transition to operations for new operational and experimental facilities.

• Lead cost-efficiency and capital-planning efforts across infrastructure and operational assets.

• Stay abreast of advancements in energy operations, plant engineering/operations, and automation relevant to testing environments.

• Additional duties as required.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Chemical, Mechanical, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field; advanced degree (MS, MBA, or PhD) preferred.

• Minimum 8+ years of progressively responsible experience in energy, nuclear, chemical, industrial, or other high-hazard or regulated operations, with at least 5 years of leadership experience managing technical or operational teams.

• Extensive experience and deep familiarity with P&IDs, process control systems (e.g., SCADA), instrumentation, or comparable industrial control systems.

• Ability to obtain and maintain Plant Manager/SRO certification and applicable emergency-response qualifications

• Demonstrated experience leading or overseeing complex engineering or industrial operations, including commissioning, startup, continuous operations, or similar operational activities; experience leading or overseeing 24/7 operations is highly desirable.

• Experience in nuclear operations, advanced reactor operations, nuclear commissioning, or startup of regulated nuclear facilities is desirable.

• Experience with radiological monitoring, radiological controls, and hazardous-material management is desriable.

• Experience supporting NRC licensing activities, regulatory inspections, audits, or other regulatory interfaces is desirable.

• Experience developing or overseeing operator training and qualification programs is desirable.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

• Knowledge of commissioning, startup, operational readiness, and transition-to-operations processes.

• Knowledge of nuclear safety culture principles, conservative decision-making, procedural adherence, and operational discipline.

• Ability to develop, implement, and improve operating procedures, management processes, training programs, and qualification frameworks.

• Ability to establish and maintain data integrity, system reliability, and appropriate operational controls for test and plant systems.

• Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams in 24/7, high-risk operational environments.

• Strong strategic planning and organizational alignment capabilities.

• Expertise in operational excellence, continuous improvement, and system reliability.

• Advanced knowledge of SCADA systems, process controls, and P&ID interpretation.

• Skilled in risk identification, mitigation, and decision-making under uncertainty.

• In-depth understanding of environmental, health, and safety (EHS) standards, job hazard analyses (JHAs) development, and regulatory compliance.

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to influence and engage stakeholders at all levels of the organization.

• Proficient in change management and integration of new technologies into operations.

• Strong project and resource management skills to oversee infrastructure investments, operational budgets, and capital planning initiatives.

• Ability to stay current with advancements in energy systems and plant operations.

• Ability to work with highly collaborative team.

• Ability to solve problems quickly and efficiently.

• Prioritizes and ensures safety of one self and others.

• Ability to proactively collect, manage and transfer knowledge.

• Ability to seek different and novel ways to create efficiencies when working on problems, challenges and issues.

Physical Demands

• Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, scissor lifts, articulated boom lifts and the like

• Setting up and transferring temporary structures (e.g. scaffolding, ladders)

• Moving self in different positions to accomplish tasks in various environments including tight and confined spaces

• Remaining in a stationary position for prolonged periods

• Moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another

• Adjusting, moving, transporting, installing, positioning, or removing objects up to 50 pounds in all directions

• Communicating with others to exchange information

• Operating motor vehicles, heavy equipment or machinery

• Use hand tools

Environmental Conditions

• Laboratory environment (chemical)

• Prototyping/Testing environment

• Low temperatures

• High temperatures

• Outdoor environment or elements such as precipitation and wind

• Noisy environments

• Small and/or enclosed spaces

• Odors or fumes from chemicals or chemical reactions

• Elevated heights

• Assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned

Safety and PPE

• Works safely in nuclear and other high-hazard operating environments in accordance with applicable procedures

• Reading and interpreting hazardous warning signs

• Manipulating, cleaning and disposal of hazardous materials

• Reporting issues with equipment or unsafe conditions
