jobs.title: Senior Android Engineer - Identity & Access Management
jobs.description:
ABOUT onX

We’re a team of builders, adventurers, and risk takers using technology to help people confidently explore the outdoors. Driven by our mission to awaken the adventurer inside everyone, we build products that optimize every outdoor experience and inspire confidence to get out and go further.

We’re a high-growth tech company. The pace is fast, the work takes grit, and ambiguity is part of the job. As the world changes around us, we adapt - continuously evolving how we build, prioritize, and deliver.

Our business moves quickly, and there’s real opportunity to shape what we build next. Each of our verticals - Hunt, Offroad, Backcountry, and Fish - is at a different stage of maturity, which means the challenges you encounter and the impact you have will vary depending on where you sit and what the business needs most.

We operate with an experimentation mindset, continually iterating and improving how we solve problems. We expect our people to use the latest tooling, including AI, thoughtfully and responsibly, pairing human judgment with technology to increase quality, speed, and impact.

Our impact comes to life through the products we build, in the stories of our customers, and in our growing commitment to land stewardship and recreational access.

ABOUT THIS OPPORTUNITY

onX is seeking a Senior Android Engineer who will contribute to meaningful, real-world outcomes that have a lasting impact for customers and the business. In this role, as part of the Identity & Access Management (IAM) team, you’ll focus on owning the Android client libraries that power authentication, sessions and feature access across every onX app , and the pipeline for sign-ups and entitlements. You’ll be supporting secure, reliable access to onX Hunt, Offroad, Fish and Backcountry for millions of hunters, anglers and outdoor enthusiasts, including when they’re far from a cell signal. You’ll take ownership of your work, collaborate closely with partners across the organization, and help move initiatives forward in an environment where priorities evolve, learning is celebrated, and you’re encouraged to keep stretching your skills. This role will report to a Software Engineering Manager III.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Essential Job Duties & Functions

• Own the platform. You’ll own onX’s Android identity, subscription, and feature-access libraries: shared Kotlin modules consumed by every onX Android app. You’ll set their technical direction, decide which patterns to keep and which to replace, and see changes through to production. You’ll co-own the API contracts with backend and push for changes when needed.

• Make auth dependable in the field. You’ll harden token refresh and session lifecycle, apply coroutines and structured concurrency correctly, and handle network loss and process death gracefully so users stay signed in when they need the app most.

• See what’s happening. You’ll build client-side observability for identity flows so the team can see auth health by device, OS version and app, then use that data to find and fix problems before customers report them.

• Champion both directions. You’ll represent Android in IAM design work (account management, session management, passkeys, one-time passwords, entitlements and bundling) and represent IAM in the Android codebase, partnering with backend engineers, Android platform leads and product teams across our apps. You’ll push for new capabilities when the current ones aren’t enough.

• Work with your iOS counterpart. You’ll be partnered on the team with an iOS counterpart to keep identity and entitlement behavior consistent: shared specs, shared test cases, and joint design docs.

• Raise the bar. You’ll grow the team’s client expertise through code review, documentation and mentoring, including backend engineers who contribute to client code. You’ll identify the next problems worth solving, write the design doc, align stakeholders, and drive it through rollout across apps.

• Adopt new technologies. You’ll look for opportunities to embed AI as a repeatable co-pilot in daily workflows by integrating experimentation into real work, and continuously refining its use with sound judgment and validation.

• Support for uptime and availability. You’ll join the team-based oncall rotation for the Identity team. While this does not require strong backend expertise, you may occasionally need to follow a runbook or escalate depending on the situation.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

• Six or more years of professional software development experience, with building and shipping production Android apps in Kotlin as a primary focus for at least three of those years, is required.

• Deep knowledge of Kotlin, coroutines and Flow, and experience diagnosing race conditions, lifecycle and threading issues in production apps.

• Experience building and maintaining a shared library or SDK used by multiple apps or teams (Gradle modules, versioning, API design for other engineers).

• Working knowledge of mobile authentication: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect, secure token storage with the Android Keystore, Custom Tabs or AppAuth, and session handling across process death and backgrounding.

• Security-first mindset: you think about secure defaults, token handling and failure modes as part of your design process.

• Comfort being the go-to expert for client identity and entitlements: you weigh tradeoffs, explain them to engineers outside Android, and push back or propose a new approach when the current one isn’t working.

• Experience driving cross-team technical initiatives, from design doc to rollout.

• A strong curiosity for exploring new technologies, including AI

• A shared passion for and ability to demonstrate onX’s Company Values.

• Permanent US work authorization is a condition of employment with onX.

• Ability to travel bi-annually for multiple days to a corporate office or other onX strategic location, such as a Basecamp.

ADDED BONUSES

Though not required, we would be thrilled to consider candidates with any of the following:

• Experience with identity platforms such as Ory (Kratos, Hydra), Auth0 or Okta, or with passkeys and the Credential Manager API.

• Experience instrumenting Android apps with Sentry or similar tools, including custom metrics and tracing.

• Experience with Google Play Billing, in-app subscriptions or entitlement checks.

• Experience building offline-first apps, or apps used where connectivity is unreliable.

• Experience working with a distributed team.

• A love of the outdoors and the apps that get people there.

THE ONX EXPERIENCE

onX is a distributed company with more than 400 employees across the country. We come together regularly to work in person and stay connected through regional basecamps and a culture that balances individual ownership with deep collaboration.

While we move quickly, we’re not a scrappy start-up. We operate with clear goals, structure, and frameworks that guide how we prioritize and execute. Priorities matter. While they may shift, data shapes how we evolve as our business, products, and the world around us change.

Clear priorities and structure don’t limit ownership - they make it possible. You’ll have the autonomy to define your work and make meaningful decisions within clear strategic boundaries. You’ll partner closely with others to solve complex problems and build solutions that scale across teams and platforms. Along the way, you’ll be supported with feedback, tools, and opportunities to grow your craft as you take on new challenges.

WHERE YOU CAN WORK

onX is a distributed company with employees across the U.S. We have physical offices in Bozeman and Missoula, MT, along with virtual workforce “Basecamps” in Austin, TX; Denver, CO; Kalispell, MT; Minneapolis, MN; Portland, OR; Salt Lake City, UT; and Seattle, WA. Basecamps are not physical offices; they are geographic hubs made up of remote employees who live within a 60-mile radius of the city center, creating opportunities for local connection and collaboration.

We have a strong preference for hiring candidates who live near one of our offices or within a Basecamp, and we prioritize candidates in these locations first. Candidates who live elsewhere in the U.S. may still be considered, provided they reside in a state where onX is currently able to employ team members.

At this time, we are NOT able to employ individuals whose primary work location is in: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia (D.C.), Florida, Hawaii, Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, South Dakota, West Virginia, and Wyoming.

HOW YOU’LL BE COMPENSATED

onX is committed to compensating all employees fairly and equitably for their contributions. For this position, we are open to considering candidates ranging in two levels (level II and level III). Spanning these levels, applicants can expect to make between $146,000 to $182,000 upon hire. The pay range will vary based on experience, skills, certifications, and education among other factors as required in the job description. In addition, full-time onX employees are eligible for a grant of common share options with a vesting schedule and a potential annual bonus of 10% based on company performance.

WHAT WE’RE OFFERING YOU

• Competitive salaries, annual bonuses, equity, and opportunities for growth

• Comprehensive health benefits, including a no-monthly-cost medical plan

• Paid parental leave of 13 weeks for birthing parents and 5 weeks for non-birthing parents

• 401k matching at 100% for the first 3% you save and 50% from 3-5%

• Company-wide outdoor adventures and amazing outdoor industry perks

• Annual “Get Out, Get Active” funds to fuel your active lifestyle

• Flexible time away package that includes PTO, STO, VTO, and paid holidays

PERFORMANCE ESSENTIALS

In this role, success is driven by cognitive abilities such as concentration and problem-solving, essential for our computer-centric tasks. onX will explore reasonable accommodations to ensure that individuals with diverse abilities can fully engage in and contribute to the essential physical and mental functions of the job. If you need assistance or accommodation, please contact us at PC@onxmaps.com.

Position open until filled.

#LI-Remote

At onX, we believe that unique perspectives make us stronger. By bringing together people with different experiences, ideas, and viewpoints, we fuel innovation and move closer to our mission of awakening the adventurer in everyone. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to fairness not only in hiring, but also in development, compensation, and promotion. Our goal is to build an inclusive community where every team member can show up authentically and thrive. Together, we win as one team. Come join us!

onX Maps will never ask for credit card or SSN details during the initial application process. For your digital safety, apply only through our legitimate website at onXmaps.com or directly via our LinkedIn page.

onX does not sell any Personal Information, but we may transfer employment related records to our service providers or third parties that provide business services to onX or as required by law. For more information, see our Privacy Policy.

As part of our interview process, your conversation may be recorded for documentation purposes to allow interviewers to focus fully on the discussion. Recordings are confidential and accessible only to authorized personnel. Please note, onX respects all applicable laws regarding recording consent, and you will have an opportunity to opt-out if preferred.

As an Intern at KEEN (KEENtern), you’ll dive into the exciting world of footwear, innovation, and community! You’ll get hands-on experience working alongside industry experts and contribute to shaping the future of KEEN.

The Integrated Marketing KEENtern will support the team that connects brand and product choices to how KEEN shows up in market-across launches, partnerships, channels and regions. This is a hands-on opportunity to learn how integrated marketing is built: from gathering consumer and cultural inputs, to supporting GTM planning, launch readiness and post-launch learning.

A key project within the internship will support the development of a stronger communications foundation for KEEN Effect - helping make the work easier for priority audiences to find, understand and connect to KEEN's broader purpose.

You will contribute useful, well-defined work that helps the team stay organized, informed and connected, while gaining exposure to KEEN's product, purpose and cultural activation agenda.

You will gain exposure to how a global brand turns sustainability and brand values, alongside consumer, product and cultural insight, into integrated market plans. You will work across product, creative, channel, market and KEEN Effect teams, and learn how launches are planned, coordinated, activated and assessed.

Essential Responsibilities

Integrated Marketing

• Support GTM planning, launch readiness and learning

• Help maintain planning decks, trackers and working documents for priority launches, moments and collaborations.

• Consolidate inputs from product, creative, fan insights, channel and market teams into clear, current source-of-truth materials.

• Capture decisions, next steps, dependencies and open questions from weekly brand and product meetings.

• Support the preparation of meeting materials, briefs and readouts for priority workstreams.

• Compile concise recaps of launches and collaborations taking place during the internship, capturing the activity, early response and key learning.

KEEN Effect storytelling

• Help develop a clearer communications foundation for KEEN Effect, translating complex work into information that is relevant, understandable and easier for priority audiences to navigate.

• Organize existing KEEN Effect online content and source materials, beginning with KOL; identify gaps, duplication, outdated information and opportunities to improve the experience.

• Research a focused set of relevant communications examples-including outdoor and purpose-led brands-to identify useful practices in content hierarchy, storytelling, navigation and calls to action.

• Support I&E and KEEN Effect in organizing existing information around priority areas of work, such as product sustainability, impact investment, thought leadership and employee action.

• Help develop a practical summary of findings, content priorities and initial recommendations that can inform future content updates and implementation.

Provide ad hoc integrated marketing team support:

• Coordinate selected product-seeding requests for creative and brand partners, including order tracking and follow-through.

• Maintain accurate project files, links and source materials.

• Support ad hoc research, meeting preparation and coordination needs across priority I&E workstreams.

Minimum Qualifications

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s degree with an interest in brand, marketing, culture, consumer insight, sustainability or product storytelling. Must be enrolled in an accredited college or university at the Junior, Senior, or Graduate level. You will also be considered if you have recently graduated from an accredited college or university.

• Must be able to work 40 hours/week during the internship program during normal working hours (Monday–Friday 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM) and be available to work in the office 5 days/week.

• Clear written communication and confidence synthesizing research, conversations and information into useful summaries.

What We’re Looking For:

We’re seeking someone who embodies our passion for creativity, sustainability, and the great outdoors. Our ideal KEENtern is:

• Passionate: Whether you’re an outdoor enthusiast, committed to sustainability, or fascinated by footwear trends and innovation, you’re excited to engage with the world around you.

• Creatively Minded: You’re detail-oriented, love bringing fresh ideas to life, and have a knack for solving problems.

• A Strong Communicator: Whether it’s collaborating with a team or presenting ideas, you know how to express yourself clearly and effectively.

• Proactive & Eager to Learn: You’re curious, ready to ask questions, take initiative, and dive into new challenges with enthusiasm.

Why Intern with Us?

Being a KEENtern means you’re not just an intern—you’re a valued part of our KEEN community. Here’s what you can look forward to:

• Meaningful Work: Tackle real-world projects that make an impact, gaining valuable hands-on experience at a globally recognized brand.

Ready to Take the Next Step?
If you’re ready to take your passions to the next level and be part of a world-class team, please apply.

jobs.title: Marketing Lead, Claude Frontier Academy
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Claude Frontier Academy is where organizations nominate their strongest people to build deep, hands-on skills with Claude. Backed by a $100 million commitment, Anthropic aims to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers by the end of 2027. The Academy’s first program, the Frontier Deployed Engineer (FDE) Residency, brings engineers from leading customers and partners together in cohorts, and more programs will follow. We’re looking for a Marketing Lead to make the Academy a name the market knows and a credential people are proud to earn.

As the Academy’s first dedicated marketer, you’ll own how it shows up in the world. You’re a creative, versatile marketer who thinks in terms of brand and communications and also knows how to position, launch, and grow programs. You’ll turn each program launch into a major market moment, celebrate milestones like new cohorts and the first badges earned, and build a community of graduates who help tell the story.

Because the Academy serves both partners and customers, this role will sit on our Partner Marketing team. You’ll work directly with partners and customers to secure their participation in announcements and bring them into our launch and amplification plans. You’ll help shape the Academy’s strategy and annual plan and represent marketing with senior leaders, while staying hands-on enough to write the first draft yourself. Partners and customers already engage with other Anthropic education and training programs, so you’ll be thoughtful about how the Academy fits alongside them. If you’ve built a branded program at a B2B technology company and want to do it again at a much bigger scale, this role is for you.

Key responsibilities

• Own the marketing strategy and annual plan for Claude Frontier Academy and its programs, working with Academy leadership to set priorities and goals

• Build and maintain a calendar of market moments for the Academy and each program, including program launches, new cohorts, and badge milestones

• Lead launches end to end, from messaging and announcement drafts through legal and executive review, launch-day execution and post-launch amplification

• Partner with Communications on press releases and announcements, including sourcing customer and partner quotes and securing approval to use their names

• Align early with Partnerships, Communications, and Account Teams on which customers and partners are named in each announcement, who gets a heads-up before it goes live, and how to answer those who aren’t named

• Develop amplification plans with partners and customers across social posts, blogs, newsletters, and their own announcements, and turn cohort results into joint customer and partner stories

• Grow the Academy’s presence on LinkedIn and other social channels with content that showcases programs, cohorts, and graduates

• Own the Academy’s web presence and any paid promotion, working with our web team and with creative and agency partners

• Build a community program that keeps cohort members and badge holders connected and turns them into advocates for the Academy

• Work with Brand to extend the Academy’s naming and brand architecture as new programs launch, keeping it consistent with, and clearly distinct from, Anthropic’s other education and training offerings

• Learn Anthropic’s other education and training programs, such as Claude Academy, Claude certifications, and Partner Basecamp, and work with their teams to define where Claude Frontier Academy fits, where the programs connect, and how they reference each other, so partners and customers see one clear path

• Equip Account Teams and Partner Account Managers with FAQs, internal announcements, and guidance so they can answer questions, help customers and partners register their interest, and set clear expectations on participation

• Keep senior stakeholders aligned through regular status updates and clear recommendations, and define and report on success metrics for Academy marketing

Minimum qualifications

• Have built and run branded B2B marketing programs at a technology company, such as customer education, certification, community, or user conference programs

• Have marketed education, training, or certification programs at a technology company, such as a partner, customer, or developer academy

• Bring a creative, brand-minded approach and know how to create market moments that get noticed

• Have led major launches or announcements, coordinating press, social, and partner amplification, and keeping everyone aligned through legal review, executive edits, and date changes

• Know how to build an audience and spark conversation on LinkedIn and other social channels with B2B audiences

• Have strong executive presence and are comfortable giving updates and making recommendations to senior leaders

• Can operate at both strategic and tactical levels, comfortable owning an annual plan and rolling up your sleeves to ship

• Build trusted relationships with partners, customers, and cross-functional teams, and can drive approvals and commitments without formal authority

• Are an excellent writer who can move easily between press releases, FAQs, and social posts

• Are energized by ambiguity and by building something new as a first-in-seat marketer

• Passionate about AI diffusion and bringing the benefits of AI to people and the world

Preferred qualifications

• 8+ years of B2B technology marketing experience spanning brand, communications, or program marketing

• Experience building community or advocacy programs where members promote the program themselves

• Experience marketing to technical audiences, particularly engineers and developers

• Experience running joint announcements with global system integrators, consulting firms, or enterprise customers

• Experience marketing to enterprise technology leaders, such as CIOs and CTOs

• Experience marketing AI/ML products

Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect all staff to be able to work from our San Francisco office at least 2 days a week, though we encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time for relocation.

Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$320,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Engagement Marketing Lead, Square
jobs.location: Bay Area, CA, United States of America
jobs.description:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.

The role

We’re looking for an Engagement Marketing Lead to help Square sellers discover more value in our products and build lasting relationships with Square. You’ll lead a team that turns seller insights into strategies that drive product adoption, deepen engagement, and deliver measurable business growth.

You’ll bring together audience strategy, messaging, experimentation, and channel planning to create relevant, connected experiences across the seller journey. Working closely with Product and cross-functional partners, you’ll set priorities, develop your team, and balance long-term growth opportunities with business commitments. The role has global scope, with an initial focus on the U.S.

You will

• Lead and develop the engagement marketing team. Set outcome-based goals, coach senior strategists, and define quarterly priorities, owners, and dependencies while delivering business commitments.

• Own cross-product growth priorities. Size opportunities and allocate capacity based on seller needs and business impact. Partner with Product on adoption, monetization, and the end-to-end seller experience.

• Establish proactive go-to-market planning. Align Product, Growth, Brand, Sales, Customer Insights, Creative, and channel partners on launch support, audiences, messaging, ownership, and resource tradeoffs.

• Lead program-wide experimentation. Partner with Data Science on coordinated holdouts and incremental measurement. Test recommendations, messaging, incentives, and channels; use evidence and economics to decide what to scale, refine, or stop.

• Establish communications governance. Set ownership, eligibility, frequency, sequencing, suppression, and risk-based review standards. Resolve competing messages, prevent over-messaging, and protect required communications.

• Scale execution responsibly. Partner with Lifecycle Operations, GTM Automation, and external agencies on production and automation. Retain accountability for strategy, approvals, access, quality, and escalation.

• Oversee portfolio delivery and partnerships. Hold owners accountable for launches, ongoing growth, incentives, and partnership commitments.

You have

• 10+ years in engagement marketing or equivalent experience demonstrating senior-level impact. A track record of leading teams and delivering measurable portfolio growth.

• Experience developing senior strategists and partnering with Product leaders. You can align teams, resolve tradeoffs, and establish clear accountability.

• Strong analytical judgment and hands-on fluency with SQL and analytics tools. You can diagnose seller behavior, size opportunities, assess economics, and distinguish incremental impact from attributed results.

• Deep experimentation experience and the ability to turn imperfect evidence into clear investment decisions.

• Strong positioning and messaging skills, with experience connecting audience insight, product value, and channel strategy.

• Experience building cross-program communications governance and translating strategy into actionable briefs, journey designs, and test plans with Lifecycle Operations.

• Fluency with lifecycle platforms, personalization, and delivery controls, with experience partnering with Engineering and Data Science on shared capabilities.

• Clear executive communication, sound judgment in ambiguity, and practical experience using AI to improve the quality or speed of your work.

• Experience with small-business customers, multi-product platforms, regulated products, agency partnerships, or international growth is valuable.

jobs.title: Strategic Communications Director
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE

Hadrian is hiring a Head of Strategic Communications to own what the company says publicly and who says it. This is the earned-media and executive-communications engine for the company: press relationships, announcement strategy, message discipline, and the voice the CEO and other leaders bring to every public moment.

You'll report to the SVP, Public Policy, who sets the direction for the company's external affairs and holds the comms slate — the master calendar of everything Hadrian says publicly, sequenced across announcements, launches, executive moments, and policy pushes. Your job is to run Strategic Comms with full ownership of its craft and its team.

You'll work in close partnership with peers across the broader external affairs function: a Brand & Marketing lead who owns owned channels, campaigns, and company events; and Government Relations and Policy leads who carry the company's positions into government offices and the broader policy ecosystem. Voice frameworks you help steward apply across all of these teams.





WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Media — Reporter relationships, inbound press handling, briefings, and embargo management. You are the person national and trade press call first.

Public Relations — Announcement strategy and execution for major company moments, reactive and issues response, and stewardship of Hadrian's standing narrative in the press.

Copy & Voice — Day-to-day ownership of how Hadrian sounds in earned and executive channels, working within the voice frameworks set at the SVP level. You're the standard-bearer for the function's copy, not the sole writer of everything.

Speeches & Public Comms — Executive speeches, talking points, prepared remarks, and Q&A prep. You are the primary support for Hadrian's CEO and other executives in public settings.

Internal Communications (in partnership with HR) — HR owns internal distribution and the employee relationship; you supply the message and voice that keep thousands of technicians and engineers across Hadrian's factory network aligned with the company's direction and momentum.

Team Leadership — Build and manage a team capable of carrying this workload without you in the room for every piece of work. Strategic Comms is currently load-bearing and under-resourced; part of this role is fixing that.

External Partners — Select, manage, and hold accountable the agencies, PR firms, speechwriters, and other outside consultants who extend the team's capacity. You set the brief, own the budget and performance of these relationships, and ensure external work meets the same bar as work produced in-house.





WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 15+ years of communications experience in tech, defense, aerospace, or a related field, with real fluency in how each of those worlds talks to the press, to government, and to itself

 - Demonstrated experience managing a team, including external consultants and agencies — you've hired and developed direct reports, and you've also run agency and freelance relationships with a clear brief, budget, and accountability for results

 - A relentless focus on mission — you understand why reindustrializing the United States matters and can translate that conviction into a story that lands with reporters, policymakers, and the public

 - Executive presence and judgment — comfortable advising a CEO in high-stakes moments, with the instinct to know when something is genuinely sensitive versus when it isn't

 - Sharp writing and editing instincts, and the ability to hold a company's voice steady across dozens of moving pieces

 - Proactive and collaborative — you propose into the external affairs and internal communications calendars rather than waiting to be handed work, and you build real partnerships with peers who own adjacent pieces of the story

 - Willing to travel — regularly, and often on short notice, to be on the ground for factory visits, executive appearances, and press moments across Hadrian's sites

 - Ability to obtain a U.S. national security clearance preferred

 - A sense of levity. You take the mission seriously and yourself less so, without ever letting standards slip


COMPENSATION

For this role, the target salary range is 210,000 - 250,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

   401k

jobs.title: Pricing Analyst
jobs.description:
About the Company:



Industrious is the largest premium workplace-as-a-service provider and home to the highest-rated workplaces in the industry. Everything we do comes down to creating great days for teams of all sizes and stages, including our own. We believe that what makes a great day at work is the people on your team and the problems you get to solve together. We’re looking for people who love thinking outside the box and thrive in a truly collaborative setting. As teammates, we encourage new ideas and toast every win. We’re excited about having a meaningful impact on people’s workplace experience.



Great days also start when everyone can be their authentic self at work. Diversity of backgrounds, thoughts, and ideas is critical to our success in delivering great workplace experiences, both for our members and for each other. Industrious is committed to creating an inclusive, respectful environment that embraces your individuality and quirkiness. You are valued for who YOU are. We celebrate our people as individuals who can accomplish great things when we work together as one team.



To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers http://www.industriousoffice.com/careers.




PRICING ANALYST (REVENUE MANAGEMENT)


Industrious is the largest premium flexible workspace company in the world, operating over 250 locations across 10 countries as part of the CBRE portfolio. We design workplaces where teams feel welcomed, supported, and able to do their best work. The same principle guides how we work together as a company.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Right now, the pricing judgment for Industrious's existing North America private office portfolio sits with one person who has built deep expertise in it: knowing which renewals need a bump, which office needs a promotion instead of a price cut, and which market is quietly slipping. That person is moving on to bigger things, and we need someone to step into that seat, formalize what works, and keep roughly 200 price changes a month running accurately, on time, and grounded in real conversations with the General Managers who run our buildings.


This is a Pricing Analyst, Revenue Management role, reporting into the pricing team. You will own business-as-usual pricing execution for the existing North America private office portfolio, with the scope to grow into other products and regions as the team expands.




WHAT MIGHT YOUR DAY LOOK LIKE

You start the morning scanning the pricing dashboard and notice a suite at 1411 Broadway that hasn't sold in weeks, while the identical suite next door is occupied at full list price. The GM has asked for a price cut. You pull the tour and application data, see it's a single-unit problem rather than a market problem, and decide a one-month promotion makes more sense than dropping the list price and setting up a harder renewal conversation down the road.



By mid-morning, you are on the phone with a GM in Nashville, walking through why an entire category of seven-to-nine person offices isn't moving. You ask about tour volume, application quality, and whether the floor plans still fit what people are searching for. You leave the call with a plan, and the GM leaves it feeling like someone actually looked at their building, not just their numbers.



In the afternoon, you work through the week's renewal batch, running each one against the pricing logic the team uses to decide what gets pushed through and what needs a second look. You flag one segment where occupancy has slipped two months running, log it for deeper review, and jot down a note on the decision tree so the next person doesn't have to relearn it from scratch.



You close the day updating the system with the changes you've made, checking your numbers against the portfolio report, and sending a short note to your manager on the one call that needs a decision above your pay grade.




WHAT YOU WILL OWN

 - Execute accurate, on-schedule pricing changes across roughly 200 price adjustments a month on the existing portfolio

 - Diagnose underperforming units or segments through variance analysis and turn findings into concrete pricing recommendations

 - Build direct, trusted relationships with General Managers as their first call on pricing, not a name behind a ticket

 - Run the renewal process end to end, from sending renewals to recommending pricing based on account and market performance

 - Evaluate the return on past promotional campaigns to shape smarter promotional decisions going forward

 - Keep pricing platforms, algorithms, and databases configured and accurate as the portfolio and product line grow

 - Document pricing logic and decision processes so institutional knowledge stops living in one person's head

 - Report on key revenue metrics, including Price/Seat, Occupancy, and RevPAR, for commercial leadership
   
   

This role leans on Problem Solving, because variance analysis only matters if you can turn a pattern in the data into a clear recommendation. It leans just as heavily on Communication, because the GMs you work with need to hear from a real person, not just see a system update. And it runs on Ownership and Bias for Action: at 200 changes a month, you move decisions forward with the information you have rather than waiting for certainty.




YOU WILL LOVE THIS ROLE IF

 - You love picking up the phone to talk through a tough pricing call instead of hiding behind a ticket update

 - You are energized by spotting the one underperforming unit before it shows up as a bigger problem in next quarter's numbers

 - You thrive on owning a defined piece of the business from day one, not waiting to be handed permission

 - You love turning ambiguous situations, like a single unit that won't sell, into a clear, defensible recommendation

 - You are comfortable moving through many decisions in a week without needing every signal to be perfectly clean

 - You thrive when your work is visible immediately to the people in the field who depend on it
   
   


THIS ROLE IS PROBABLY NOT FOR YOU IF

 - You want a long ramp-up before owning real decisions: this role hands you live pricing calls from week one

 - You would rather analyze quietly than get on the phone with a GM to talk through a hard pricing conversation

 - You are looking to build pricing models and algorithms from scratch: the frameworks already exist, and the job is to execute, refine, and document them

 - You need every process fully written down before you start: a lot of this knowledge currently lives in one person's experience, and part of the job is writing it down as you go

 - You want a role that stays narrowly scoped forever: this one is expected to grow beyond North America private office into new products and regions over time
   
   


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - A track record analyzing data to recommend pricing changes, working through problems independently with moderate guidance

 - Experience running variance or deep-dive analysis to identify underperforming segments and translate findings into action

 - Comfort configuring and maintaining pricing systems, algorithms, or databases, not just reading from them

 - Demonstrated ease building relationships with operational stakeholders, with a real preference for direct conversation over purely desk-based analysis

 - A background in a dynamic, demand-based pricing environment such as hospitality, hotels, or cruise lines, or experience with subscription-style renewal pricing, is a genuine plus
   
   


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS





The base salary for this role is $80,000 to $85,000, depending on experience, skills, and role alignment. This role is also eligible for an annual bonus and participation in our long term incentive program.



At Industrious, we believe a good workplace supports the whole person. Our benefits include:



 - Heavily subsidized medical, dental, and vision plans to support you and your family

 - Flexible paid time off, to maintain balance

 - Paid parental leave to help you welcome a new child and focus on what matters most

 - Annual professional development grants so you can keep learning and growing

 - 401(k) retirement savings program to support long-term financial wellbeing

 - Wellness initiatives and additional employee support programs
   
   

Specific benefits may vary by role, location, and eligibility requirements.



Equal Employment Opportunity: Industrious is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity. We have a long-standing commitment to providing equal employment opportunity to all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, veteran status, political belief, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Principal, Programs and Policy (Philanthropic Partnerships)
jobs.description:
About Omidyar Network (ON):

Omidyar Network (ON) is a philanthropic organization whose mission is to bend the arc of the digital revolution toward shared power, prosperity, and possibility. Digital technology is a powerful and ubiquitous force that, harnessed wisely, makes wondrous things happen. We believe in working together to guide tech’s trajectory intentionally. Our vision is for our shared humanity to steer our digital future.

So far, we have committed more than $1.94 billion to initiatives that share our vision. We engage, partner with, and fund some of the world’s brightest thinkers and innovators to guide our digital future toward the greatest good for the greatest number of people.

About the Programs and Policy team:

Our Programs and Policy team focuses on the key drivers of our shared digital future: the culture, the governance, and the business of digital tech. Through grantmaking, advocacy, and funder partnership, we aim to shape more intentional societal governance and amplify our shared agency. We work with a broad range of stakeholders, including investors, tech firms, policymakers, consumers, and workers, to guide tech’s trajectory and build coalitions and counterweights to concentrated power in civil society. Our team members come from policy, advocacy, nonprofits, community organizing, technology, consulting, philanthropy, education, and the arts.

About the Role:

As the Principal, Programs and Policy (Philanthropic Partnerships) at ON you will play a central role in honing our engagement across the philanthropic ecosystem at a time when so many funders, new and seasoned alike, are asking questions about artificial intelligence and digital technology: What role should we play? Where to begin? Who’s doing what? What opportunities stand out?

In this role, you will upgrade our approach to philanthropic partnership in three domains: (1) funder education, everything we do to help individual and institutional funders get oriented, networked, and off the sidelines; (2) funder collaboration, including a portfolio of formal partnerships and faster-moving aligned funding opportunities; and (3) signature initiatives or products to elevate our network’s point-of-view and priorities.

This is an exciting time to join ON. In recent years, we’ve incubated or seeded new initiatives (e.g., Andaris, The Tech We Want), co-founded philanthropic collaboratives (e.g., Humanity AI, Responsible Tech Youth Power Fund), and co-convened funder learning tables and workshops (e.g., AI and labor, competition, California policy).

The ideal candidate is a savvy orchestrator who excels at the relational, intellectual, and strategic dimensions of moving a fragmented philanthropic ecosystem toward greater impact. You are equally at ease one-on-one with a family foundation principal discussing what we know about AI’s labor implications or briefing an eclectic room of 30 funders on ON’s priorities. Day to day, you are the conductor of a team-wide partnership approach that demands judgment calls about what to spotlight, who to pull into meetings, and how to translate an opportunity for different audiences.

This role reports to the Senior Director, Programs and Policy, who is based remotely in Los Angeles, CA.

How You’ll Contribute to our Impact:

• Be a trusted resource for funders. Run substantive briefings on the tech/AI and society landscape and the opportunities most responsive to field and funder priorities. Create and manage a library of assets including briefing presentations and two-pagers that illuminate opportunities for institutional philanthropy, high-net-worth individuals and family offices, funding intermediaries, donor advisors, and other public interest funds. Plan and facilitate events that connect funders with learning and investment opportunities, bringing in relevant experts and ON colleagues.

• Steward relationships with funders. Manage a pipeline of funder relationships spanning inbound inquiries, proactive outreach, and existing partnerships. Convene regular strategy and learning conversations across our anchor partnerships (e.g., Humanity AI, Andaris, The Tech We Want, etc). Collaborate with ON’s leadership and members of the Programs and Policy team to share timely co-funding opportunities, joint initiatives, and aligned strategies. Work with our Strategy, Learning, and Impact team on tracking and reporting our impact.

• Listen, learn, and shape the philanthropic conversation. Stay current on the evolving philanthropic landscape as it relates to the governance of digital technology, artificial intelligence, and societal implications. Travel to represent ON at strategic convenings and conferences. Be a recognized voice on philanthropic partnership and our priority areas.

Location:

This is a hybrid role, with employees working in the office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. This position will be based out of our San Francisco or Washington, DC office. Employees must reside within 100 miles of their assigned office location. This role will require moderate travel (20-30% depending on time of year).

Candidates must have a current U.S. work authorization to be considered. ON does not sponsor or provide support for visas or work authorization, including H-1B, OPT, STEM OPT, and other temporary work authorization programs.

Compensation:

This is a full-time, salaried position that features competitive pay and benefits, including health care (medical/dental/vision), paid time off, and a generous employer 401(k) contribution. The starting salary range for this role is $171,400-$214,200 in San Francisco and $154,200-$192,800 in Washington, DC. ON manages pay equity seriously and new hires generally start at the midpoint of this range.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

• Minimum of 7 years in philanthropy, partnerships, fundraising, or a related field. Relevant experience may include, but is not limited to: work with foundations or funder collaboratives; donor advisory or family office teams; institutional or major-gift fundraising at a non profit, research institution, or policy organization.

• An entrepreneurial mindset and commitment to our mission. You’re comfortable with ambiguity, energized by building, and quick to spot emerging trends across technology, policy, and philanthropy. You care about shaping the digital future for shared power, prosperity, and possibility.

• Credibility within the philanthropic ecosystem and a strong track record with funders. You build trust quickly with senior decision-makers, listen as well as you advocate, and have produced sustained high-impact partnerships that produced results and stayed true to shared values. You understand who is funding what and where the openings for collaboration are. You bring relationships in some part of the philanthropic ecosystem (institutional and family foundations, family offices, individual donors and their advisors, funding intermediaries, or newer tech and AI funders) and the instincts to build the rest.

• Fluency in digital technology, AI, and its societal implications. You don’t need to be a technologist, but you demonstrate a sophisticated level of engagement with major aspects of technology and AI governance, grasp what’s at stake, and can translate issues in a clear and accessible manner.

• Strategic thinking and execution. You connect outside opportunities to our goals, turn big-picture thinking into concrete next steps, and keep many relationships moving at different stages, with the organization and follow-up discipline that earns funders’ trust: nothing slips, every conversation has a next step, and you know where your time matters most.

• Outstanding writing and presentation skills. You have delivered presentations or briefings that oriented senior audiences, including board level rooms, to a complex field, and you can write the materials yourself.

Omidyar Network is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes people from all experiences, abilities, and perspectives to apply. We fundamentally believe that people are inherently capable but often lack opportunity. We know that a diverse workforce reflecting a broad range of backgrounds and views allows us to see problems in more nuanced ways, creating the thought leadership needed to elevate humanity and evolve the culture, governance, and business of technology. We actively recruit, develop, and retain the most talented people from a broad candidate pool. We are committed to an inclusive and accessible hiring process. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in any part of the application or interview process, please let us know at recruitment@omidyar.com.

jobs.title: Senior Flight Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Welcome to Planet. We believe in using space to help life on Earth.

Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company all rolled into one.

Customers and users across the globe use Planet's data to develop new technologies, drive revenue, power research, and solve our world’s toughest obstacles.

As we control every component of hardware design, manufacturing, data processing, and software engineering, our office is a truly inspiring mix of experts from a variety of domains.

We have a people-centric approach toward culture and community and we strive to iterate in a way that puts our team members first and prepares our company for growth. Join Planet and be a part of our mission to change the way people see the world.

Planet is a global company with employees working remotely world wide and joining us from offices in San Francisco, Washington DC, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, and The Netherlands.

About the Role:

Planet’s Flight Software Team is responsible for all of the embedded software that powers our diverse fleet of Superdove, Skysat, Pelican, and Tanager satellites. The software we build and maintain deploys to orbiting spacecraft hundreds of kilometers away and spans many functional verticals, including navigation and avionics, payload control, radio software, and supporting tooling and infrastructure. We collaborate closely with many other teams at Planet, including Payload, EE, RF, Ground Stations, and Missions teams, to deliver reliable and innovative solutions that ensure the success of Planet’s missions. As a Senior Flight Software Engineer for Superdove, you will lead ongoing development, verification, and on-orbit anomaly escalation for Planet’s core satellite platform. In this role, you will work with domain experts to design improved flight software, optimize operational efficiency, and ensure seamless hardware and software integration. Ideal candidates are curious, data-driven, and passionate about scaling orbital systems.

We are currently seeking a Senior Software Engineer to lead ongoing development, verification, and on-orbit anomaly escalation for Planet’s existing satellite platform, Superdove. As a Senior Flight Software Engineer, you will develop a deep understanding of existing on-orbit software systems and how the software interacts with hardware, firmware, Satellite Operations, and the complex physical environment found in LEO. You will work closely with Manufacturing and Manufacturing Test to ensure successful satellite builds. You will work with domain experts in RF, ADCS, EE, FPGA, and our Flight Software team to design and implement improved flight software, and to support new requirements and circuit designs. You will use systems including Mission Control and telemetry to understand the behavior of our software on orbital scale, and will work with teams across Space Systems to deliver improved efficiency and productivity of our core Superdove imaging platform.

This is a full-time, hybrid role which will require you to work from our San Francisco office 3 days per week.

Impact You'll Own:

• Develop improved software systems for the Superdove spacecraft

• Identify opportunities for efficiency and productivity gains, and implement them

• Work with FSW experts to deeply learn how existing systems work, gather ideas for how to improve them, plan long-term improvement projects, and deliver sustained value over months.

jobs.title: Director, Growth Marketing
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Nova Credit is the industry’s leading cash flow intelligence platform, enabling businesses to unlock the power of cash flow data in how they operate. The company leverages its industry-leading data infrastructure, innovative intelligence layer, & robust FCRA-compliance to boost approvals, improve offers, fight fraud, drive responsible growth, and more. Nova Credit supports over 7,000 businesses including organizations such as Chase, HSBC, SoFi, Sallie Mae, Appfolio, and Yardi, with a growing suite of products. Nova Credit is proud to be backed by an exceptional group of investors and was named in Forbes’ Fintech 50 in 2025 and Built In’s Best Places to Work, 2025.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Nova Credit’s solutions are among the most widely used in multifamily. They’re embedded in four of the top five property management software platforms and used by more than 7,000 property management companies. Our Rental Housing platform helps operators verify income, determine eligibility, and assess risk using bank, payroll, and document data that traditional screening misses, so they can approve more qualified renters and lease units faster.

As Director of Growth Marketing, you’ll own brand and demand across our Rental Housing platform. Your most important challenge is creating the market for cash flow underwriting: we want every leasing director, regional manager, and asset manager to know Nova Credit and why it matters to their portfolio. Operators who have access to our products through their software should use them, and operators who don’t should ask for them.

We expect about three-quarters of your focus to go to Nova-owned programs and a quarter to co-marketing with our platform partners. You’ll report to our Head of Rental Housing, partner with a growth team that spans partner enablement, events, and product marketing, and work closely with our account management and new business teams. This is a hands-on individual contributor role to start, with the opportunity to build a team as the program proves itself.

This is a hybrid full-time role (3 days per week in office on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays) based in the New York Metropolitan area.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

• Own the strategy to take cash flow underwriting from unknown to in demand. Define the problem in the industry’s own language: the qualified renters, vacancy days, and risk that credit-only screening costs operators and owners.

• Develop ideas for original research and flagship content, often built on Nova’s proprietary renter cash flow data. Partner with product marketing to produce them, and own the campaigns that make each one a reference point for the industry.

• Partner with account management and new business to recruit early-adopter operators, and turn their results into stories and proof points that make the category credible.

• Run campaigns across our full platform, from income verification to eligibility determination and cash flow underwriting, and build Nova’s reputation in industry media and PR as the authority on fair, compliant screening.

• Grow a clean, compliant, well-segmented database of property management decision-makers, and engage it through email, newsletters, and nurture programs.

• Run high-reach programs with industry media and associations. Set our rental housing event strategy, including which events we attend and what we focus on there, with our events partner leading execution.

• Build account-based programs for high-value operators and institutional portfolios, including REITs and PE-backed owners, making the case that screening policy drives NOI, risk, and asset value. Create demand on platforms where Nova isn’t yet available.

• Co-market with our software partners through co-branded research, joint webinars, and campaigns that reach their customers.

• Close the loop on every program. Plan follow-up before launch, personally follow up with interested decision-makers alongside the Head of Rental Housing, and report results from awareness through adoption and revenue. Set goals and manage budget.

WITHIN THE FIRST 90 DAYS, YOU’LL:

• Learn our products, partners, customers, and market, and audit our existing contacts, content, events, and past programs.

• Deliver a quick win using existing assets, such as a campaign built on our published cash flow research.

• Present a 12-month plan, including our event calendar, with clear goals for awareness, demand, database growth, and adoption.

WITHIN THE FIRST YEAR, YOU’LL:

• Run Nova’s owned channels on a consistent cadence with regular reporting, and measurably grow our database and demand for our products.

• Help bring our first early-adopter operators live on cash flow underwriting and publish their results.

• Make cash flow underwriting a recognized idea among property management decision-makers, with Nova Credit as the name associated with it.

• Generate demand both on platforms where our products are available and on platforms where they aren’t yet.

YOUR SKILLSET:

• 8+ years in B2B marketing, with significant experience in property management, proptech, multifamily, or rental housing. Industry fluency is required.

• A proven track record of creating a market for a new product or category. You’ve made customers want something they didn’t know they needed. This is the most important skill for this role.

• Experience building a marketable database and consistently running owned programs (email, content, sponsored programs, events) with measurable results.

• Discipline about follow-through. A program isn’t finished until leads are worked and results are reported.

• An existing network across operators, software platforms, industry media, and associations.

• Strong storytelling and campaign instincts. You know which ideas will get the industry’s attention and how to turn data-driven content into campaigns people read and share.

• Experience co-marketing with partners in markets where customers buy through platforms.

• A hands-on builder who is comfortable as the first dedicated marketer in a fast-moving business and ties marketing to adoption and revenue.

$195,000 - $222,300 USD per year

The above compensation range is for U.S.-based candidates and is dependent on individual experience, skills, education, location, and qualifications. We consider all elements of compensation as a part of the value we provide to Novans. This may include base salary, equity grants, incentive compensation for eligible roles, professional development, flexible PTO, and tenure rewards. We offer U.S.-based Novans competitive, employer-subsidized medical, dental, and vision plans, in addition to mental health and wellness benefits and a range of other benefits and perks.

We are an equal-opportunity employer where everyone is welcome at Nova Credit. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected class, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We encourage all qualified candidates, including those with a criminal history, to apply.

Before submitting your application, please review our Applicant Privacy Notice to learn how we collect, use, and protect your personal information during the application process.

jobs.title: Senior GTM Compensation Manager
jobs.description:
About Anaconda

Be at the center of AI

Anaconda is built to advance AI with open source at scale, giving builders and organizations the confidence to increase productivity, and save time, spend and risk associated with open source. 95% of the Fortune 500 including Panasonic, AmTrust, Booz Allen Hamilton and over 50 million users rely on the value The Anaconda AI Platform delivers through a centralized approach to sourcing, securing, building, and deploying AI. With 21 billion downloads and growing, Anaconda has established itself as the gold standard for Python, data science, and AI and the enterprise-ready solution of choice for AI innovation. Anaconda is backed by world-class investors including Insight Partners. Learn more at https://www.anaconda.com.

Summary

Anaconda is hiring a Senior GTM Compensation Manager to own sales compensation within our Finance team. You’ll be responsible for commissions calculation accuracy and the performance insights that help guide our Go-To-Market (GTM) direction. You’ll work between Finance, Sales Ops, and GTM leadership, and you’ll be the person the field trusts when a commission question comes up. This is a chance to apply your experience to the world of data science, AI, and machine learning.

What You’ll Do

• Own the commission program end-to-end. Run plan design input, quota crediting, payout, and audit, with accuracy and on a predictable cadence.
• Run our ICM system. Own the commissions database and system configuration, and keep the data clean. We use Everstage.
• Turn data into insights and direction. Analyze quota attainment, pipeline coverage, and sales performance, and bring leadership clear recommendations.
• Plan capacity. Model and forecast GTM headcount, productivity, and coverage against revenue goals.
• Be the point person for the field. Handle commissions questions and disputes, interpret plan policy, and explain the reasoning clearly to reps and sales leaders.
• Partner with the Revenue team. Be the glue to all things Compensation between the Revenue and Finance organizations.
• Use AI in your daily work. Apply AI tools to speed up commission audits, reconciliations, inquiry triage, and analysis, and share what works with the team.
• Build controls. Put checks in place that catch payout errors before they reach a paycheck.

What You Need

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Data Science, or another analytical field
• 5+ years of hands-on experience in sales compensation, GTM finance, or GTM operations at a SaaS or high-growth software company
• Proven ownership of a commission function at a senior level, including plan administration, quota crediting, payout, and audit. You’ve done this before and can step in without a long ramp
• Experience administering an ICM platform. Experience using Everstage is a plus, and experience using both spreadsheets and more than one ICM tool is highly valued
• Advanced Excel/Sheets and modeling skills, plus a solid grasp of databases and data techniques
• Experience with Salesforce and other SaaS tools used in the comp workflow (Rippling, etc.)
• Experience handling and resolving customer-facing questions and disputes, not just building models behind the scenes
• You use AI tools in your day-to-day work (drafting, analysis, data cleanup, workflow automation) and are comfortable using them on high-stakes numbers with a human check
• Detail-oriented with a high degree of accuracy handling high-stakes calculations

What Will Make You Stand Out

• Reps and sales leaders like working with you, and you can explain a complex payout in plain language
• You treat your function like a small business: you have opinions, you make a case for them, and you build processes that scale
• You can point to a control or process you built that caught real payout errors
• You’ve built or shared AI-assisted workflows, such as automated reconciliation checks or plan-document Q&A, that saved your team time
• Python, R, or SQL experience, and familiarity using Anaconda’s products
• Experience at a fast-paced startup or at an open-source, AI, or data science company

Why You'll Like Working Here

• You'll thrive in a high-performance environment where results are recognized and rewarded
• Your work directly contributes to shaping the future of data science, machine learning, and AI in the enterprise.
• You'll work alongside a collaborative team that values diverse, thoughtful discussion, clarity and candor.
• You'll be supported by a culture that puts employees first - with flexible hours, a fully remote setup, and a genuine commitment to your wellbeing and growth.

The application deadline for this role is 01/02/2026; applicants will be reviewed on an ongoing basis until the role is filled.

The base salary range for this role is $100,000 - $140,000. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. jobs.title: Legal Operations Specialist - Employment (Contract)
jobs.description:
About Rippling

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

About the role

We are looking for a sharp, highly motivated, and innately curious Legal Operations Specialist - Employment (Contract) to support our growing employment legal team on a contract basis. In this role, you will build efficient, scalable operations, with a strong focus on employment litigation, disputes, and investigations. You will be instrumental in managing and improving litigation workflows, including issuing legal holds, managing data collection through e-discovery platforms, and tracking employment disputes and claims. You will also contribute to broader employment legal operations and compliance initiatives. This role will report directly to the Assistant General Counsel - Employment, but will work closely with other employment counsel, litigation team members, and cross-functional stakeholders.

The ideal candidate is extremely detail-oriented, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and can juggle competing priorities with ease. A resourceful and proactive problem-solver with strong judgment, exceptional organizational skills, and a collaborative mindset will excel in this role.

What you will do

• Design, implement, and support legal operations infrastructure, with a focus on employment litigation, disputes, and investigation workflows.
• Lead investigatory research for our most sensitive employment matters, connecting information across internal systems to uncover key facts and inform litigation strategy.
• Coordinate internal employment litigation and discovery needs, including case management, legal hold issuance and tracking, data collection and processing, and document review and production.
• Serve as a liaison between internal stakeholders and outside counsel for active employment litigation, arbitrations, and agency charges, driving information gathering and follow-through.
• Create and drive processes around employment legal compliance, including auditing key training and employment document execution and partnering with the legal and recruiting teams on other employment document needs.
• Develop, implement, and continually improve employment legal operations policies, processes, and procedures.
• Design and build systems that turn employment matter data into actionable insights, helping the team identify trends, anticipate risks, and prioritize resources

What you will need

• 3–5+ years of experience in legal operations, litigation support, legal assistant, or paralegal roles, including experience supporting employment litigation or disputes. A combination of in-house technology company and law firm experience is preferred.
• We welcome candidates who are earlier in their in-house careers and are eager to grow their legal operations experience in a fast-paced tech environment.
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
• Demonstrated ability to manage complex litigation processes, including familiarity with e-discovery tools and case tracking platforms; experience with employment agency charges and arbitrations is a plus.
• Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail.
• Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.
• Sound judgment and discretion in handling sensitive employment matters and confidential information.
• Team player who takes initiative and demonstrates curiosity about how our company and business work.
• Entrepreneurial mindset, self-starting, and comfortable working in a highly dynamic environment.
• Sense of humor!

What would be nice to have

• Experience supporting employment arbitrations, EEOC or state-agency charges, or wage-and-hour litigation.
• A combination of law firm and in-house experience, particularly in a fast-paced technology company.
• Experience building or improving matter trackers, intake processes, playbooks, dashboards, or other legal operations systems.
• Experience conducting investigative research across HR, payroll, and collaboration systems.
• Paralegal education or certification, subject to applicable requirements.

Additional Information

Rippling is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other legally protected characteristics, Rippling is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities who need assistance during the hiring process. jobs.title: Associate Director, QC Analytics
jobs.description:
ElevateBio is a technology-driven company powering the industry forward by helping partners realize the potential of their therapies from design to commercialization. We have integrated a differentiated set of technologies, end-to-end services, and industry-leading manufacturing expertise to develop advanced therapies faster and more efficiently.

The Role

The Associate Director, QC Analytics provides operational leadership for routine GMP analytical testing at ElevateBio’s Waltham site and leads a team of managers responsible for seven-day laboratory operations. This role is accountable for predictable execution of product release and in-process testing, laboratory excellence, right-first-time performance, and timely, compliant reporting of results. The Associate Director leads the testing organization through disciplined capacity planning, daily management, schedule control, performance management, and rapid resolution of operational barriers across the full operating week. The role partners closely with Quality Control Analytical Technologies (QCAT), which provides technical enablement and analytical lifecycle leadership, to ensure new or changed methods, equipment, controls, critical reagents, and digital capabilities transition into stable, sustainable routine operations.

jobs.description:

It pairs AI with human expertise to turn data from the world’s largest Safety Network into life-saving intelligence. The network includes more than 730 million connected devices and more than 325 global technology companies. That intelligence reaches more than 23,600 federal, state and local agencies, serving 1.2 million first responders. RapidSOS has supported more than 1.1 billion emergencies in 16 countries.
