jobs.title: Production Chemist, CGMP Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve. 



Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about http://hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works http://hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals http://www.hims.com/careers-professionals.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Production Chemist performs hands-on cGMP peptide manufacturing, supporting either upstream operations (synthesis and cleavage) or downstream operations (preparative HPLC purification and lyophilization). You will carry out assigned batch tasks safely, accurately, and on schedule. Note that cross-training in the other area may follow once you are established in the role. Experience in both areas is not required; strength in either one is enough.

This role reports to the Supervisor, CGMP Manufacturing. Recent graduates are encouraged to apply; training will be provided.

This role is based in Menlo Park, CA at our H&H Peptides facility. 




YOU WILL:

Execution:

 - Execute assigned manufacturing tasks per approved batch records, SOPs, and work instructions with minimal supervision, in a timely and efficient manner.

 - Read work orders and batch records thoroughly and understand the instructions and final product specifications before starting each task.

 - Upstream: perform SPPS and cleavage operations, including resin preparation, synthesizer operation, cleavage, precipitation, and crude peptide isolation.

 - Upstream: verify protected amino acids batch by batch against specification, including solubility and appearance, before use.

 - Downstream: perform prep HPLC purification, fraction pooling, concentration, lyophilization, and final packaging.

 - Downstream: check analytical HPLC and mass of dissolved crude peptide and identify the target peptide peak by integration and mass spectrometry to guide purification and fraction pooling.

 - Handle raw materials, solvents, and reagents safely; operate and clean production equipment and instruments (such as HPLCs, centrifuges, freeze dryers, stir plates, laboratory balances, mass spectrometers (optional), sonicators, vacuum ovens, and nitrogen supply) and report issues promptly.

 - Prepare and label chemical solutions and buffers according to standard formulas.

 - Perform in-process checks and escalate unexpected results right away.

Schedule Adherence:

 - Complete assigned tasks on time to support batch and campaign schedules.

 - Communicate delays or material and equipment constraints to the Supervisor early and support shift hand-offs.

Documentation & Compliance:

 - Complete batch records, logbooks, and standardized forms accurately and in real time, including purification and other process records.

 - Review data for accuracy and completeness before submission and perform data analysis as assigned.

 - Report deviations promptly, keep the work area clean, organized, and inspection-ready, and complete GMP and safety training on time.

Teamwork:

 - Work closely with teammates, Quality, QC, and Maintenance, and take part in cross-training.

 - Contribute observations and data that support process improvement and product quality.

Competencies:

To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies:

 - Problem Solving - Identifies and resolves problems in a timely manner; Gathers and analyzes information skillfully; Develops alternative solutions; Works well in group problem solving situations.

 - Teamwork - Balances team and individual responsibilities; Exhibits objectivity and openness to others' views; Gives and welcomes feedback; Supports everyone's efforts to succeed.

 - Organizational Support - Follows policies and procedures; Completes tasks correctly and on time; Supports organization goals and values.

 - Motivation - Sets and achieves challenging goals; Demonstrates persistence and overcomes obstacles; Measures self against standard of excellence.

 - Adaptability - Adapts to changes in the work environment; Manages competing demands; Changes approach or method to best fit the situation; Able to deal with frequent change, delays, or unexpected events. 


YOU HAVE:

 -  Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related discipline (recent graduates welcome)

 - Hands-on laboratory experience, through coursework, internships, or work

 - Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow procedures precisely and document accurately

 - Strong communication and time management skills, and ability to work independently and as part of a fast-moving team

 - Ability to stand for extended periods, lift up-to 40 lbs., and wear required PPE

 - Ability to work Saturdays and/or Sundays as required by the production schedule


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: 

 - Background or hands-on experience in peptide synthesis (SPPS), from academic research, an internship, or industry (upstream)

 - Experience with HPLC purification or lyophilization (downstream). Experience in either area is sufficient

 - Familiarity with analytical HPLC and mass spectrometry for in-process data review

 - Prior exposure to cGMP or regulated environments


OUR BENEFITS (THERE ARE MORE BUT HERE ARE SOME HIGHLIGHTS):

 - Competitive salary & comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision

 

Conditions of Employment: 

 - This position will require working with Hazardous Drugs (HD) and would require that Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) be worn for the length of working with these drugs. These items would include gloves, respiratory protection, gown and other items as required.

 - This position requires medical approval to wear respiratory protection in the form of negative or positive pressure respirators, including N95, full face respirator, SCBA, or Powered Air Purifying Respirator (PAPR).

 - Physical exertion required. Including, but not limited to, walking up to 50% of the time, standing up to 100% of the time, squatting and bending up to 20% of the time and lifting up to 80% of the time for up to a twelve hour shift. Must be able to lift up to 50lbs.

 - Due to the risk of reproductive capability in handling or compounding certain Hazardous Drugs (HD) associates must be willing to confirm that they understand the potential risks (teratogenicity, carcinogenicity and reproductive effects) of handling hazardous drugs.

 



We are committed to building a workforce that reflects diverse perspectives and prioritizes ethics, wellness, and a strong sense of belonging. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you're not sure if your background or experience is a perfect match.



Hims considers all qualified applicants for employment, including applicants with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act, and any similar state or local fair chance laws.



It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

jobs.title: Chip Simulation Lead
jobs.description:
About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.



Job Summary

We are looking for a Lead Chip Simulation Engineer to drive the technical direction and development of our custom AI accelerator simulation infrastructure.

Our chip simulation team builds the hardware models that enable software development, debugging, and hardware-software co-design before silicon is available.

In this role, you will guide engineers working on our bit-accurate, cycle-aware chip simulator, review designs and code, and ensure the team builds accurate, performant, and maintainable simulation infrastructure. You'll work closely with hardware architects, firmware, kernel, and software teams to identify technical challenges, set priorities, and enable early development of our full software stack.

This is a highly technical leadership role for someone who enjoys mentoring engineers, solving complex systems problems, and staying close to the code.



Key Responsibilities

 - Provide technical leadership for the chip simulation team, guiding engineers through architecture, implementation, debugging, and performance optimization.

 - Own the technical direction of our simulation infrastructure, ensuring accuracy, scalability, performance, and maintainability.

 - Lead design and code reviews, establishing engineering best practices and maintaining a high bar for code quality.

 - Mentor and support engineers, helping them navigate complex technical challenges.

 - Drive hardware-software co-design, partnering with hardware architects and software teams to influence architecture and enable pre-silicon development.

 - Oversee simulator integration, including simulated hardware modules, QEMU-based host integration, and multi-chip simulation.

 - Guide validation and testing strategies to ensure simulation correctness and alignment with hardware specifications.

 - Remain technically hands-on when needed, contributing to critical implementations, debugging, and architectural prototyping.



Representative Projects

 - Lead the development of simulation models for our custom AI accelerator.

 - Guide engineers building and validating bit-accurate and cycle-aware models of on-chip modules.

 - Review and drive integration of simulated chips with QEMU hosts, enabling kernel driver development and host software testing.

 - Define the architecture for multi-chip simulation to validate scale-out and scale-up approaches.

 - Establish code review, testing, and debugging practices to improve simulator accuracy and engineering velocity.

 - Partnering with hardware architects and software engineering leads to resolve complex pre-silicon issues and guide technical decisions.



You May Be a Good Fit If You Have

 - Deep expertise in C/C++ and low-level systems software development.

 - Experience leading complex technical projects and guiding other engineers through design, implementation, and code reviews.

 - Strong understanding of computer architecture, hardware-software interfaces, and systems programming.

 - Experience building or developing hardware simulators, architectural models, or other complex systems software.

 - Ability to make architectural decisions, evaluate technical tradeoffs, and maintain high engineering standards.

 - Strong debugging and problem-solving skills across hardware and software boundaries.

 - Experience mentoring engineers and collaborating across technical disciplines.

 - A track record of owning complex software systems from architecture through delivery.



Strong Candidates May Also Have Experience With

 - Developing hardware or system simulators using SystemC, gem5, QEMU, or custom simulation frameworks.

 - Cycle-accurate, cycle-aware, or bit-accurate hardware modeling.

 - Custom AI accelerators, GPUs, CPUs, or SoC architectures.

 - Firmware, kernel, and driver development, including Linux or FreeRTOS.

 - Hardware verification and validation methodologies.

 - Multithreaded and multiprocessing simulation frameworks.

 - Simulation performance profiling and optimization.

 - Python-based testing infrastructure, Bazel, and Git.

 - Leading small technical teams or owning simulation infrastructure in a semiconductor or accelerator startup.



Benefits

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
   
   - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

 - Housing subsidy of $2,500 per month for those living within walking distance of the office

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

 - Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification



How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.



We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

jobs.title: Principal AI Architect & Governance
jobs.description:
As Principal, AI Architect and Governance, you will serve as Vuori's senior technical authority for AI platform design, enterprise architecture standards, and responsible AI. You will define how AI systems are designed, built, integrated, and governed across the organization, ensuring they are secure, compliant, scalable, reliable, and aligned with business priorities.

This is a senior role for someone who combines deep, hands-on technical expertise with enterprise influence. You will work directly with engineers on architecture and design decisions, translate emerging AI capabilities into pragmatic enterprise patterns, and advise technology, business, security, legal, and data leaders on platform choices and risk. You will raise the quality and consistency of AI development through clear standards, reusable patterns, design reviews, and governance guardrails, without direct people-management responsibility.

What you'll get to do:

Set direction and raise the bar

• Shape the evolution of Vuori's enterprise AI architecture, ensuring it keeps pace with the growth of the business and the maturity of the AI ecosystem.
• Establish reference architectures, engineering standards, and integration patterns that teams across Vuori use when building AI systems.
• Lead technical evaluations of AI platforms, foundation models, cloud services, and tooling — recommending adoption decisions based on rigorous analysis of performance, cost, security, and fit.
• Raise the architectural capability of engineers across Vuori through design reviews, pairing, documentation, and reusable patterns others adopt because they are good.
• Bring clarity to complex, ambiguous problems — including calling out when a proposed AI approach is not the right solution.
• Make build-versus-buy-versus-partner recommendations that shape the AI platform for years and communicate the rationale clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

Build and maintain AI governance

• Develop and operationalize Vuori's AI governance framework, covering model risk management, data privacy, bias detection, audit trails, and regulatory compliance.
• Establish AI engineering standards, security guardrails, testing and evaluation protocols, and responsible AI policies that apply consistently across all teams building AI systems.
• Create governance structures that give teams a clear path to building and shipping AI responsibly — balancing speed of innovation with enterprise-grade risk management.
• Partner with Legal, Compliance, Security, and Data teams to ensure AI systems meet applicable regulations, data handling requirements, and ethical standards.
• Implement ongoing monitoring, incident response, and continuous improvement processes for AI systems in production.

Partner across the organization

• Work closely with senior technology and business leaders to align AI architecture and governance with organizational priorities and investment decisions.
• Serve as a clear, credible voice on AI architecture and risk in conversations with executive sponsors, engineering leadership, and external partners or auditors.
• Collaborate with AI product, engineering, and data teams to ensure architectural and governance requirements are understood and built in from the start — not added after the fact.
• Mentor engineers and technical leads through architectural guidance, design reviews, and the development of shared standards they can apply independently.

Measure and evolve

• Track and report on platform reliability, governance adherence, security posture, and the business impact of AI architecture investments.
• Continuously assess the AI landscape and incorporate emerging technologies, best practices, and industry standards to keep Vuori's AI ecosystem well-positioned.
• Use data and operational experience to refine standards, improve governance processes, and remove friction for teams building AI responsibly.

Who you are:

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field; advanced degree preferred.
• 12+ years of experience in software engineering, platform engineering, or technology architecture, including significant experience owning enterprise AI or data platform architecture at scale.
• Demonstrated experience designing and governing AI systems in production — including LLMs, agentic systems, ML pipelines, and model serving infrastructure.
• Deep expertise in enterprise AI governance, risk management, security, and compliance frameworks.
• Proven ability to define technical standards, make architecture decisions, and drive adoption across large, cross-functional engineering organizations through influence rather than direct authority.
• Experience with cloud-native architectures on Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud, and modern AI infrastructure patterns including RAG, vector databases, and orchestration frameworks.
• Experience building and deploying with frontier AI lab models, platforms, and/or frameworks (i.e. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, etc.).
• Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to explain complex AI architecture and governance requirements clearly to engineering, business, and executive audiences.
• Strong executive presence and a demonstrated ability to build alignment, challenge assumptions constructively, and influence decisions across a matrixed organization.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with enterprise AI governance platforms, model risk management frameworks, or AI regulatory standards such as the EU AI Act or NIST AI RMF.
• Familiarity with MLOps, model lifecycle management, AI observability, and responsible AI tooling.
• Experience with low-code and pro-code enterprise AI platforms such as Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Copilot Studio, or Google Gemini Enterprise.
• Background in retail, direct-to-consumer, e-commerce, or a similar consumer operating environment.
• Demonstrated ability to establish and scale practical architecture standards and governance capabilities in high-growth organizations.
• Active engagement with the broader AI and technology community through publications, speaking, or open-source contributions.

Our investment in you:

At Vuori, we’re proud to offer the following to our employees:

• Health Insurance
• Savings and Retirement Plan
• Employee Assistance Program
• Generous Vuori Discount & Industry Perks
• Paid Time Off
• Wellness & Fitness benefits

The salary range for this role is $197,500 per year - $264,390 per year. This role is bonus eligible.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We encourage you to help us break that statistic!

About Tailscale

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

We're looking for an Integrated ABM Campaign Manager to develop and scale creative, targeted campaigns that engage priority accounts and drive pipeline across our Enterprise and Mid-Market segments.

You'll own the strategy and execution of 1:1 and 1:few ABM campaigns, bringing together paid advertising, personalized content, direct mail, gifting, and coordinated Sales outreach to reach the right people at the right accounts.

This is a hands-on role where you'll have the freedom to test new ideas, build integrated programs, and use data to understand what's working. You'll also partner closely with our wider ABM, Sales, and Partner Marketing team to connect campaigns with account priorities, strategic experiences, and partner-led opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

• Own the strategy, planning, execution, and optimization of integrated ABM campaigns across Enterprise and Mid-Market audiences.

• Develop campaign audiences, messaging, channel plans, budgets, and success metrics based on Sales priorities and account insights.

• Manage targeted paid advertising, particularly LinkedIn, alongside personalized landing pages and other digital ABM experiences.

• Own direct mail, gifting, and scalable prospect engagement programs, including gifting program workflows.

• Partner with Sales and GTM Operations to identify target accounts, build contact lists, and activate campaigns.

• Develop coordinated Sales outreach plays and sequences with the Sales Enablement Lead to support campaign engagement and follow-up.

• Work with Product Marketing and Content to develop relevant messaging and creative for priority audiences.

• Collaborate with our wider Enterprise ABM, Events, and Partner Marketing teams on account-specific activations, event invitations, and joint campaigns.

• Proactively identify new campaign opportunities based on engagement signals, account intelligence, and business priorities.

• Track performance, test new approaches, and optimize for account engagement, meetings, pipeline creation, and progression.

What We Are Looking For

• 5+ years of B2B marketing experience, with a background in building ABM campaigns for both net-new acquisition and customer expansion.

• Experience independently developing and executing multi-channel campaigns from strategy through measurement.

• Hands-on experience with LinkedIn advertising, audience segmentation, and marketing automation.

• Hands-on experience with personalized landing page platforms like Userled or Mutiny.

• Experience with direct mail, gifting, personalization, or other creative account engagement tactics and platforms like Reachdesk or Sendoso.

• Strong understanding of how marketing campaigns support Sales engagement and pipeline generation.

• Comfortable working with data, testing new ideas, and using performance insights to improve results.

• Organized, creative, and comfortable managing multiple campaigns and stakeholders at once.

Nice to Have

• Experience marketing to technical or Enterprise B2B audiences.

• Familiarity with Salesforce, HubSpot, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Clay, or Common Room.

• Experience with partner or co-marketing campaigns.

As a company, we strive to maintain fair and equitable compensation practices within our team across all roles and all levels. Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set.

US Pay Range

$118,000—$148,000 USD

What We Offer

• An inclusive, flexible environment where you can be your authentic self. We recognize the impact of diverse voices and backgrounds on the growth of our people, product, and company. And that flexibility in how and when you work empowers our team to integrate work and life.

• A competitive total compensation package. This includes a base salary, an equity incentive plan and variable commission (for quota-based roles).

• Comprehensive group benefits with no waiting period. Take advantage of coverage for health, vision, dental, and more for you and your family!

Enjoy a change of scenery wherever you can get wifi, participate in virtual and in-person social events, and leverage our corporate co-working program to visit WeWork (or other similar spaces near you). jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Search
jobs.description:
What the Role Is

We’re hiring a Staff Software Engineer who’ll be the technical lead for a new Search team at Babylist. This new team will be focused on moving Babylist’s search capability in-house, making our search results more relevant and personalized, and partnering with other teams to transform search in the product from functional to delightful.

Registry building is the heart of the Babylist product. Every parent builds a list of dozens of products, from swaddle to stroller, with real stakes (a friend or family member is going to buy these things, and a baby is going to use them). As a universal registry, this registry also typically spans many retailers. This makes registry building on Babylist one of the most interesting search and personalization problems in consumer e-commerce.

This is zero-to-one work, with big ambitions. You’d build a search capability from the ground up, with a clear mandate from leadership to do it. In your first year, we expect to have rebuilt search to be highly relevant and personalized, and delivered big bets like universal search: one experience across items we sell and items from other retailers, and across products, guides and registries. We also want to work with Addie, our AI registry assistant, to have LLMs play a role in the search experience.

If you want to tune an established search system, this isn’t the right role. If you’ve worked inside a strong search team and want to build a new system from scratch at a company earlier in that journey, read on.

What You'll Own

A Staff Engineer at Babylist sets direction. You’ll be the technical lead for search: you decide where it goes over the next year or two, sequence the bets that get there, and make the technical and product calls along the way. You’re still in the code and will drive initiatives forward across multiple teams. You’ll have software engineering and machine learning engineering support on the team.

A few examples of initiatives you’d drive on the Search team:

• Build search in-house. Choose the architecture for indexing, retrieval and serving, and plan a seamless migration. The system you design replaces what we use today and is the foundation for everything below.

• Define what a good result is. Decide how we measure result quality, then improve it through query understanding, ranking and the behavioral signals we collect.

• Unify search across everything we show. One experience across items we sell and items from other retailers, and across products, guides and registries, including how to rank items we don’t sell next to ones we do.

• Decide how search and recommendations fit together. Bring what we know about a user and their registry into results, and decide how much retrieval and ranking search shares with our recommendation models.

• Make search conversational. Work with the Addie team, our AI registry assistant, on queries like “best stroller for urban family,” where the shopper describes a need instead of naming a product.

Like every Staff Engineer here, you will:

• Take a fuzzy business problem from the first sketch through to production, and stay on the hook for whether it actually helped customers.

• Build the platform or tooling other teams adopt by choice, and own it as it scales.

• Set the standard for how search builds with AI. Decide what good looks like, build the patterns and evals that get agents there and catch the output that's confidently wrong before it ships.

• Partner with product, design and data as a peer, shaping what's worth building from the start.

• Coach Senior engineers through the hard calls, the ambiguous ones as much as the technical ones

Who You Are

You meet the Staff bar at Babylist. You’ve shipped production systems for enough years to have earned strong opinions, and you hold them loosely. You can pick up an ambiguous problem and start moving before anyone hands you the full picture. You’ve already changed how a team builds with AI, and the new way stuck.

On top of that, you’ve worked on search problems before, ideally in an e-commerce setting. This role needs depth in the systems behind search and a clear focus on the people using it. You bring:

• Hands-on search experience: building and running search in production, including indexing, retrieval, ranking and query understanding. You know how to keep a search service fast, relevant and reliable as traffic and catalog size grow.

• Experience evaluating search quality: offline and online, including relevance judgments and A/B tests.

• A focus on the user: you use query data, behavior and judgment about result quality to decide what to build, and you can connect a search change to what shoppers do, and to conversion or revenue.

• Comfort building from zero: you can define the problem, design the system and own it end to end.

• You measure yourself by impact: a customer outcome, or a system a dozen teams come to depend on.

Compensation

We post real numbers. For a US-based Staff Engineer, the starting base salary range is $233,500 to $290,700, plus a target annual bonus of 20 percent of base. That's total target cash of roughly $280,200 to $348,840. On top of that you get meaningful equity and a 401(k) match. Where you start in that range depends on your experience, and your pay grows from there with performance and scope.

How We Build

AI is the default here. Engineers run agentic sessions for most of the work, and a lot of the interesting engineering now lives in the scaffolding that makes the agents good: the eval harnesses, the curated context, custom review skills and fast CI. Agents also triage incidents and handle a big share of support. A human always owns the outcome.

The architecture is intentionally simple: one Rails monolith, MySQL and few moving parts. That's deliberate. Simple infrastructure lets us move fast and lets AI reason about the whole system, so the hardest problems are the ones in front of customers.

The Stack

• Core app: Rails, Packwerk, React, TypeScript, Sidekiq

• Mobile: iOS (Swift), Android (Kotlin)

• Data, search & events: MySQL, Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, Weaviate, WarpStream, Hex, Sigma

• Machine learning: deep learning, matrix factorization, retrieval & ranking, AWS SageMaker, MLflow

• AI & dev tooling: Claude Code, Devin, Linear, CodeRabbit, Warden, LangChain, Bedrock AgentCore, Maxim

• Infra & ops: AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Datadog, incident.io, LaunchDarkly

• Key integrations: Shopify (payments), Iterable (CRM)

Why Babylist

An engineer, expecting her first baby, couldn't find the registry she wanted. So she built it. That's how Babylist started, and it's still how we work: engineers solving problems for families. Becoming a parent is one of the biggest moments in a person's life. Millions reach it for the first time every year, making thousands of decisions and figuring it out as they go. That's who we build for, and we're a long way from done.

Ten million people give gifts through Babylist every year. We did more than $750M in revenue in 2025, up 45 percent over the year before, and we've been profitable for eight years while staying independent. So you can take on a hard, multi-year problem without watching over your shoulder for the next round or the next correction. And the team is small, around 65 engineers, so what you ship stays visible and your scope stays wide.

How We Work

Remote-first across the US and Canada, and we have been for years. That's not changing. We trust you to own your time and your outcomes, and we get everyone in a room together twice a year. Teams are small, pods of three to five engineers, so nothing you ship disappears into a committee. You'll work shoulder to shoulder with product, design and data, and with the partners across the business who rely on what you ship. You'll also stay close to customers yourself: sitting in on user interviews, watching session recordings, riding along with support. Here that's part of the engineering job, on a regular basis.

How We Hire

Three rounds, usually two to three weeks start to finish.

• Recruiter conversation (30 minutes). Trade context: what you want next, what we're building and straight answers on comp, team and remote.

• Technical screen (1 hour). One round, no AI, language-agnostic. Reach for Google when you normally would. We just want to see how you reason from first principles.

• Final round (4 hours). Four one-hour interviews: system design, AI-assisted coding with the tools you'd actually use here, product sense and culture and values. You'll hear back either way within 24 to 48 hours.

Benefits

• Company-paid medical and fully covered dental and vision

• A 401(k) match

• Generous paid parental leave for birthing and non-birthing parents, plus a gradual return-to-work program

• Winter Wonder Week, a paid company-wide week off at the end of the year

• A remote-work stipend

• Mental-health and wellness support

A Few Things to Know

• We record and transcribe interviews to evaluate candidates, in line with applicable privacy laws.

• We expect you to use AI in your work and we welcome it in the process, but what you submit and say should reflect your own thinking.

• If you have a family member or close relationship with a Babylist employee, let your recruiter know.

• Official outreach only ever comes from an @babylist.com address

jobs.title: Trust Technical Investigator
jobs.description:
At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

This position will be hybrid in LinkedIn’s Mountain View campus.

About the Role

Trust Investigations is seeking a Trust Technical Investigator to support our work managing fraud and scams. In this role, you'll develop and apply approaches to detect, understand, and mitigate coordinated, persistent, and high-harm activity from highly adversarial actors, helping ensure a safe and trustworthy experience for LinkedIn members.

Our teams work in close partnership with product, engineering, and data science partners dedicated to advancing our visibility, controls and measurement. In this role, you will run investigations and contribute to building our technology as we operate an AI-first trust environment: you'll lead complex investigation and incidents, using case insights to develop and maintain our detection rules, pipelines, and runbooks that help LinkedIn stop scam activity at scale. Our investigations drive product vulnerability assessments and risk recommendations, so you’ll work with our intelligence and product-risk teams to ensure findings inform how the company builds and protects its products going forward.

Key Responsibilities:

Investigation & Incident Leadership

• Lead root-cause investigations into complex, coordinated, or high-impact scam campaigns and abuse networks, from initial leads through resolution.
• Serve as incident commander for major scam-related incidents, coordinating response and ensuring timely, accurate resolution.
• Generate proactive investigative leads and track emerging coordinated threat activity relevant to scams and fraud.

Detection Engineering & Technical Tradecraft

• Author detection rules and data pipelines tuned specifically to scam patterns and typologies.
• Innovate on investigative tradecraft, staying current on tools, techniques, and adversary tactics used across the fraud and scams landscape broadly.
• Partner with Engineering and Data Science to build and refine how we do analysis, threat-hunting and mitigations for scams.
• Develop technical playbooks that help the broader team scale its investigative work.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Vulnerability Reporting

• Partner with intelligence and product-risk teams to ensure investigative findings and intel inform product planning and risk posture.
• Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Legal, and Policy partners to align investigative priorities with product roadmaps and the broader trust and safety strategy.
• Represent the technical substance of your team's work in cross-functional forums and externally to peers in the sector.

Quality & Mentorship

• Mentor other investigators on technical, investigative, and tooling capabilities, fostering a culture of rigor and continuous learning.

Basic Qualifications:

• Bachelor's Degree in Cyber Security, Criminal Justice, or other related technical disciplines, or equivalent technical experience
• 3+ years of experience with scripting or data analysis tools (SQL, Python, or similar), with the ability to synthesize complex data into actionable insights.
• 3+ years of experience in proactive threat investigations of account, content, or behavioral abuse in trust & safety, social media, online platforms, or fintech — including meaningful direct experience with fraud or scams.
• 3+ years of experience with investigation techniques/tools and evidence handling, including working across diverse structured and unstructured data sets.

Preferred Qualifications:

• BS and 5+ years of relevant work experience, MS and 4+ years of relevant work experience, or PhD and 2+ years of relevant work experience.
• Direct experience building or maintaining detection rules, alerting logic, or data pipelines (not just consuming them).
• Strong technical acumen and the ability to translate data and investigative outcomes into actionable insights for engineering, AI, and senior leadership partners.
• Experience leading proactive threat or fraud hunting against large-scale, coordinated abuse.
• Experience with frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK or the cyber kill chain, and the ability to adapt them to social-platform scam typologies.
• Demonstrated ability to navigate cross-functional dependencies and drive collaboration across engineering, product, data science, and legal teams.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence across all levels of an organization.
• Experience mentoring or developing other investigators.
• Experience working in global teams spanning multiple locations and time zones.

Suggest Skills:

• Trust & Safety Investigations
• Detection Engineering
• Investigating coordinated & complex fraud/scams investigations
• Threat Intelligence
• Platform Abuse Prevention

You will Benefit from our Culture

We strongly believe in the well-being of our employees and their families. That is why we offer generous health and wellness programs and time away for employees of all levels. LinkedIn is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices.

The pay range for this role is $109,000 to $180,000. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor.

The total compensation package for this position may also include annual performance bonus, stock, benefits and/or other applicable incentive compensation plans. For more information, visit https://careers.linkedin.com/benefits.

• Free Weekends

• Protected Time-Off

• No Calls

• Full malpractice insurance

• Equipment

• 2 Fully covered weekend educational retreats per year with 16 hours of CME each

• Work in Your Community

• Yearly and quarterly bonus potential based on performance

• Independent Contractor, Fee for Service Pay Model

THE POSITION

We're able to offer you all of these amazing benefits by transitioning you from hospitals and clinics over to home health and long-term care facilities. Our practice specializes in consistently delivering exceptional wound care and unparalleled bedside procedures to patients in these settings.

We are on the frontier of wound care science and innovation. This is your opportunity to learn from the best in the field, be trained in advanced bedside procedures & wound care, to be at the cutting edge of this science, and to bring advanced procedures to patients' bedsides.

LOCATION

Our home office is located in Los Angeles, California, but the beauty of this job is you can work from anywhere. We have relationships with facilities all across the nation and are adding new locations every day.

REQUIREMENTS

Currently we are looking for a minimum of two full weekdays; however, you should know full-time Monday through Friday physicians will receive priority consideration due to the magnitude of elderly care that's needed.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

Be warned, we aren't a good fit for everyone. Please do not reply if the only reason you went to school was to get "Dr" or "M.D." next to your name or so you could have a large group of subordinates to bark orders to, you will not fit in here. If other physicians or nurses describe your procedure technique as "working on meat" vs. having the intent to relieve human suffering, then this isn't the place for you.

But, if you're looking for the right specialty, if you're truly passionate about performing surgical procedures, or if you feel stalled out in your current position, then reach out to us. Maybe you're looking for a new challenge, and a chance to feel like your work really matters. If so, apply to join our team now.

The American Journal of Medicine says that the average doctor works 60 HOURS A WEEK inside of a hospital. We want to offer physicians a better alternative. We want to give you more freedom and more control. If this is something that excites you, then contact us today so we can begin crafting the perfect career for you!

WHATS NEXT

After you contact us, one of our Talent Acquisition teammates will contact you to discuss the position in its entirety. Our practice team of physicians will help train you in everything you need to know over the first few months of working with us. After that time we have CME approved activities to further train you in wound, skin and ostomy care.

Help us achieve our mission of touching and improving as many lives as possible! Apply now.

Earn $50-$150 per patient visit with no nights, no calls, no weekends, and no Holidays

SKILLED WOUND CARE | Life beyond Work, Work beyond Measure!

jobs.title: Senior Compliance Associate, Personal Account Dealing
jobs.description:
Who are we?

FalconX is a pioneering team of operators, investors, and builders committed to revolutionizing institutional access to the crypto markets. Operating at the intersection of traditional finance and  cutting-edge technology, FalconX addresses the industry's foremost challenges: Navigating the digital asset market can be complex and fragmented, with limited products and services that support trading strategies, structures, and liquidity found in conventional financial markets. As a comprehensive solution for all digital asset strategies from start to scale, FalconX operates as the connective tissue empowering clients with seamless navigation through the ever- evolving cryptocurrency landscape.

Position Summary

FalconX is seeking a Personal Account Dealing Senior Compliance Associate to join our team and help to manage the program governing employee trading and conflicts of interest across the firm. In this role, you will review and adjudicate personal trading pre-clearance requests, monitor employee holdings and transactions for policy breaches, and administer the systems that make this program run. You will work at the intersection of compliance, data, and market structure — operating vendor-based employee compliance tooling alongside FalconX's internal systems to identify conflicts, detect undisclosed activity, and ensure the firm meets its code of ethics and market abuse obligations across the jurisdictions in which we operate.

Because FalconX operates in digital assets, this role extends the traditional personal account dealing discipline into self-custody wallets, on-chain activity, and token holdings. This role requires equal parts investigative rigor, technical comfort, and absolute discretion, and offers a unique opportunity to shape personal trading practice at one of the leading institutional digital asset platforms.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Pre-Clearance Adjudication: Independently review, approve, deny, or escalate employee pre-clearance requests for personal securities and digital asset transactions, applying restricted list rules, blackout periods, holding period requirements, and conflict checks within committed turnaround times.

• Breach Identification & Escalation: Investigate suspected breaches of the personal account dealing policy — trading in restricted names, front-running firm or client activity, breach of minimum holding periods, use of undisclosed accounts — and prepare clear investigative narratives with supporting evidence for escalation to the Compliance Manager.

• Restricted & Watch List Maintenance: Assist with maintaining the firm's restricted and watch lists, ensuring names and tokens are added and released on the correct triggers, and that list changes propagate correctly into the pre-clearance rule set.

• MNPI Coordination: Work with Legal, Corporate Development, and business heads to ensure that material non-public information — deal activity, upcoming listings, client mandates — is reflected in trading restrictions on a timely basis.

• Gifts & Entertainment / Outside Business Activities: Review and disposition gifts and entertainment and OBA submissions against firm thresholds, identify aggregation and pattern concerns, and escalate submissions raising bribery, inducement, or client-conflict risk.

Regulatory Compliance & Audit Support

• Regulatory Alignment: Maintain a deep, up-to-date understanding of the personal trading and conflicts requirements applicable to the firm's regulated entities and their equivalents across jurisdictions, together with digital-asset-specific guidance, ensuring the program's coverage remains fully compliant as the regulatory perimeter shifts.

• Policy Contribution: Partner with the Compliance Manager to update the personal account dealing policy, code of ethics, review playbooks, and standard operating procedures as regulations, product lines, and market structures evolve — with particular focus on where existing policy language does not cleanly address digital asset activity.

• Audit Readiness: Assemble pre-clearance records, breach files, attestation completion evidence, and decision rationale for internal audit, bank partner reviews, and regulatory examinations, ensuring each file stands on its own without verbal explanation.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Law, Data Science, or a related field.

Experience: 1–3 years of direct experience in personal account dealing, code of ethics, or employee compliance monitoring at a broker-dealer, asset manager, bank, proprietary trading firm, fintech, or digital asset platform. Experience running or administering a personal trading program — not solely submitting into one — is strongly preferred.

Platform Experience: Hands-on experience with STAR Compliance is strongly preferred, including administrator-level familiarity with pre-clearance rule configuration, broker and custodian data feeds, attestation campaigns, and reporting. Experience with comparable employee compliance platforms (ComplySci, MyComplianceOffice, Schwab Compliance Technologies) will be considered, provided the candidate has configured and maintained the system rather than only used its front end.

Analytical Mindset: Exceptional attention to detail, with the ability to reconstruct what an employee actually traded from incomplete records, spot the account that was never disclosed, and distinguish a genuine oversight from a deliberate circumvention.

Discretion & Judgment: Proven ability to handle sensitive personal information about colleagues with complete confidentiality, and the composure to make and defend unpopular decisions — including denying a request from a senior stakeholder — without escalating unnecessarily or capitulating inappropriately.

Communication: Crisp verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to document decisions clearly, explain a denial in terms an employee understands, and articulate personal trading expectations to non-compliance stakeholders across the firm.

Digital Asset Interest: Genuine interest in digital asset markets and the practical mechanics of self-custody, on-chain activity, staking, and airdrops — enough to reason about how a policy written for equities should apply to a wallet.

The base pay for this role is expected to be between $132,000 - $167,000 in the New York City Area. This expected base pay range is based on information at the time this post was generated. This role will also be eligible for other forms of compensation such as a performance linked bonus, equity, and a competitive benefits package. Actual compensation for a successful candidate will be determined based on a number of factors such as location, skillset, experience, qualifications and the level at which the candidate is hired.

Notice at Collection and Privacy Policy

Applicants located in California and/or applying to a role based in California, please refer to our Notice at Collection and Privacy Policy here.

Inclusivity Statement

jobs.title: Parts Lead Supervisor
jobs.description:
Pay Rate:  $23.00/hr to $30.00/hr

About Carvana
At Carvana, we sell cars but we aren’t car salesmen. Our promise is simple: we won’t sell a car to a customer that we wouldn’t sell to our own Mom. Period. To make sure our cars are in first-rate condition, we’ve built multiple vehicle Reconditioning Centers around the country, where our cars are inspected, perfected, and photographed before reaching the Carvana website. Using our Carvana Certified 150-point inspection process, we’re able to verify that every vehicle meets our rigorous mechanical and cosmetic standards.

We strive to provide only the highest quality vehicles to our customers in our mission to deliver a no-hassle, better car buying experience. We are actively looking for passionate and talented individuals who can help us deliver on that promise.

Think you’ve got what it takes to join our team? Keep reading below to see what we’re looking for!

Position Overview:
Parts Line Lead Supervisor (Automotive)  a front-line supervisor role, responsible for directly managing and developing a team of hourly associates in an Inspection Center to regularly achieve production targets.

What you’ll be doing:

• Manage the movement of cars into and out of the Inspection Center safely for repairs, while meeting or exceeding set production and quality goals.

• Meet or exceed inventory production goals on a daily, weekly and monthly basis.

• Oversee day-to-day activities of assigned team; identify team’s strengths and weaknesses; determine areas of opportunity and the appropriate steps to improve.

• Engage assigned team, provide appropriate coaching, development and performance management; offer feedback and demonstrate desired skills.

• Create a work and team environment that inspires positive communication, team cohesion, and adherence to Carvana’s Values.

• Proactively communicate information to team members, providing clear understanding of expectations, performance measures, and goals.

• Prevent and resolve conflict among team members.

• Monitor and ensure adherence to systems, policies, procedures, and performance standards.

• Review and approve identified mechanical and physical defects of incoming inventory.

• Lead a team of production associates and partner with the Inspection Center General Manager to repair or reject inventory based on estimated cost of repairs and/or the overall quality of the vehicle.

• Train a team of production associates using Quality Control standards to identify and complete repairs effectively and efficiently the first time, minimizing re-checks and delays in production.

• Identify and complete repairs effectively and efficiently the first time, to minimize re-work and delays in production.

• Conscientiously work in ways that decrease the possibility of injury to yourself or other team members in the shop due to spills or other preventable hazardous conditions.

• Effectively manage multiple associates, including ensuring appropriate employee development and performance management.

What the job requires:

• High School Diploma or GED equivalent

• Experience using computers

• Must be at least 18 years of age

• Demonstrated functional expertise in one or more areas pertaining to Carvana’s reconditioning process

• Demonstrated understanding of our current reconditioning processes and lean principles

• Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no DUIs and no more than two moving violations in the last 3 years).

• Must be able to lift up to 60 pounds independently; majority of lifting from knee to shoulder heights; other lifting required from various levels

• Requires standing for extended periods of time with frequent stretching, reaching, walking, stooping, pushing, and/or pulling in an environment that may be cold, hot, noisy, and wet and may have fumes or odors due to vehicle maintenance.

• Requires use of safety equipment that may include but not limited to face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment.

• Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to effectively delegate tasks to team members.

• Ability to communicate and interact with others effectively in a professional, courteous manner.

• Ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both written and oral.

• Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to multitask and prioritize effectively.

• Ability to resolve complex issues with guidance from others.

• Ability to work overtime and on weekends.

• Ability to work variable schedule(s) as necessary.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

What we’ll offer in return

• Full-Time Position with a competitive salary

• Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits

• 401K with company match

• A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more

• A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy, both physically and mentally

• Access to opportunities to expand your skillset and share your knowledge with others across the organization

• A company culture of promotions from within, with a start-up atmosphere allowing for varied and rapid career development

• A seat in one of the fastest-growing companies in the country

jobs.title: Clinical Research Nurse Coordinator
jobs.description:
M3 Wake Research is looking for a Clinical Research Nurse Coordinator (CNC) to support our mission by performing trial-related procedures as directed by the Principal Investigator, including accurate dispensing and dosing of investigational product. While the Principal Investigator is responsible for the overall conduct of the trial, you’ll manage, support, and coordinate the daily work that keeps the study on track, and you’ll play a critical role in how it runs. You’ll work closely with the Investigator team, sponsors, and site staff to make sure every part of the study is compliant.

What you’ll do:

• Follow assigned protocols, including study procedures, timelines, and inclusion/exclusion criteria
• Perform infusions as dictated by the clinical trial protocol
• Handle, prepare, administer, and track investigational product, including inventory and accountability
• Lead patient consultations and education in an outpatient setting under the direction of the PI
• Take part in the informed consent process and make sure amended consents are properly implemented
• Perform delegated study procedures such as vitals, EKGs, phlebotomy, pulmonary function testing, and sample processing, and document them accurately in source
• Review medical and concomitant medication history and help complete case report forms
• Keep regulatory binders, source documents, and the Delegation of Authority Log organized and audit-ready
• Partner with the recruitment team to meet enrollment goals

• Currently licensed as a RN or LPN in the state of NC
• Current ACLS provider card
• At least 1 to 2 years of experience performing infusions
• Ideally, 1 to 2 years of clinical research related experience
• Working knowledge of IP handling, sterile compounding, infusion administration, medication administration, and source documentation in a research setting
• Solid understanding of FDA regulations, ICH-GCP, and ISO standards
• Comfortable with clinical and sponsor systems and strong computer skills

jobs.title: Group Product Manager, Revenue Platform
jobs.description:
This is Adyen

Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.

For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster.

Group Product Manager, Revenue Platform

The Opportunity

Adyen is a full-stack payment processor and licensed global bank, serving many of the world’s largest enterprises across more than 250 payment methods and dozens of markets. One of the reasons they choose us is how we charge them. Our Interchange++ model shows interchange, scheme fees and Adyen’s own markup as separate, visible components, with no hidden fees. On top of that transparency, we offer pricing that flexes to how global businesses actually operate: by market, card type, channel, payment method or ticket size, all on one platform and one invoice.

That promise is only as good as the systems behind it. Revenue Platform is the backbone of it. We build the platform that turns every payment and every product into a correct, explainable, compliant invoice, and that gives our commercial teams the freedom to price creatively without engineering work. It also gives Finance and our customers a true view of cost and margin.

We are looking for a Group Product Manager in Chicago to lead Revenue Platform’s product managers and own the group’s strategy and results. We need a platform leader: someone who knows that the best internal platforms are measured by how much they let other teams do without them. You will set the direction for how Adyen monetizes for the next decade, on a modern event-based foundation we have already built.

What You’ll Do

• Own a Core Differentiator: Set the vision for how Adyen delivers transparent, flexible pricing to the world’s largest businesses. Decide what the platform builds, what it retires and what it deliberately leaves out, and tie every bet to customer trust, commercial growth or revenue accuracy.

• Build a Platform Others Build On: Shape revenue capabilities into reusable, well-designed services that product teams can use as they are, without workarounds. Measure success by how fast teams across Adyen can launch, price and monetize new products on their own.

• Unlock Pricing Freedom: Give commercial teams the models, data and tools to structure any deal, from transaction-value pricing to custom enterprise contracts, without bespoke engineering.

• Make Cost and Margin Visible: Extend the platform from revenue to cost, so Adyen and its customers can see what every payment truly costs and earns.

• Treat Compliance as Product: Partner with Tax, Legal and Finance to turn tax and invoicing obligations across markets into automated, auditable capabilities, with a pragmatic view of what each one requires.

• Lead & Develop Senior Talent: Hire, coach and grow a team of product managers who own their domains end to end.

• Make the Hard Calls: Align Engineering, Finance, Commercial and the many product teams that depend on the platform, without direct authority. Hold the line on platform design even when that means saying “no.”

Who You Are

• Platform Leader: You have led internal or B2B platform products with many consuming teams, and you know how to design interfaces, contracts and incentives that drive adoption.

• Product Leader: You have 8+ years in product management, including hands-on experience hiring and developing product managers.

• Technically Deep: You are comfortable going deep with engineers on event-driven, high-volume, data-intensive systems where correctness is non-negotiable.

• Financially Fluent: You understand how pricing, cost, margin and tax flow into invoicing and financial reporting, and you can earn the trust of a finance organization.

• Grounded in the Space: You have experience with billing, pricing, revenue or payments infrastructure. Experience in fintech or regulated industries is a strong plus.

• Influential Communicator: You are clear and confident with technical, commercial, finance and executive audiences worldwide.

Total rewards & compensation

The annual base salary range for this role is $235,000 - $317,000 USD. Compensation is based on factors including qualifications, experience, and location. Total compensation package includes equity (RSUs), 401(k), health, dental, vision, and more.

In-office expectations

This role is based in our San Francisco office. We're an office-first company and expect employees to work in-office at least 3 days a week on average. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while also supporting flexibility.

This role is based out of our Chicago office.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Adyen

We actively seek different perspectives to sharpen our ideas. Our unique culture is a product of our diverse backgrounds and experiences. No matter who you are or where you’re from, you’re welcome to be your true self at Adyen.

If you need accommodations or support during the recruitment process to perform at your best, you’ll have the opportunity to let our team know in your application. We encourage people from all backgrounds and abilities to apply.

What’s next?

Ensuring a smooth and enjoyable candidate experience is critical for us. We aim to get back to you regarding your application within 5 business days. Our interview process tends to take about 4 weeks to complete, but may fluctuate depending on the role. Learn more about our hiring process here. Don’t be afraid to let us know if you need more flexibility.

jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

jobs.title: Loads and Dynamics Engineer, Satellites (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

LOADS AND DYNAMICS ENGINEER, SATELLITES (STARLINK)

At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

Dynamics is responsible for low and high-frequency loads, vibration, and forcing functions for Starlink satellites during ground transportation, ascent (launch), and on-orbit operation. Responsibilities also include database design and software programming for tool development. This role will also be responsible for test planning, setup, execution, and data processing. Dynamics engineers are expected to have a strong intuition of the frequency domain in addition to having solid software and analytical skills.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Resolve dynamics problems through analysis and test

• Execute dynamic testing from start to finish including pre-test analysis, sensor selection & installation, testing, data analysis, signal processing and model correlation

• Build finite element models

• Perform analyses using commercial and in-house codes as well as write new code

• Perform other analyses that improve products including, but not limited to, satellite brightness, stress analyses, and fatigue analysis

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in physics, mathematics, or an engineering discipline

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 1+ years of professional experience with dynamics

• Hands-on experience either analyzing data or building hardware

• Experience with vibration and shock testing

• Experience with NASTRAN

• Finite element modeling experience (use of FEMAP)

• Working knowledge of structural analysis and test, including a fundamental understanding of strength, stability and fatigue failure mechanisms

• Excellent oral and written communication skills

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Ability to work long hours and weekends as necessary to support critical milestones

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:

Level 1: $100,000.00 - $135,000.00
Level 2: $115,000.00 - $165,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. Company shuttles are offered to employees for roundtrip travel from select Seattle locations to the SpaceX Redmond office Monday to Friday.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

jobs.description:
About FirstSteps

The FirstSteps Team is inspired by the belief that every child deserves the opportunity to achieve their fullest potential. To that end, our mission is twofold: to provide the best evidence-based, behavior analytic treatment to our children diagnosed with autism and related learning differences, and to offer a positive, collaborative, and dynamic work experience for our team. We are steadfastly committed to ongoing training and mentorship of our employees, always motivated to support the next generation of clinical leaders in our field and at FirstSteps. Our greatest reward is witnessing the rapid and joyful learning of our little ones and knowing that together, we are creating more happy days for the kids and families we serve.

The Behavior Technician Position (referred to as "Instructors" at FirstSteps)

There is nothing more rewarding than knowing you are making a difference in the life of a child. As a FirstSteps Behavior Technician:

You will have the great privilege of teaching our little ones diagnosed with autism meaningful skills including communication, socialization, self-care, and school readiness

• Experience first-hand a child’s first words, first friend, first shoe tie, and much more

• You will work closely with and learn from teachers, parents, FirstSteps BCBAs, and behavioral health/ mental health specialists

• You will become a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) with all initial credentialing fees paid by FirstSteps in conjunction with our paid training program

*Want to hear straight from our RBTs about the job and their experiences? Check out our reel series ChatRBT and Day in the Life on IG @firststepsforkids

FirstSteps on Diversity & Equity:

We believe that we have a responsibility and an opportunity to contribute to a kinder and more compassionate world by living our values of diversity and equity in all our daily operations. As an equal opportunity employer, we value diversity, equity, and inclusivity in our service delivery with our clients, in collaboration with families and communities, and in our organizational culture and practices with our wonderful Behavior Technicians and support staff.

Behavior Technician Wage Info

Our new team members earn a starting clinical wage of $23 - $25 per hour depending on experience. Our Instructors are also eligible to earn multiple wage increases throughout the year.

Behavior Technicians at FirstSteps access benefits including:

• Exceptional training, on-going support, & career development opportunities

• Health Insurance with generous employer contribution

• Access to discounted dental and vision insurance

• 401(k) Retirement Plan with generous company match

• Paid time-off (PTO) & anniversary PTO awards

• Compensation for drive time, mileage, and data usage

• Tuition discounts with our partner universities offering Bachelor's, Master's, and doctorate degree programs

• Employment Assistance Program

• Employee referral bonus program

• Ongoing team building and community events during and outside of work hours

• Fun, team approach and work atmosphere

To APPLY for the Behavior Technician position, we ask that you:

Share our Values & Mission:

• Show up with enthusiasm and dedication, knowing that your work is creating more life-long opportunities for our kids diagnosed with autism

• Believe that our children (and all children) are wonderfully unique and capable of communicating what is important to them and achieving their goals

Have some "Kid" Experience:

• We look for "kid people" and related work, study, or volunteer experience demonstrating an interest in child development and commitment to the care and well-being of all children

Completed Education:
